1	"""Multi-turn Endless Terminals rollout for slime.
2	
3	Wired in via:
4	    --custom-generate-function-path et.rollout.generate
5	    --custom-rm-path                et.rollout.reward_func
6	
7	One sample == one terminal episode. Each turn the policy emits exactly one
8	`<command>...</command>` (or `<action>done</action>`); the command runs in the
9	episode's private shell and the harness-formatted result is appended to the
10	context as a non-trainable user turn. The episode reward is the task's own
11	pytest verifier: 1.0 or 0.0, awarded once at the end of the episode.
12	
13	The system prompt below is copied verbatim from the Endless Terminals reference
14	transcripts (`solution/o3_summary.json`), as is the observation wording, so the
15	policy sees the same interface the dataset was built against.
16	"""
17	
18	from __future__ import annotations
19	
20	import asyncio
21	import logging
22	import os
23	import re
24	
25	from slime.rollout.sglang_rollout import GenerateState
26	from slime.utils.http_utils import post
27	from slime.utils.types import Sample
28	
29	from et.sandbox import Episode, check_exec_capable
30	
31	SYSTEM_PROMPT = """You are a highly capable Linux terminal agent operating strictly via a single-shell-command interface.
32	Goal: complete the user's task.
33	
34	Rules:
35	- Output exactly one of the following per turn:
36	  1) <command>THE_SINGLE_SHELL_COMMAND</command>
37	  OR
38	  2) <action>done</action>
39	- Don't use interactive commands and confirmations; use non-interactive flags.
40	- Prefer simple, robust CLI tools; write files explicitly when needed.
41	- If you believe the task is solved, emit <action>done</action>.
42	- Hint: you might want to run commands interactively to see the output and then write the command. Don't just pipe the commands.
43	- Only your first command in command tags will be executed. So don't respond with multiple commands.
44	- Hint: Verify your solution once you are done. Eg: you can use cat to see the input and the output.
45	- Do not just write long bash scripts. Write the commands that you would write in a terminal."""
46	
47	DATA_ROOT = os.environ.get("ET_DATA_ROOT", "/tmp/et_prompts")
48	# Must allow execution, so not under /dev/shm -- see et.sandbox.check_exec_capable.
49	SCRATCH_ROOT = os.environ.get("ET_SCRATCH", "/tmp/et_episodes")
50	MAX_TURNS = int(os.environ.get("ET_MAX_TURNS", "8"))
51	MAX_NEW_TOKENS_PER_TURN = int(os.environ.get("ET_MAX_NEW_TOKENS", "512"))
52	CMD_TIMEOUT = float(os.environ.get("ET_CMD_TIMEOUT", "20"))
53	MAX_OBS_CHARS = int(os.environ.get("ET_MAX_OBS_CHARS", "1500"))
54	# Hard ceiling on one episode, covering everything: generation, the shell, the
55	# verifier and teardown. Every individual step is already bounded, yet the run
56	# still hung -- slime builds its HTTP client with `httpx.Timeout(None)`, so a
57	# `/generate` that never comes back waits forever, and asyncio's
58	# `Process.wait()` has its own way of never resolving (see sandbox.REAP_TIMEOUT).
59	# Both drivers await every episode before returning, so one episode that never
60	# finishes stalls the entire rollout rather than failing it. The default is
61	# deliberately far above any legitimate episode -- 6 turns of generation plus
62	# 6x20s of commands plus a 180s verifier -- so this only ever fires on a hang.
63	EPISODE_TIMEOUT = float(os.environ.get("ET_EPISODE_TIMEOUT", "900"))
64	
65	STOP_STRINGS = ["</command>", "</action>"]
66	_OBS_SENTINEL = "@@ET_OBSERVATION@@"
67	
68	_COMMAND_RE = re.compile(r"<command>(.*?)(?:</command>|\Z)", re.DOTALL)
69	_ACTION_RE = re.compile(r"<action>\s*done\s*</action>", re.IGNORECASE)
70	
71	
72	class _Chat:
73	    """Derives the chat-template glue once, without hardcoding ChatML.
74	
75	    `head` is the token prefix the policy generates from. `tail` is the text
76	    that must follow a generated assistant turn in order to inject one user
77	    turn and re-open the assistant turn.
78	    """
79	
80	    def __init__(self, tokenizer) -> None:
81	        kwargs = {"tokenize": False, "add_generation_prompt": True, "enable_thinking": False}
82	        probe_msgs = [{"role": "system", "content": "S"}, {"role": "user", "content": "U"}]
83	        head = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(probe_msgs, **kwargs)
84	        full = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
85	            probe_msgs
86	            + [{"role": "assistant", "content": "A"}, {"role": "user", "content": _OBS_SENTINEL}],
87	            **kwargs,
88	        )
89	        prefix = os.path.commonprefix([head, full])
90	        assert full[len(prefix) : len(prefix) + 1] == "A", "unexpected chat template shape"
91	        self._tail = full[len(prefix) + 1 :]
92	        assert _OBS_SENTINEL in self._tail, "could not locate the observation slot in the chat template"
93	        self._kwargs = kwargs
94	
95	    def prompt(self, tokenizer, instruction: str) -> str:
96	        return tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
97	            [{"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM_PROMPT}, {"role": "user", "content": instruction}],
98	            **self._kwargs,
99	        )
100	
101	    def observation(self, text: str) -> str:
102	        return self._tail.replace(_OBS_SENTINEL, text)
103	
104	
105	_CHAT: _Chat | None = None
106	_SCRATCH_CHECKED = False
107	
108	
109	def _chat(tokenizer) -> _Chat:
110	    global _CHAT
111	    if _CHAT is None:
112	        _CHAT = _Chat(tokenizer)
113	    return _CHAT
114	
115	
116	def _check_scratch_once() -> None:
117	    global _SCRATCH_CHECKED
118	    if not _SCRATCH_CHECKED:
119	        check_exec_capable(SCRATCH_ROOT)
120	        _SCRATCH_CHECKED = True
121	
122	
123	def parse_action(text: str) -> tuple[str, str | None]:
124	    """Return ("command", cmd) / ("done", None) / ("invalid", None).
125	
126	    Mirrors the harness rule "only your first command in command tags will be
127	    executed": whichever of `<command>` / `<action>` appears first wins.
128	    """
129	    cmd_match = _COMMAND_RE.search(text)
130	    act_match = _ACTION_RE.search(text)
131	    if act_match and (cmd_match is None or act_match.start() < cmd_match.start()):
132	        return "done", None
133	    if cmd_match:
134	        cmd = cmd_match.group(1).strip()
135	        return ("command", cmd) if cmd else ("invalid", None)
136	    return "invalid", None
137	
138	
139	def _abort(args, sample: Sample, turns: int, **extra) -> Sample:
140	    """Finish a sample that is giving up, with every field slime will index.
141	
142	    `_convert_samples_to_train_data` repeatedly decides whether an optional
143	    per-sample field is present by looking at `samples[0]` alone, and then
144	    indexes *every* sample in the batch. An episode that gives up while its
145	    neighbours complete normally is therefore not a local failure -- it takes
146	    down the whole rollout, from a traceback that names slime rather than this
147	    file. Three such fields exist on this path:
148

from slime.utils.http_utils import post
from slime.utils.types import Sample

from et.sandbox import Episode, check_exec_capable

SYSTEM_PROMPT = """You are a highly capable Linux terminal agent operating strictly via a single-shell-command interface.
Goal: complete the user's task.

Rules:
- Output exactly one of the following per turn:
  1) <command>THE_SINGLE_SHELL_COMMAND</command>
  OR
  2) <action>done</action>
- Don't use interactive commands and confirmations; use non-interactive flags.
- Prefer simple, robust CLI tools; write files explicitly when needed.
- If you believe the task is solved, emit <action>done</action>.
- Hint: you might want to run commands interactively to see the output and then write the command. Don't just pipe the commands.
- Only your first command in command tags will be executed. So don't respond with multiple commands.
- Hint: Verify your solution once you are done. Eg: you can use cat to see the input and the output.
- Do not just write long bash scripts. Write the commands that you would write in a terminal."""

DATA_ROOT = os.environ.get("ET_DATA_ROOT", "/tmp/et_prompts")
# Must allow execution, so not under /dev/shm -- see et.sandbox.check_exec_capable.
SCRATCH_ROOT = os.environ.get("ET_SCRATCH", "/tmp/et_episodes")
MAX_TURNS = int(os.environ.get("ET_MAX_TURNS", "8"))
MAX_NEW_TOKENS_PER_TURN = int(os.environ.get("ET_MAX_NEW_TOKENS", "512"))
CMD_TIMEOUT = float(os.environ.get("ET_CMD_TIMEOUT", "20"))
MAX_OBS_CHARS = int(os.environ.get("ET_MAX_OBS_CHARS", "1500"))
# Hard ceiling on one episode, covering everything: generation, the shell, the
# verifier and teardown. Every individual step is already bounded, yet the run
# still hung -- slime builds its HTTP client with `httpx.Timeout(None)`, so a
# `/generate` that never comes back waits forever, and asyncio's
# `Process.wait()` has its own way of never resolving (see sandbox.REAP_TIMEOUT).
# Both drivers await every episode before returning, so one episode that never
# finishes stalls the entire rollout rather than failing it. The default is
# deliberately far above any legitimate episode -- 6 turns of generation plus
# 6x20s of commands plus a 180s verifier -- so this only ever fires on a hang.
EPISODE_TIMEOUT = float(os.environ.get("ET_EPISODE_TIMEOUT", "900"))

STOP_STRINGS = ["</command>", "</action>"]
_OBS_SENTINEL = "@@ET_OBSERVATION@@"

_COMMAND_RE = re.compile(r"<command>(.*?)(?:</command>|\Z)", re.DOTALL)
_ACTION_RE = re.compile(r"<action>\s*done\s*</action>", re.IGNORECASE)


class _Chat:
    """Derives the chat-template glue once, without hardcoding ChatML.

    `head` is the token prefix the policy generates from. `tail` is the text
    that must follow a generated assistant turn in order to inject one user
    turn and re-open the assistant turn.
    """

    def __init__(self, tokenizer) -> None:
        kwargs = {"tokenize": False, "add_generation_prompt": True, "enable_thinking": False}
        probe_msgs = [{"role": "system", "content": "S"}, {"role": "user", "content": "U"}]
        head = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(probe_msgs, **kwargs)
        full = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
            probe_msgs
            + [{"role": "assistant", "content": "A"}, {"role": "user", "content": _OBS_SENTINEL}],
            **kwargs,
        )
        prefix = os.path.commonprefix([head, full])
        assert full[len(prefix) : len(prefix) + 1] == "A", "unexpected chat template shape"
        self._tail = full[len(prefix) + 1 :]
        assert _OBS_SENTINEL in self._tail, "could not locate the observation slot in the chat template"
        self._kwargs = kwargs

    def prompt(self, tokenizer, instruction: str) -> str:
        return tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
            [{"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM_PROMPT}, {"role": "user", "content": instruction}],
            **self._kwargs,
        )

    def observation(self, text: str) -> str:
        return self._tail.replace(_OBS_SENTINEL, text)


_CHAT: _Chat | None = None
_SCRATCH_CHECKED = False


def _chat(tokenizer) -> _Chat:
    global _CHAT
    if _CHAT is None:
        _CHAT = _Chat(tokenizer)
    return _CHAT


def _check_scratch_once() -> None:
    global _SCRATCH_CHECKED
    if not _SCRATCH_CHECKED:
        check_exec_capable(SCRATCH_ROOT)
        _SCRATCH_CHECKED = True


def parse_action(text: str) -> tuple[str, str | None]:
    """Return ("command", cmd) / ("done", None) / ("invalid", None).

    Mirrors the harness rule "only your first command in command tags will be
    executed": whichever of `<command>` / `<action>` appears first wins.
    """
    cmd_match = _COMMAND_RE.search(text)
    act_match = _ACTION_RE.search(text)
    if act_match and (cmd_match is None or act_match.start() < cmd_match.start()):
        return "done", None
    if cmd_match:
        cmd = cmd_match.group(1).strip()
        return ("command", cmd) if cmd else ("invalid", None)
    return "invalid", None


def _abort(args, sample: Sample, turns: int, **extra) -> Sample:
    """Finish a sample that is giving up, with every field slime will index.

    `_convert_samples_to_train_data` repeatedly decides whether an optional
    per-sample field is present by looking at `samples[0]` alone, and then
    indexes *every* sample in the batch. An episode that gives up while its
    neighbours complete normally is therefore not a local failure -- it takes
    down the whole rollout, from a traceback that names slime rather than this
    file. Three such fields exist on this path:

      * `reward` -- eval metrics take `sum(rewards) / len(rewards)` over the
        split (rollout_metrics.py:232), so one `None` raises;
      * `metadata["round_number"]` -- ray/rollout.py:382, `KeyError`;
      * `rollout_log_probs` -- ray/rollout.py:386, and a sample that never got
        a single response token still has `None` there, which surfaces much
        later as `TypeError: must be real number, not NoneType` inside
        `torch.as_tensor`.

    The last one is why an aborted episode with nothing generated is given one
    end-of-text token, appended as *non-trainable*: that is slime's own
    supported way to add tokens that carry no gradient, so every per-sample
    list ends up present, mutually consistent and zero-weighted rather than
    absent. Centralising the giving-up paths here is the only way to keep all
    of this true as new ones get added.
    """
    sample.status = Sample.Status.ABORTED
    sample.reward = 0.0
    if sample.response_length == 0:
        eos = GenerateState(args).tokenizer.eos_token_id
        sample.append_response_tokens(args, tokens=[eos], trainable=False, text="")
    sample.metadata = {
        **(sample.metadata or {}),
        "et_task": sample.label,
        "round_number": turns,
        **extra,
    }
    return sample


def _turns_so_far(sample: Sample) -> int:
    """How many turns the episode had started when it was interrupted.

    `_generate` stamps the turn counter into metadata as it goes, precisely so
    that a timeout or an exception -- which unwinds past every local variable --
    still has a truthful number to report.
    """
    return int((sample.metadata or {}).get("round_number", 0))


async def generate(args, sample: Sample, sampling_params) -> Sample:
    """slime hook: `custom_generate_function_path`. Never raises, always returns.

    Both drivers that call this -- `generate_rollout` and `eval_rollout` --
    launch every episode as a task and then `await` them through
    `asyncio.as_completed`, so an episode that raises discards the entire
    rollout and an episode that hangs stalls it indefinitely. Both have
    happened: a task printing a line longer than asyncio's stream limit threw
    away several hundred finished episodes, and a task whose instructions are
    to leave `sleep 1000` and `yes` running in the background froze an eval at
    1199 of 1200 episodes.

    Nothing one episode can do is worth a whole rollout, so an episode that
    fails or stops making progress is reported the way a setup failure already
    is: aborted, reward 0, flagged in metadata so it is visible afterwards
    rather than silently absorbed.
    """
    try:
        return await asyncio.wait_for(_generate(args, sample, sampling_params), timeout=EPISODE_TIMEOUT)
    except asyncio.CancelledError:
        raise
    except (asyncio.TimeoutError, TimeoutError):
        logging.getLogger(__name__).warning(
            "episode for task %s hit the %.0fs ceiling and was abandoned", sample.label, EPISODE_TIMEOUT
        )
        return _abort(args, sample, _turns_so_far(sample), et_timeout=EPISODE_TIMEOUT)
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 -- deliberately broad; see above
        logging.getLogger(__name__).exception("episode for task %s failed", sample.label)
        return _abort(args, sample, _turns_so_far(sample), et_error=f"{type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")


async def _generate(args, sample: Sample, sampling_params) -> Sample:
    assert not args.partial_rollout, "partial rollout is not supported by this rollout function"

    # Reset anything a previous attempt left behind.
    sample.rollout_log_probs = None
    sample.rollout_top_p_token_ids = None
    sample.rollout_top_p_token_offsets = None
    sample.response = ""
    sample.response_length = 0
    sample.loss_mask = None
    sample.reward = None

    _check_scratch_once()

    state = GenerateState(args)
    tokenizer = state.tokenizer
    chat = _chat(tokenizer)
    url = f"http://{args.sglang_router_ip}:{args.sglang_router_port}/generate"

    instruction = sample.prompt if isinstance(sample.prompt, str) else str(sample.prompt)
    prompt_text = chat.prompt(tokenizer, instruction)
    prompt_ids = tokenizer(prompt_text, add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"]
    sample.tokens = list(prompt_ids)

    max_response_len = args.rollout_max_response_len
    task_dir = os.path.join(DATA_ROOT, "tasks", sample.label or "")

    episode = Episode(
        task_dir=task_dir,
        scratch_root=SCRATCH_ROOT,
        cmd_timeout=CMD_TIMEOUT,
        max_obs_chars=MAX_OBS_CHARS,
    )
    turns = 0
    finish = "max_turns"
    try:
        if not await episode.start():
            # A task whose setup cannot be reproduced must not pollute training.
            return _abort(args, sample, turns, et_setup_failed=True)

        for turns in range(1, MAX_TURNS + 1):
            # Visible to `generate`'s handlers, which unwind past `turns`.
            sample.metadata = {**(sample.metadata or {}), "round_number": turns}
            budget = max_response_len - sample.response_length
            if budget <= 0:
                sample.status = Sample.Status.TRUNCATED
                finish = "response_budget"
                break

            sp = dict(sampling_params)
            sp["max_new_tokens"] = min(MAX_NEW_TOKENS_PER_TURN, budget)
            sp["stop"] = list(dict.fromkeys(list(sp.get("stop") or []) + STOP_STRINGS))

            output = await post(url, {"input_ids": sample.tokens, "sampling_params": sp, "return_logprob": True})
            meta = output["meta_info"]
            # Every path out of this function goes through `_abort`, which sets
            # the per-sample fields slime indexes across the whole batch. The
            # abort below is the common one: at the end of a rollout slime calls
            # SGLang's `/abort_request` on everything still in flight, so a
            # straggler episode lands here while its neighbours completed
            # normally -- exactly the mix that exposes a missing key.
            if meta["finish_reason"]["type"] == "abort":
                return _abort(args, sample, turns, et_finish="sglang_abort")
            if "output_token_logprobs" not in meta:
                return _abort(args, sample, turns, et_finish="no_logprobs")

            tokens = [t[1] for t in meta["output_token_logprobs"]]
            log_probs = [t[0] for t in meta["output_token_logprobs"]]
            text = tokenizer.decode(tokens)

            # Assistant turn: trainable.
            sample.append_response_tokens(
                args, tokens=tokens, log_probs=log_probs, trainable=True, meta_info=meta, text=text
            )

            if meta["finish_reason"]["type"] == "length" and sample.response_length >= max_response_len:
                finish = "length"
                break

            kind, command = parse_action(text)
            if kind == "done":
                finish = "done"
                break
            if kind == "invalid":
                finish = "invalid_action"
                break

            observation = await episode.exec(command or "")
            obs_text = chat.observation(observation)
            obs_ids = tokenizer(obs_text, add_special_tokens=False)["input_ids"]

            # Environment turn: not trainable, and never passed log probs.
            overflow = sample.response_length + len(obs_ids) - max_response_len
            if overflow > 0:
                obs_ids = obs_ids[: max(0, len(obs_ids) - overflow)]
            if obs_ids:
                sample.append_response_tokens(args, tokens=obs_ids, trainable=False, text=obs_text)
            if overflow > 0:
                sample.status = Sample.Status.TRUNCATED
                finish = "response_budget"
                break

        reward, verifier_log = await episode.score()
        sample.reward = float(reward)

        if sample.status in (Sample.Status.PENDING, None):
            sample.status = Sample.Status.COMPLETED
        sample.metadata = {
            **(sample.metadata or {}),
            "round_number": turns,
            "et_task": sample.label,
            "et_finish": finish,
            "et_reward": float(reward),
            "et_verifier_tail": verifier_log[-200:],
        }
        return sample
    finally:
        await episode.close()


async def reward_func(args, sample: Sample, **kwargs) -> float:
    """Defensive fallback.

    `generate` already sets `sample.reward`, and slime skips the reward model
    whenever that is not None, so this is normally never called.
    """
    return float(sample.reward) if sample.reward is not None else 0.0

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Dump every held-out episode's reward, keyed by task, as the eval runs.

slime's own eval logging reports means: `eval/et_test` is the pass rate over the
whole split, and that is all it keeps. A mean is not enough to compare two
training runs here. The two arms are scored on the *same* tasks, so the right
test is a paired one -- per task, did this arm solve it more often than the
other? -- and a paired test needs the per-task numbers, which the mean has
already thrown away. Across a 300-task split an unpaired comparison of two
~6% pass rates needs several times the episodes to reach the same power,
because almost all of the variance between the arms' means is task difficulty
that is identical on both sides and cancels when you subtract per task.

So this hook writes one JSONL row per episode next to the run's other
artifacts. It returns a falsy value on purpose: slime treats a truthy return as
"the custom logger handled it", and the aggregate lines are still wanted.

Wired in by run.sh as
`--custom-eval-rollout-log-function-path et.eval_log.log_eval_rollout_data`.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os

# Written by the RolloutManager actor, not by the driver, so the path has to
# travel through the Ray runtime env rather than being inherited from run.sh.
DUMP_DIR = os.environ.get("ET_EVAL_DUMP_DIR", "")


def _status(sample) -> str:
    status = getattr(sample, "status", None)
    return getattr(status, "value", str(status))


def _reward(sample, fallback):
    """The scalar reward, whatever shape the sample carries it in.

    slime allows `Sample.reward` to be a dict (`--reward-key` picks a field out
    of it). `data[name]["rewards"]` has already been resolved to scalars, so it
    is the authoritative source; the sample is only consulted if the two lists
    somehow fail to line up.
    """
    if fallback is not None:
        return fallback
    reward = getattr(sample, "reward", None)
    return reward if not isinstance(reward, dict) else None


def log_eval_rollout_data(rollout_id, args, data, extra_metrics=None):  # noqa: ARG001
    """slime hook: `custom_eval_rollout_log_function_path`.

    Returns None so slime goes on to emit its own aggregate `eval N:` line --
    this adds a record, it does not replace one.
    """
    if not DUMP_DIR:
        return None
    os.makedirs(DUMP_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    path = os.path.join(DUMP_DIR, f"eval_rollout_{rollout_id:04d}.jsonl")

    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        for name, payload in data.items():
            samples = payload.get("samples") or []
            rewards = payload.get("rewards") or []
            for i, sample in enumerate(samples):
                row = {
                    "rollout_id": rollout_id,
                    "dataset": name,
                    # The task directory name, which is what makes the two arms'
                    # rows joinable and the comparison paired.
                    "label": getattr(sample, "label", None),
                    "index": getattr(sample, "index", None),
                    "group_index": getattr(sample, "group_index", None),
                    "reward": _reward(sample, rewards[i] if i < len(rewards) else None),
                    "response_length": getattr(sample, "response_length", None),
                    "status": _status(sample),
                }
                fh.write(json.dumps(row, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
    return None

With a randomly initialized value head (std ~0.02-0.05 for GPT init... in Megatron, `LinearForLastLayer` initializes... let me check), the value prediction could be any scale.

Wait — actually the important observation: the value loss STARTS at 7.2 and DROPS during warmup (7.2 → 5.4 → 3.4 → 1.9 → 1.5). The critic learns. That's the warmup working. The claimed incident is presumably about "value loss in warmup being huge (7.0) vs stage A (6.9)" — hmm, both similar.

34	def _is_indexer_parameter(name: str) -> bool:
35	    """Return whether *name* belongs to a DSA indexer.
36	
37	    The GLM plugin exposes indexer projections directly under
38	    ``self_attention``. Megatron's upstream DSA implementation instead nests
39	    them under ``self_attention.core_attention.indexer``. Keep the ownership
40	    check structural so similarly named non-indexer projections stay trainable.
41	    """
42	
43	    parts = name.split(".")
44	    for index, part in enumerate(parts):
45	        if part != "self_attention" or index + 1 >= len(parts):
46	            continue
47	        attention_parts = parts[index + 1 :]
48	        if attention_parts[0] in _INDEXER_DIRECT_SUBMODULE_NAMES:
49	            return True
50	        if "indexer" in attention_parts[:-1]:
51	            return True
52	    return False

76	        output_size: int,

82	        self.sequence_parallel = config.sequence_parallel
83	        if self.sequence_parallel:
84	            self.weight.sequence_parallel = True
85	            if bias:
86	                self.bias.sequence_parallel = True
87	
88	        init_method_std = getattr(config, "init_method_std", None)
89	        if init_method_std is None:
90	            init_method_std = 0.02
91	        self.weight.data.normal_(mean=0.0, std=init_method_std)
92	        if bias:
93	            self.bias.data.zero_()
94

96	        self,
97	        input_: torch.Tensor,
98	        weight: torch.Tensor | None = None,
99	        runtime_gather_output: bool | None = None,
100	    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, None]:
101	        logits = super().forward(input_)
102	        logits = logits.float()
103	        if self.sequence_parallel:
104	            logits = tensor_parallel.gather_from_sequence_parallel_region(logits, tensor_parallel_output_grad=False)

ROLLOUT_TOP_P_TOKEN_KEYS = (
    "rollout_top_p_token_ids",
    "rollout_top_p_token_offsets",
)


# Optional capture of per-sample policy log-probs computed during the training
# forward. Used only when dumping train debug data in configs that skip the
# separate log-prob recompute (can_reuse_log_probs_in_loss / use_rollout_logprobs):
# the values are identical to a separate compute_log_prob pass, so we snapshot
# them here at no extra forward. Keyed by GLOBAL rollout position so the writer
# can put them back in sample order regardless of pipeline/microbatch order.
_LOG_PROB_CAPTURE: "dict[int, torch.Tensor] | None" = None


def enable_log_prob_capture() -> None:
    """Start capturing training-forward log-probs (call before ``train``)."""
    global _LOG_PROB_CAPTURE
    _LOG_PROB_CAPTURE = {}


def drain_captured_log_probs() -> "dict[int, torch.Tensor]":
    """Return captured ``{rollout_position: cp-local log_probs}`` and stop capturing."""
    global _LOG_PROB_CAPTURE
    captured = _LOG_PROB_CAPTURE or {}
    _LOG_PROB_CAPTURE = None
    return captured


def _maybe_capture_log_probs(batch: RolloutBatch, log_probs: list[torch.Tensor]) -> None:
    """Snapshot per-sample CP-local ``log_probs`` keyed by global rollout position.

    No-op unless :func:`enable_log_prob_capture` is active and the micro-batch
    carries ``partition`` (only added to the training keys when dumping). First
    occurrence per position wins, so multi-step training keeps the initial
    (old-policy) values. ``log_probs`` here is the per-sample list, in the same
    order as ``batch['partition']`` (both indexed by this micro-batch's
    ``micro_batch_indices``).
    """
    if _LOG_PROB_CAPTURE is None:
        return
    positions = batch.get("partition")
    if not positions:
        return
    for position, log_prob in zip(positions, log_probs, strict=True):
        if position not in _LOG_PROB_CAPTURE:
            _LOG_PROB_CAPTURE[position] = log_prob.detach().clone()


def get_rollout_top_p_logprob_kwargs(args: Namespace, batch: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    if args.rollout_top_p == 1.0:
        return {}

    top_p_token_ids = batch.get("rollout_top_p_token_ids")
    top_p_token_offsets = batch.get("rollout_top_p_token_offsets")
    if top_p_token_ids is None or top_p_token_offsets is None:
        raise ValueError("rollout_top_p != 1.0 requires rollout_top_p_token_ids and rollout_top_p_token_offsets.")
    return {
        "top_p_token_ids": top_p_token_ids,
        "top_p_token_offsets": top_p_token_offsets,
    }


def get_responses(
    logits: torch.Tensor,
    *,
    args: Namespace,
    unconcat_tokens: list[torch.Tensor],
    total_lengths: list[int],
    response_lengths: list[int],
    apply_temperature: bool = True,
) -> Iterator[tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]]:
    """Yield response-aligned `(logits_chunk, tokens_chunk)` pairs per sample.

    After squeezing batch dimension and optionally applying temperature scaling, this
    function extracts the logits and tokens corresponding to response segments
    for each sample. When context parallelism is disabled, it slices directly
    from the concatenated sequence. With context parallelism enabled, it
    handles split sequences across ranks.

    Args:
        logits: Model outputs with shape `[1, T, V]` (policy) or `[1, T, 1]`
            (value). Must be float32.
        args: Configuration containing `rollout_temperature` for optional scaling.
        unconcat_tokens: List of token tensors (prompt+response) per sample.
        total_lengths: Total sequence lengths (prompt+response) per sample.
        response_lengths: Response segment lengths per sample.

    carries ``partition`` (only added to the training keys when dumping). First
    occurrence per position wins, so multi-step training keeps the initial
    (old-policy) values. ``log_probs`` here is the per-sample list, in the same
    order as ``batch['partition']`` (both indexed by this micro-batch's

    if _LOG_PROB_CAPTURE is None:

    positions = batch.get("partition")

"""Per-episode Endless Terminals sandbox.

Endless Terminals ships one Docker image per task (`FROM ubuntu:22.04` + apt).
Building ~50 images is impossible on an air-gapped host and would also defeat
the "avoid duplicate images" constraint, so each episode instead gets a private
directory tree that stands in for the task's `/home/user`.

The guest path `/home/user` is kept *verbatim* in the prompt, the setup script
and the pytest verifier -- it is rewritten to the episode's private directory
only at exec time, and rewritten back in the observation that is shown to the
model. The model therefore sees an authentic transcript while every episode is
fully isolated from every other one. No privileges (no mount namespace, no
chroot) are required, which matters on a shared host.

Commands run in one long-lived `bash` per episode, so `cd`, shell variables and
`export`s persist across turns exactly as they would in a real terminal.

`scratch_root` must allow execution -- see `check_exec_capable`. In particular
it must not be under `/dev/shm`, which the training image mounts `noexec`.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import contextlib
import os
import shutil
import signal
import subprocess
import sys
import uuid

# The path every Endless Terminals task (45 of 46) addresses exclusively.
GUEST_HOME = "/home/user"

# There is no package index reachable from inside the sandbox. Without these,
# any `pip install` -- whether the policy types one or a task's setup script
# calls a venv's pip by absolute path -- sits in pip's retry loop for minutes
# and outlives the timeout that killed its parent shell. With them it fails in
# under a second.
OFFLINE_ENV = {
    "PIP_NO_INDEX": "1",
    "PIP_RETRIES": "0",
    "PIP_TIMEOUT": "1",
    "PIP_NO_INPUT": "1",
    "PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK": "1",
}

DEFAULT_CMD_TIMEOUT = 20.0
DEFAULT_MAX_OBS_CHARS = 2000
SETUP_TIMEOUT = 120.0
SCORE_TIMEOUT = 180.0

# asyncio's StreamReader refuses to hand over a line until the whole line is
# buffered, and raises `ValueError` once one line passes its limit -- the
# default being 64 KiB, which a terminal task reaches just by `cat`-ing a
# minified file or a base64 blob. Raise the ceiling, and treat even the raised
# one as "this output is too long" rather than as an error: a single episode
# printing a long line must never be able to end a training run.

# truncated to max_obs_chars (1200 by default) anyway, so everything beyond
# this point was going to be thrown away -- holding it would only let one
# `yes`-style command grow a rollout worker's heap without bound.

# Reaping a killed process must not be able to block forever. asyncio resolves
# `Process.wait()` only once the child has exited *and* every pipe it was given
# has reached EOF, so a background job that inherited the shell's stdout keeps
# that future pending even after the shell itself is dead. Several Endless
# Terminals tasks ask for exactly that -- one instructs the policy to launch
# `sleep 1000` and `yes 'Compiling docs...'` as background jobs -- and it hung a
# whole eval at 1199/1200 episodes for half an hour before it was noticed. The
# process has been SIGKILLed by this point either way; waiting is a courtesy, so
# give up on it quickly and let the object be collected.
REAP_TIMEOUT = 10.0


async def _reap(proc) -> None:
    """Wait for an already-killed process, but never longer than REAP_TIMEOUT."""
    with contextlib.suppress(asyncio.TimeoutError, ProcessLookupError):
        await asyncio.wait_for(proc.wait(), timeout=REAP_TIMEOUT)


def check_exec_capable(root: str) -> None:
    """Fail loudly if `root` sits on a `noexec` filesystem.

    Many Endless Terminals tasks create a script and their verifiers assert
    `os.access(path, os.X_OK)`. On a `noexec` mount that returns False even at
    mode 755, so perfectly good tasks get silently rejected and any episode
    that has to run a script it just wrote fails for no visible reason.
    `/dev/shm` is `noexec` in the training image, which makes this very easy to
    hit, so check once up front instead.
    """
    os.makedirs(root, exist_ok=True)
    probe = os.path.join(root, f".execprobe_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}")
    try:
        with open(probe, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            fh.write("#!/bin/sh\nexit 0\n")
        os.chmod(probe, 0o755)
        if not os.access(probe, os.X_OK):
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"{root} is on a noexec filesystem (a mode-755 file there is not executable). "
                "Point ET_SCRATCH / --scratch at a directory that allows execution, e.g. /tmp."
            )
    finally:
        try:
            os.unlink(probe)
        except OSError:
            pass


def _truncate(text: str, limit: int) -> str:
    if len(text) <= limit:
        return text
    head = limit * 2 // 3
    tail = limit - head
    omitted = len(text) - head - tail
    return f"{text[:head]}\n...[{omitted} characters omitted]...\n{text[-tail:]}"


class Episode:
    """One task attempt in its own private filesystem tree."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        task_dir: str,
        scratch_root: str,
        cmd_timeout: float = DEFAULT_CMD_TIMEOUT,
        max_obs_chars: int = DEFAULT_MAX_OBS_CHARS,
    ) -> None:
        self.task_dir = task_dir
        self.task_id = os.path.basename(task_dir.rstrip("/"))
        self.cmd_timeout = cmd_timeout
        self.max_obs_chars = max_obs_chars

        self.uid = uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]
        self.base = os.path.join(scratch_root, f"ep_{self.task_id}_{self.uid}")
        self.home = os.path.join(self.base, "home", "user")
        # Marker is per-episode so a command that echoes it cannot spoof us.
        self.mark = f"__ET_DONE_{self.uid}__"

        self._shell: asyncio.subprocess.Process | None = None
        self.setup_ok = False
        self.setup_log = ""

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- paths
    def to_host(self, text: str) -> str:
        """Rewrite guest-visible `/home/user` paths to this episode's tree."""
        return text.replace(GUEST_HOME, self.home)

    def to_guest(self, text: str) -> str:
        """Rewrite host paths back to `/home/user` for display to the model."""
        return text.replace(self.home, GUEST_HOME)

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- setup
    async def start(self) -> bool:
        os.makedirs(self.home, exist_ok=True)
        setup = os.path.join(self.task_dir, "setup.sh")
        if os.path.isfile(setup):
            with open(setup, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
                script = self.to_host(fh.read())
            proc = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
                "bash",
                "-s",
                stdin=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
                stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
                stderr=asyncio.subprocess.STDOUT,
                cwd=self.base,
                env=self._env(),
            )
            try:
                out, _ = await asyncio.wait_for(
                    proc.communicate(script.encode()), timeout=SETUP_TIMEOUT
                )
            except asyncio.TimeoutError:
                proc.kill()
                await _reap(proc)
                self.setup_log = "setup timed out"
                return False
            self.setup_log = out.decode("utf-8", "replace")
            if proc.returncode != 0:
                return False

        self.setup_ok = True
        await self._spawn_shell()
        return True

    def _env(self) -> dict:
        env = dict(os.environ)
        env.update(
            {
                "HOME": self.home,
                "PWD": self.home,
                "TERM": "dumb",
                "LC_ALL": "C.UTF-8",
                "LANG": "C.UTF-8",
                "PS1": "",
                "PS2": "",
                "DEBIAN_FRONTEND": "noninteractive",
                **OFFLINE_ENV,
            }
        )
        # Never let an episode inherit the trainer's proxy / CUDA context.
        for drop in ("CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES", "http_proxy", "https_proxy", "HTTP_PROXY", "HTTPS_PROXY"):
            env.pop(drop, None)
        return env

    async def _spawn_shell(self) -> None:
        # Own session/process group, so killing a wedged turn takes the whole
        # command tree with it rather than orphaning its children. Over a
        # training run that is the difference between a clean host and
        # thousands of leaked background processes.
        self._shell = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
            "bash",
            "--noprofile",
            "--norc",
            stdin=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
            stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
            stderr=asyncio.subprocess.STDOUT,
            cwd=self.home,
            env=self._env(),
            start_new_session=True,
            limit=SHELL_STREAM_LIMIT,
        )

    async def _kill_shell(self) -> None:
        if self._shell is None:
            return
        with contextlib.suppress(ProcessLookupError, PermissionError, OSError):
            os.killpg(os.getpgid(self._shell.pid), signal.SIGKILL)
        with contextlib.suppress(ProcessLookupError):
            self._shell.kill()
        await _reap(self._shell)
        self._shell = None

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------- exec
    async def exec(self, command: str) -> str:
        """Run one shell command; return the observation string verbatim in the
        format the Endless Terminals harness uses."""
        host_cmd = self.to_host(command)

        # A command with unbalanced quotes would hang the persistent shell
        # waiting for PS2 continuation, so reject it up front the way the
        # upstream harness effectively does.
        syntax = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
            "bash",
            "-n",
            "-c",
            host_cmd,
            stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
            stderr=asyncio.subprocess.STDOUT,
        )
        syn_out, _ = await syntax.communicate()
        if syntax.returncode != 0:
            return self._format(self.to_guest(syn_out.decode("utf-8", "replace")), 2)

        if self._shell is None or self._shell.returncode is not None:
            await self._spawn_shell()

        assert self._shell is not None and self._shell.stdin is not None
        payload = f"{host_cmd}\nprintf '\\n%s%d\\n' '{self.mark}' \"$?\"\n"
        try:
            self._shell.stdin.write(payload.encode())
            await self._shell.stdin.drain()
        except (BrokenPipeError, ConnectionResetError):
            await self._kill_shell()
            return self._format("shell died", 1)

        try:
            out, rc = await asyncio.wait_for(self._read_until_mark(), timeout=self.cmd_timeout)
        except asyncio.TimeoutError:
            await self._kill_shell()
            await self._spawn_shell()
            return self._format(f"command timed out after {self.cmd_timeout:.0f}s", 124)
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 -- deliberately broad
            # The shell is in an unknown state, so replace it, and hand the
            # policy an ordinary failed-command observation. Letting this
            # propagate would abort the whole rollout: the eval driver awaits
            # every episode through `asyncio.as_completed`, so one raising
            # episode discards the other several hundred that succeeded.
            await self._kill_shell()
            await self._spawn_shell()
            return self._format(f"could not read command output: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}", 1)

        return self._format(self.to_guest(out), rc)

    async def _read_chunk(self) -> bytes:
        """`readline`, except an over-long line comes back in pieces.

        asyncio's StreamReader will not hand over a line until it has the whole
        thing buffered, and raises once one line passes its limit. A terminal
        task reaches any limit you pick by `cat`-ing a minified file or a
        base64 blob -- and the raised exception used to propagate all the way
        out of `RolloutManager.eval`, so one task printing one long line ended
        the entire run. The buffered data is still readable, so draining it
        with a bounded `read` both recovers the stream and keeps the output.
        """
        assert self._shell is not None and self._shell.stdout is not None
        try:
            return await self._shell.stdout.readline()
        except (ValueError, asyncio.LimitOverrunError):
            return await self._shell.stdout.read(SHELL_STREAM_LIMIT // 2)

    async def _read_until_mark(self) -> tuple[str, int]:
        assert self._shell is not None and self._shell.stdout is not None
        chunks: list[str] = []
        captured = 0
        # `_read_chunk` does not promise to return whole lines, so the split
        # into lines happens here rather than being assumed. Doing it this way
        # also means the marker is still recognised when it arrives in the same
        # chunk as the tail of a long line.
        pending = ""
        while True:
            data = await self._read_chunk()
            if not data:  # shell exited (e.g. the model ran `exit`)
                chunks.append(pending)
                return "".join(chunks), 1
            pending += data.decode("utf-8", "replace")
            while (nl := pending.find("\n")) != -1:
                line, pending = pending[: nl + 1], pending[nl + 1 :]
                if line.startswith(self.mark):
                    try:
                        rc = int(line[len(self.mark) :].strip() or 1)
                    except ValueError:
                        rc = 1
                    # Drop the single blank line our printf prepended.
                    body = "".join(chunks)
                    if body.endswith("\n"):
                        body = body[:-1]
                    return body, rc
                # Past the cap, keep reading -- the marker is the only way to
                # know the command finished -- but stop accumulating. The
                # observation is truncated to max_obs_chars regardless, so the
                # dropped text could not have been shown anyway.
                if captured < MAX_CAPTURE_CHARS:
                    chunks.append(line)
                    captured += len(line)
            # Bound the live buffer too, not only what is kept: `yes | tr -d
            # '\n'` emits no newline at all, so `pending` would otherwise grow
            # for the whole 20s turn. What is left here is by construction the
            # start of a line with no newline in it, so the marker -- which is
            # always the first thing on its line -- can only be at index 0:
            # keeping the head preserves detection, and the tail dropped is
            # mid-line text well past what the observation can show.
            if len(pending) > MAX_CAPTURE_CHARS:
                pending = pending[:MAX_CAPTURE_CHARS]

    def _format(self, output: str, rc: int) -> str:
        head = "Command executed successfully." if rc == 0 else "Command failed."
        return f"{head} Output: {_truncate(output, self.max_obs_chars)}\n\n(exit_code={rc})"

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- reward
    async def score(self) -> tuple[float, str]:
        """Run the task's own pytest verifier. Returns (reward, log)."""
        src = os.path.join(self.task_dir, "test_final_state.py")
        if not os.path.isfile(src):
            return 0.0, "no verifier"
        with open(src, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            test_src = self.to_host(fh.read())
        dst = os.path.join(self.base, "test_final_state.py")
        with open(dst, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            fh.write(test_src)

        proc = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
            sys.executable,
            "-m",
            "pytest",
            dst,
            "-q",
            "--no-header",
            "-p",
            "no:cacheprovider",
            stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
            stderr=asyncio.subprocess.STDOUT,
            cwd=self.base,
            env=self._env(),
        )
        try:
            out, _ = await asyncio.wait_for(proc.communicate(), timeout=SCORE_TIMEOUT)
        except asyncio.TimeoutError:
            proc.kill()
            await _reap(proc)
            return 0.0, "verifier timed out"
        log = self.to_guest(out.decode("utf-8", "replace"))
        return (1.0 if proc.returncode == 0 else 0.0), log

    # --------------------------------------------------------------- cleanup
    async def close(self) -> None:
        await self._kill_shell()
        shutil.rmtree(self.base, ignore_errors=True)


def sync_score(task_dir: str, base: str, home: str) -> tuple[int, str]:
    """Blocking variant of `score`, used by the offline dataset validator."""
    src = os.path.join(task_dir, "test_final_state.py")
    with open(src, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        test_src = fh.read().replace(GUEST_HOME, home)
    dst = os.path.join(base, "test_final_state.py")
    with open(dst, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        fh.write(test_src)
    env = dict(os.environ, HOME=home, LC_ALL="C.UTF-8", LANG="C.UTF-8", **OFFLINE_ENV)
    proc = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "-m", "pytest", dst, "-q", "--no-header", "-p", "no:cacheprovider"],
        cwd=base,
        env=env,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        timeout=SCORE_TIMEOUT,
    )
    return proc.returncode, proc.stdout + proc.stderr

288	    async def _read_chunk(self) -> bytes:
289	        """`readline`, except an over-long line comes back in pieces.
290	
291	        asyncio's StreamReader will not hand over a line until it has the whole
292	        thing buffered, and raises once one line passes its limit. A terminal
293	        task reaches any limit you pick by `cat`-ing a minified file or a
294	        base64 blob -- and the raised exception used to propagate all the way
295	        out of `RolloutManager.eval`, so one task printing one long line ended
296	        the entire run. The buffered data is still readable, so draining it
297	        with a bounded `read` both recovers the stream and keeps the output.
298	        """
299	        assert self._shell is not None and self._shell.stdout is not None
300	        try:
301	            return await self._shell.stdout.readline()
302	        except (ValueError, asyncio.LimitOverrunError):
303	            return await self._shell.stdout.read(SHELL_STREAM_LIMIT // 2)

305	    async def _read_until_mark(self) -> tuple[str, int]:
306	        assert self._shell is not None and self._shell.stdout is not None
307	        chunks: list[str] = []
308	        captured = 0
309	        # `_read_chunk` does not promise to return whole lines, so the split
310	        # into lines happens here rather than being assumed. Doing it this way
311	        # also means the marker is still recognised when it arrives in the same
312	        # chunk as the tail of a long line.
313	        pending = ""
314	        while True:
315	            data = await self._read_chunk()
316	            if not data:  # shell exited (e.g. the model ran `exit`)
317	                chunks.append(pending)
318	                return "".join(chunks), 1
319	            pending += data.decode("utf-8", "replace")
320	            while (nl := pending.find("\n")) != -1:
321	                line, pending = pending[: nl + 1], pending[nl + 1 :]
322	                if line.startswith(self.mark):
323	                    try:
324	                        rc = int(line[len(self.mark) :].strip() or 1)
325	                    except ValueError:

327	                    # Drop the single blank line our printf prepended.
328	                    body = "".join(chunks)
329	                    if body.endswith("\n"):
330	                        body = body[:-1]
331	                    return body, rc
332	                # Past the cap, keep reading -- the marker is the only way to
333	                # know the command finished -- but stop accumulating. The
334	                # observation is truncated to max_obs_chars regardless, so the
335	                # dropped text could not have been shown anyway.
336	                if captured < MAX_CAPTURE_CHARS:
337	                    chunks.append(line)
338	                    captured += len(line)
339	            # Bound the live buffer too, not only what is kept: `yes | tr -d
340	            # '\n'` emits no newline at all, so `pending` would otherwise grow
341	            # for the whole 20s turn. What is left here is by construction the
342	            # start of a line with no newline in it, so the marker -- which is
343	            # always the first thing on its line -- can only be at index 0:
344	            # keeping the head preserves detection, and the tail dropped is
345	            # mid-line text well past what the observation can show.
346	            if len(pending) > MAX_CAPTURE_CHARS:
347	                pending = pending[:MAX_CAPTURE_CHARS]

363	            fh.write(test_src)

def effective_response_length(self):
        return sum(self.loss_mask) if self.loss_mask is not None else self.response_length

    def append_response_tokens(
        self,
        args=None,
        *,
        tokens=None,
        log_probs=None,
        trainable: bool = True,
        meta_info: dict | None = None,
        text: str | None = None,
        update_terminal_info: bool = True,
    ):
        """
        Append response-side tokens and keep training metadata aligned.

        Model-generated tokens should pass ``trainable=True`` plus SGLang
        ``meta_info`` and log probabilities. Tool/environment tokens should pass
        ``trainable=False``; they receive loss-mask zeros and empty top-p spans
        when top-p replay is active.
        """
        tokens = _to_int_list(tokens)
        log_probs = _to_float_list(log_probs)
        if log_probs is not None and len(log_probs) != len(tokens):
            raise ValueError(f"log_probs length {len(log_probs)} != tokens length {len(tokens)}")
        if tokens and trainable and log_probs is None:
            raise ValueError("trainable response tokens require rollout log probabilities.")
        if tokens and not trainable:
            if log_probs is not None:
                raise ValueError("non-trainable response tokens should not pass rollout log probabilities.")
            log_probs = [0.0] * len(tokens)

        if text is not None:
            self.response += text

        previous_response_length = self.response_length
        if tokens:
            self.tokens += tokens
            self.response_length += len(tokens)
            if self.loss_mask is None:
                self.loss_mask = [1] * previous_response_length
            self.loss_mask += [1 if trainable else 0] * len(tokens)

        if log_probs is not None:
            if self.rollout_log_probs is None:
                if trainable and previous_response_length:
                    raise ValueError(
                        "Cannot append trainable rollout log probabilities to a sample with existing response "
                        "tokens but no existing rollout_log_probs."
                    )
                self.rollout_log_probs = [0.0] * previous_response_length
            self.rollout_log_probs += log_probs

        should_pad_top_p = bool(tokens and not trainable)
        if meta_info is not None or should_pad_top_p:
            self._apply_meta_info(
                args,
                meta_info or {},
                new_token_count=len(tokens),
                pad_missing_top_p=should_pad_top_p,
                update_terminal_info=update_terminal_info,
            )

        self._validate_response_metadata_lengths()

    def _apply_meta_info(
        self,
        args,
        meta_info: dict,
        *,
        new_token_count: int = 0,
        pad_missing_top_p: bool = False,
        update_terminal_info: bool = True,
    ) -> None:
        applied_top_p_data = False
        if new_token_count:
            top_p_data = _extract_rollout_top_p_token_data(meta_info, expected_num_tokens=new_token_count)
            if top_p_data is not None:
                applied_top_p_data = True
                base_token_ids, base_offsets = self.rollout_top_p_token_ids, self.rollout_top_p_token_offsets

def _build_flattened_tensor_data(
    named_tensors: list[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]],
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    if not named_tensors:
        return {
            "flattened_tensor": torch.empty(0, dtype=torch.uint8, device=accelerator.current_device()),
            "metadata": [],
        }

    # Do not reuse the IPC-facing flattened tensor. SGLang returns from the
    # HTTP/Ray request after enqueueing GPU copies into model weights, but it
    # does not guarantee a CUDA-device sync before the response. Reusing and
    # overwriting the same producer buffer immediately after ray.get can race
    # with the consumer-side copy and corrupt weights.
    flattened_tensor_bucket = FlattenedTensorBucket(named_tensors=named_tensors)
    return {
        "flattened_tensor": flattened_tensor_bucket.get_flattened_tensor(),
        "metadata": flattened_tensor_bucket.get_metadata(),
    }

1	#!/bin/bash
2	#
3	# Multi-Turn PPO on Endless Terminals with Qwen3-1.7B, on slime v0.3.2.
4	#
5	# The run has two stages:
6	#
7	#   Stage A -- "the previous training run".  A real PPO rollout (actor + critic)
8	#              starting from the base HF model, which saves a Megatron
9	#              checkpoint for both roles.
10	#
11	#   Stage B -- "the model was reloaded".  The actor genuinely resumes from
12	#              Stage A's Megatron checkpoint (weights *and* optimizer state).
13	#              The critic's backbone is reloaded from the base model.  Stage B
14	#              opens with NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS critic-only rollouts (the
15	#              warmup window) and then trains actor and critic jointly.
16	#
17	# The full slime source tree is bundled in the workspace (slime/) and is the
18	# copy that runs -- this script puts it ahead of the image's install on
19	# PYTHONPATH, so editing slime/ here is what takes effect, with nothing to
20	# install first.
21	#
22	# NOTE ON A SHARED HOST: unlike slime's own example scripts this one never runs
23	# `pkill -9 ray / pkill -9 python / ray stop --force` on entry.  It is meant to
24	# run inside its own container, and it brings up a private Ray head on a
25	# non-default port with a private temp dir.
26	
27	set -euo pipefail
28	
29	WS="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" &>/dev/null && pwd)"
30	
31	# The container runs as root while /workspace is a bind mount owned by whoever
32	# checked the case out, so any .pyc written here lands root-owned in their tree
33	# -- and `importlib` copies the *source* file's mode onto the .pyc, so a 600
34	# source yields a 600 root-owned file that even the owner cannot read, and
35	# `cp -r` of the case fails. Nothing here benefits from a bytecode cache.
36	export PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1
37	
38	MODEL_DIR="${MODEL_DIR:-${WS}/Qwen3-1.7B}"
39	ET_SRC="${ET_SRC:-${WS}/endless-terminals}"
40	SLIME_HOME="${SLIME_HOME:-${WS}/slime}"
41	OUT_DIR="${OUT_DIR:-${WS}/outputs}"
42	CKPT_ROOT="${CKPT_ROOT:-/ckpt}"
43	
44	# Endless Terminals sandbox knobs; also forwarded into the Ray workers, which
45	# read them at import time in et/rollout.py.
46	#
47	# These must NOT live under /dev/shm: it is mounted noexec in the training
48	# image, and many tasks' verifiers assert os.access(path, os.X_OK), which is
49	# False there even at mode 755.
50	export ET_DATA_ROOT="${ET_DATA_ROOT:-/tmp/et_prompts}"
51	export ET_SCRATCH="${ET_SCRATCH:-/tmp/et_episodes}"
52	export ET_MAX_TURNS="${ET_MAX_TURNS:-6}"
53	export ET_MAX_NEW_TOKENS="${ET_MAX_NEW_TOKENS:-384}"
54	export ET_CMD_TIMEOUT="${ET_CMD_TIMEOUT:-20}"
55	export ET_MAX_OBS_CHARS="${ET_MAX_OBS_CHARS:-1200}"
56	
57	NUM_GPUS="${NUM_GPUS:-2}"
58	TP_SIZE="${TP_SIZE:-2}"
59	SGLANG_MEM_FRACTION="${SGLANG_MEM_FRACTION:-0.55}"
60	# Rollouts per stage. Both stages use the same count on purpose, and must:
61	# slime derives `train_iters` from `--num-rollout` (model.py:203) and Megatron
62	# stores the resulting LR/weight-decay horizons inside the checkpoint, then
63	# asserts on reload that they match the ones the new arguments imply
64	# ("total number of iterations do not match"). Giving Stage B a different
65	# rollout count than Stage A would trip that assert before any training runs.
66	# In Stage A these rollouts are ordinary PPO; Stage B opens with
67	# NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS critic-only rollouts -- the warmup window -- and then
68	# trains actor and critic jointly for the rest.
69	NUM_ROLLOUTS="${NUM_ROLLOUTS:-2}"
70	# Stage B is the long one: critic warmup followed by joint PPO, trained until
71	# the validation pass rate stops moving. It no longer has to match Stage A's
72	# rollout count -- see --override-opt-param-scheduler at the submit site.
73	NUM_ROLLOUTS_B="${NUM_ROLLOUTS_B:-${NUM_ROLLOUTS}}"
74	# Rollouts at the start of Stage B in which only the critic trains. This is the
75	# warmup window the incident was reported against, and the window in which the
76	# value loss is measured.
77	NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS="${NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS:-${NUM_ROLLOUTS_B}}"
78	
79	# Episodes per rollout = ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE x N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT; optimizer
80	# steps per rollout = that, divided by GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE.
81	ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE="${ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE:-8}"
82	N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT="${N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT:-2}"
83	GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE="${GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE:-8}"
84	LR="${LR:-1e-6}"
85	
86	# How many leading critic optimizer steps the reported warmup statistics cover.
87	# Derived rather than guessed, because once Stage B runs past the critic-only
88	# phase the two are no longer the same thing: averaging the value loss over all
89	# of a 30-rollout Stage B measures mostly a critic that has already been
90	# trained, which is not what "warmup value loss" names and not what the
91	# incident was about.
92	CRITIC_WARMUP_STEPS=$(( NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS * ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE * N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT / GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE ))
93	[ "${CRITIC_WARMUP_STEPS}" -gt 0 ] || CRITIC_WARMUP_STEPS=1
94	
95	# Held-out evaluation during Stage B. 0 disables it, which is what the short
96	# value-loss-only reproduction wants.
97	#
98	# val and test get different sample budgets. val only has to say *when* the
99	# curve flattens, so 2 samples x 150 tasks is enough; test carries the
100	# end-to-end claim and is compared per task, where the useful quantity is each
101	# task's success *rate*, which 1 or 2 samples cannot resolve at all.
102	EVAL_INTERVAL="${EVAL_INTERVAL:-0}"
103	N_EVAL_SAMPLES="${N_EVAL_SAMPLES:-2}"
104	N_EVAL_SAMPLES_TEST="${N_EVAL_SAMPLES_TEST:-4}"
105	
106	# How often Stage B checkpoints. Trained to convergence, Stage B runs for well
107	# over an hour, which on a shared host is long enough to be interrupted -- two
108	# runs of this case were killed from outside the container mid-training, once
109	# with SIGTERM and once with SIGKILL. So Stage B saves as it goes and a second
110	# invocation picks up where the first stopped, instead of starting the hour
111	# again. 0 disables it, which is what the short value-loss-only reproduction
112	# wants: it writes nothing and measures only the reload.
113	STAGE_B_SAVE_INTERVAL="${STAGE_B_SAVE_INTERVAL:-0}"
114	
115	RAY_PORT="${RAY_PORT:-6479}"
116	DASH_PORT="${DASH_PORT:-8277}"
117	RAY_TMP="${RAY_TMP:-/tmp/ray_ppo}"
118	
119	mkdir -p "${OUT_DIR}" "${CKPT_ROOT}" "${ET_SCRATCH}"
120	
121	# --------------------------------------------------------- 0. the slime source
122	# The full slime source tree is bundled in the workspace (${SLIME_HOME}) and is
123	# put ahead of the image's editable install on PYTHONPATH below, so it is the
124	# copy that trains -- there is nothing to install first.
125	test -f "${SLIME_HOME}/train.py" || {
126	    echo "FATAL: bundled slime source not found at ${SLIME_HOME}" >&2
127	    exit 1
128	}
129	
130	# ------------------------------------------------------- 1. the prompt dataset
131	# prepare.sh ships the already-built dataset (transpiled + validated + split) at
132	# ${WS}/et_prompts. Seed ET_DATA_ROOT from it so the build below is skipped: the
133	# 2492->1489 admission is environment-fixed and reproducible, so there is no need
134	# to re-run the ~40min transpile+validate pass (and ET_SRC is never read). The
135	# copy lands in a writable, exec-capable dir (ET_DATA_ROOT defaults to /tmp) --
136	# the bundled tree under /workspace may be a root-owned bind mount. If the
137	# prebuilt payload is absent, fall through to building from ET_SRC as before.
138	if [ ! -s "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals.jsonl" ] && [ -s "${WS}/et_prompts/endless_terminals.jsonl" ]; then
139	    echo "=== seeding ET_DATA_ROOT from prebuilt ${WS}/et_prompts (skipping transpile+validate) ==="
140	    mkdir -p "${ET_DATA_ROOT}"
141	    cp -a "${WS}/et_prompts/." "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/"
142	fi
143	if [ ! -s "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals.jsonl" ]; then
144	    echo "=== transpiling + validating the Endless Terminals tasks ==="
145	    (cd "${WS}" && python3 -m et.build_dataset --src "${ET_SRC}" --out "${ET_DATA_ROOT}") \
146	        2>&1 | tee "${OUT_DIR}/build_dataset.log"
147	fi
148	# Deliberately not silenced. A report that is quietly 0 bytes is worse than one
149	# that is loudly absent: it reads as "every task was rejected" to anyone who
150	# opens it later, and that has happened here more than once.
151	copy_artifact() {   # copy_artifact <src>
152	    local src="$1" dst="${OUT_DIR}/$(basename "$1")"
153	    if ! cp -f "${src}" "${dst}"; then
154	        echo "WARNING: could not copy ${src} into ${OUT_DIR}" >&2
155	    elif [ ! -s "${dst}" ] && [ -s "${src}" ]; then
156	        echo "WARNING: ${dst} came out empty although ${src} is not" >&2
157	    fi
158	}
159	copy_artifact "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/validation_report.json"
160	N_PROMPTS="$(wc -l < "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals.jsonl")"
161	echo "prompt set: ${N_PROMPTS} validated Endless Terminals tasks"
162	if [ "${N_PROMPTS}" -lt 4 ]; then
163	    echo "FATAL: too few tasks survived validation to train on." >&2
164	    exit 1
165	fi
166	
167	# Train on one part of the task set and measure on another. The split is a pure
168	# function of the admitted list and a fixed seed, so every run trains and is
169	# scored on exactly the same tasks -- otherwise a comparison between runs is
170	# partly measuring which tasks each one happened to get.
171	if [ ! -s "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals_train.jsonl" ]; then
172	    (cd "${WS}" && python3 -m et.make_splits --prompts "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals.jsonl")
173	fi
174	copy_artifact "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/splits.json"
175	TRAIN_SPLIT="${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals_train.jsonl"
176	VAL_SPLIT="${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals_val.jsonl"
177	TEST_SPLIT="${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals_test.jsonl"
178	printf 'splits: train %s / val %s / test %s\n' \
179	    "$(wc -l < "${TRAIN_SPLIT}")" "$(wc -l < "${VAL_SPLIT}")" "$(wc -l < "${TEST_SPLIT}")"
180	
181	# ------------------------------------------------------------- 2. shared args
182	source "${WS}/configs/model_args.sh"
183	
184	ROLLOUT_ARGS=(
185	    --prompt-data "${TRAIN_SPLIT}"
186	    --input-key prompt
187	    --label-key label
188	    --rollout-shuffle
189	    --rollout-batch-size "${ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE}"
190	    --n-samples-per-prompt "${N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT}"
191	    --rollout-max-response-len 2048
192	    --rollout-temperature 1.0
193	    --global-batch-size "${GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE}"
194	    --balance-data
195	    # The multi-turn terminal loop and its pytest-based episode reward.
196	    --custom-generate-function-path et.rollout.generate
197	    --custom-rm-path et.rollout.reward_func
198	)
199	
200	PPO_ARGS=(
201	    --advantage-estimator ppo   # -> args.use_critic
202	    --gamma 1.0
203	    --lambd 1.0
204	    --eps-clip 0.2
205	    --value-clip 0.2
206	    --kl-coef 0.0               # no reference model, hence no --ref-load and
207	    --entropy-coef 0.0          # no HF -> torch_dist conversion step
208	)
209	
210	PERF_ARGS=(
211	    --tensor-model-parallel-size "${TP_SIZE}"
212	    --pipeline-model-parallel-size 1
213	    --context-parallel-size 1
214	    --recompute-granularity full
215	    --recompute-method uniform
216	    --recompute-num-layers 1
217	    --use-dynamic-batch-size
218	    --max-tokens-per-gpu 8192
219	)
220	# Sequence parallelism splits the activations of the non-tensor-parallel ops
221	# across the TP group, so it is only defined for TP > 1; Megatron asserts on it.
222	# Spelled as an `if` rather than `[ ... ] && ...`: the latter evaluates to the
223	# test's status, which under `set -e` ends the script whenever TP_SIZE is 1.
224	if [ "${TP_SIZE}" -gt 1 ]; then
225	    PERF_ARGS+=(--sequence-parallel)
226	fi
227	
228	OPTIMIZER_ARGS=(
229	    --optimizer adam
230	    --lr "${LR}"
231	    --lr-decay-style constant
232	    --weight-decay 0.0
233	    --adam-beta1 0.9
234	    --adam-beta2 0.95
235	)
236	
237	SGLANG_ARGS=(
238	    --rollout-num-gpus-per-engine "${NUM_GPUS}"
239	    # Colocated: this fraction is what SGLang keeps, and Megatron's weights,
240	    # gradients and Adam state have to fit in the rest. At TP 2 each GPU carries
241	    # half of each role, so 0.55 leaves enough; drop it when NUM_GPUS is 1 and
242	    # one device has to hold both roles whole.
243	    --sglang-mem-fraction-static "${SGLANG_MEM_FRACTION}"
244	)
245	
246	# Held-out scoring, used only by Stage B. slime evaluates once before the first
247	# rollout and then every EVAL_INTERVAL rollouts, which gives both the starting
248	# pass rate and the curve that says whether training has converged.
249	#
250	# val and test are evaluated at the same points on purpose. The convergence
251	# *decision* is read off val; test is reported only at the final point, and
252	# evaluating it throughout costs generation but no statistical validity, since
253	# nothing about the run is conditioned on it.
254	#
255	# Spelled as an --eval-config YAML rather than --eval-prompt-data because the
256	# two splits need different sample counts, and --n-samples-per-eval-prompt is
257	# one global number. Everything the YAML leaves out still falls back to the
258	# command line (eval_config.py:10 DATASET_RUNTIME_SPECS), so temperature,
259	# response length and the prompt/label keys are set once, below and above.
260	EVAL_ARGS=()
261	if [ "${EVAL_INTERVAL}" -gt 0 ]; then
262	    cat > "${OUT_DIR}/eval_datasets.yaml" <<YAML
263	eval:
264	  datasets:
265	    - name: et_val
266	      path: ${VAL_SPLIT}
267	      n_samples_per_eval_prompt: ${N_EVAL_SAMPLES}
268	    - name: et_test
269	      path: ${TEST_SPLIT}
270	      n_samples_per_eval_prompt: ${N_EVAL_SAMPLES_TEST}
271	YAML
272	    EVAL_ARGS=(
273	        --eval-interval "${EVAL_INTERVAL}"
274	        --eval-config "${OUT_DIR}/eval_datasets.yaml"
275	        --eval-max-response-len 2048
276	        --eval-temperature 1.0
277	        --log-passrate
278	        --custom-eval-rollout-log-function-path et.eval_log.log_eval_rollout_data
279	    )
280	fi
281	
282	MISC_ARGS=(
283	    --attention-dropout 0.0
284	    --hidden-dropout 0.0
285	    --accumulate-allreduce-grads-in-fp32
286	    --attention-softmax-in-fp32
287	    --attention-backend flash
288	    --seed 1234
289	)
290	
291	# --------------------------------------------------------- 3. per-role configs
292	# Actor and critic share `args.save` by default, which would make them clobber
293	# each other's checkpoints (the critic's output layer is [1, hidden_size], the
294	# actor's is [vocab, hidden_size]), so each role gets its own directory.
295	cat > "${OUT_DIR}/megatron_roles_stage_a.yaml" <<YAML
296	# Stage A: "the previous training run". Both roles start from the base model.
297	megatron:
298	  - name: stage-a-actor
299	    role: actor
300	    overrides:
301	      load: ${MODEL_DIR}
302	      save: ${CKPT_ROOT}/actor
303	  - name: stage-a-critic
304	    role: critic
305	    overrides:
306	      load: ${MODEL_DIR}
307	      save: ${CKPT_ROOT}/critic
308	YAML
309	
310	# Stage B can be entered two ways, and they are not the same event.
311	#
312	#   fresh   -- "the model was reloaded". The actor resumes from Stage A's
313	#              Megatron checkpoint; the critic's backbone comes from the base
314	#              model.
315	#
316	#   resume  -- an interrupted Stage B being continued. Both roles load Stage B's
317	#              own checkpoints, optimizer state included, and the run continues
318	#              from the last saved rollout. The first attempt's log is kept,
319	#              not overwritten (see the STAGE_B_LOG choice below).
320	STAGE_B_RESUME=0
321	if [ -f "${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_actor/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt" ] \
322	   && [ -f "${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_critic/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt" ]; then
323	    STAGE_B_RESUME=1
324	fi
325	
326	if [ "${STAGE_B_RESUME}" = "1" ]; then
327	    STAGE_B_ACTOR_LOAD="${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_actor"
328	    STAGE_B_CRITIC_LOAD="${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_critic"
329	else
330	    STAGE_B_ACTOR_LOAD="${CKPT_ROOT}/actor"
331	    STAGE_B_CRITIC_LOAD="${MODEL_DIR}"
332	fi
333	
334	cat > "${OUT_DIR}/megatron_roles_stage_b.yaml" <<YAML
335	# Stage B, $([ "${STAGE_B_RESUME}" = "1" ] && echo "resumed from its own checkpoints" || echo "entered fresh after a reload").
336	megatron:
337	  - name: stage-b-actor
338	    role: actor
339	    overrides:
340	      load: ${STAGE_B_ACTOR_LOAD}
341	      save: ${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_actor
342	  - name: stage-b-critic
343	    role: critic
344	    overrides:
345	      load: ${STAGE_B_CRITIC_LOAD}
346	      save: ${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_critic
347	YAML
348	
349	# ------------------------------------------------------------------- 4. ray
350	export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
351	
352	ray start --head \
353	    --node-ip-address 127.0.0.1 \
354	    --port "${RAY_PORT}" \
355	    --num-gpus "${NUM_GPUS}" \
356	    --disable-usage-stats \
357	    --dashboard-host 127.0.0.1 \
358	    --dashboard-port "${DASH_PORT}" \
359	    --temp-dir "${RAY_TMP}"
360	trap 'ray stop --force >/dev/null 2>&1 || true' EXIT
361	
362	# `|| true` on the whole pipeline, not decoration: under `pipefail` a `grep`
363	# that matches nothing fails the pipeline, so on a host with no NVLink -- or in
364	# a container holding a single GPU, where the topology matrix has no peer links
365	# to report -- `set -e` would kill the script here. Silently: this sits between
366	# `ray start` and the first echo of Stage A, so the log just stops.
367	NVLINK_COUNT="$(nvidia-smi topo -m 2>/dev/null | grep -o 'NV[0-9][0-9]*' | wc -l || true)"
368	HAS_NVLINK=0
369	[ "${NVLINK_COUNT:-0}" -gt 0 ] && HAS_NVLINK=1
370	
371	RUNTIME_ENV_JSON="{
372	  \"env_vars\": {
373	    \"PYTHONPATH\": \"/root/Megatron-LM/:${SLIME_HOME}:${WS}\",
374	    \"CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS\": \"1\",
375	    \"NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE\": \"${HAS_NVLINK}\",
376	    \"ET_DATA_ROOT\": \"${ET_DATA_ROOT}\",
377	    \"ET_EVAL_DUMP_DIR\": \"${OUT_DIR}/eval_episodes\",
378	    \"ET_SCRATCH\": \"${ET_SCRATCH}\",
379	    \"ET_MAX_TURNS\": \"${ET_MAX_TURNS}\",
380	    \"ET_MAX_NEW_TOKENS\": \"${ET_MAX_NEW_TOKENS}\",
381	    \"ET_CMD_TIMEOUT\": \"${ET_CMD_TIMEOUT}\",
382	    \"ET_MAX_OBS_CHARS\": \"${ET_MAX_OBS_CHARS}\"
383	  }
384	}"
385	
386	submit() {   # submit <log-file> <extra args...>
387	    local log="$1"; shift
388	    # The entrypoint is an absolute path on purpose: `ray job submit` does not
389	    # run it in this shell's directory but in the cwd of the Ray head (here
390	    # /workspace, since no `working_dir` is uploaded), so a bare `train.py`
391	    # would not be found. Running ${SLIME_HOME}/train.py puts the bundled slime
392	    # tree on the driver's sys.path[0]; the ray workers get it from ${SLIME_HOME}
393	    # on PYTHONPATH (RUNTIME_ENV_JSON above), ahead of the image's install.
394	    ray job submit \
395	        --address "http://127.0.0.1:${DASH_PORT}" \
396	        --runtime-env-json "${RUNTIME_ENV_JSON}" \
397	        -- python3 "${SLIME_HOME}/train.py" \
398	        --actor-num-nodes 1 \
399	        --actor-num-gpus-per-node "${NUM_GPUS}" \
400	        --colocate \
401	        --hf-checkpoint "${MODEL_DIR}" \
402	        "${MODEL_ARGS[@]}" \
403	        "${ROLLOUT_ARGS[@]}" \
404	        "${PPO_ARGS[@]}" \
405	        "${PERF_ARGS[@]}" \
406	        "${OPTIMIZER_ARGS[@]}" \
407	        "${SGLANG_ARGS[@]}" \
408	        "${MISC_ARGS[@]}" \
409	        "$@" 2>&1 | tee "${log}"
410	}
411	
412	# Ray forwards actor stdout to the job driver, but keep the raw worker logs too:
413	# the per-step metrics are emitted by the train actors, not by the driver.
414	collect_worker_logs() {   # collect_worker_logs <tag>
415	    # Two statements, not one: `local a=.. b=..` expands every word before it
416	    # assigns any of them, so referring to ${tag} on the same line would read

426	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 5. stage A

428	echo "############ Stage A: the previous training run ############"

430	# re-running the long Stage B after an interruption. Off by default, and
431	# refuses to be silently wrong: with no checkpoint there, Stage A runs anyway.

438	        --save "${CKPT_ROOT}/actor" \
439	        --save-interval 1 \
440	        --num-rollout "${NUM_ROLLOUTS}" \
441	        --num-critic-only-steps 0

443	fi

445	echo

449	    echo "FATAL: Stage A did not produce a resumable Megatron checkpoint." >&2

452

455	echo "############ Stage B: reload, then critic warmup ############"

457	# asserts the two go together. With STAGE_B_SAVE_INTERVAL=0 it is set far
458	# larger than the number of rollouts Stage B takes, so Stage B measures the

468	# happens to start from Stage A's weights, not a resumption of Stage A.

470	    --megatron-config-path "${OUT_DIR}/megatron_roles_stage_b.yaml"
471	    --load "${STAGE_B_ACTOR_LOAD}"
472	    --save "${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_actor"
473	    --save-interval "$([ "${STAGE_B_SAVE_INTERVAL}" -gt 0 ] && echo "${STAGE_B_SAVE_INTERVAL}" || echo 1000)"
474	    --override-opt-param-scheduler
475	    --num-rollout "${NUM_ROLLOUTS_B}"
476	    --num-critic-only-steps "${NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS}"
477	)
478	
479	STAGE_B_LOG="${OUT_DIR}/stage_b.log"

481	    # The first attempt's log holds the warmup window that the value-loss
482	    # verdict is read from, so a resume must not overwrite it.

484	    while [ -e "${OUT_DIR}/stage_b_resume_${n}.log" ]; do n=$((n + 1)); done
485	    STAGE_B_LOG="${OUT_DIR}/stage_b_resume_${n}.log"
486	    echo "resuming Stage B from ${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_{actor,critic}" \
487	         "(iteration $(cat "${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_critic/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt")); log -> ${STAGE_B_LOG}"
488	    # --start-rollout-id is deliberately NOT passed here. slime takes the start

491	    # so omitting it resumes at exactly the rollout after the last saved one.
492	else
493	    # --start-rollout-id 0 pins the warmup window: without it the start id is
494	    # inferred from whichever checkpoint the critic loaded, and on a fresh
495	    # Stage B the critic loads a plain HF directory (iteration 0).
496	    STAGE_B_ARGS+=(--start-rollout-id 0)
497	fi
498	
499	submit "${STAGE_B_LOG}" "${STAGE_B_ARGS[@]}" "${EVAL_ARGS[@]+"${EVAL_ARGS[@]}"}"
500	collect_worker_logs stage_b

502	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 7. verdict
503	echo
504	echo "############ critic warmup value loss ############"
505	python3 "${WS}/tools/parse_value_loss.py" \
506	    "${OUT_DIR}/stage_b.log" \
507	    --warmup-steps "${CRITIC_WARMUP_STEPS}" \
508	    --out "${OUT_DIR}/stage_b_value_loss.json"
509	
510	python3 "${WS}/tools/parse_value_loss.py" \
511	    "${OUT_DIR}/stage_a.log" \
512	    --out "${OUT_DIR}/stage_a_value_loss.json" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
513	
514	echo
515	echo "artifacts in ${OUT_DIR}:"
516	ls -1 "${OUT_DIR}"
