608	def chunked_discounted_returns(
609	    rewards: torch.Tensor,
610	    discount: float,
611	    chunk_size: int = 128,
612	) -> torch.Tensor:
613	    """
614	    Compute discounted returns using a parallel scan within fixed-size chunks.
615	
616	    This reduces the sequential dependency length from O(T) to O(T / chunk_size),
617	    while keeping chunk computations fully parallelizable (O(C^2) per chunk).
618	
619	    Args:
620	        rewards (Tensor): [B, T] reward sequence.
621	        discount (float): Discount factor applied at each step.
622	        chunk_size (int): sequence chunk length for parallel scan.
623	
624	    Returns:
625	        Tensor: [B, T] discounted returns.
626	    """
627	    assert rewards.ndim == 2
628	    B, T = rewards.shape
629	
630	    device = rewards.device
631	    dtype = rewards.dtype
632	
633	    # Reformulate the backward recurrence as a forward scan on the reversed
634	    # sequence: S[i] = rewards[i] + discount * S[i - 1].
635	    rewards_rev = torch.flip(rewards, dims=[1])
636	
637	    if T % chunk_size != 0:
638	        pad = chunk_size - (T % chunk_size)
639	        rewards_rev = F.pad(rewards_rev, (0, pad))
640	    else:
641	        pad = 0
642	
643	    B, T_pad = rewards_rev.shape
644	    n_chunks = T_pad // chunk_size
645	    rewards_chunks = rewards_rev.view(B, n_chunks, chunk_size)
646	
647	    idx = torch.arange(chunk_size, device=device)
648	    row = idx[:, None]
649	    col = idx[None, :]
650	    diff = col - row
651	
652	    M = torch.zeros(chunk_size, chunk_size, device=device, dtype=dtype)
653	    mask = diff >= 0
654	
655	    if discount == 0.0:
656	        M[mask & (diff == 0)] = 1.0
657	    else:
658	        M[mask] = discount ** diff[mask].to(dtype)
659	
660	    if discount == 0.0:
661	        pow_vec = torch.zeros(chunk_size, device=device, dtype=dtype)
662	    else:
663	        pow_vec = discount ** torch.arange(1, chunk_size + 1, device=device, dtype=dtype)
664	
665	    rewards_flat = rewards_chunks.reshape(B * n_chunks, chunk_size)
666	    S_local_flat = rewards_flat @ M
667	    S_local_chunks = S_local_flat.view(B, n_chunks, chunk_size)
668	
669	    lengths = [chunk_size] * n_chunks
670	    if pad > 0:
671	        lengths[-1] = chunk_size - pad
672	
673	    S_rev = rewards_rev.new_zeros(B, T_pad)
674	    s_prev = torch.zeros(B, device=device, dtype=dtype)
675	
676	    for c in range(n_chunks):
677	        Lc = lengths[c]
678	        start = c * chunk_size
679	        end = start + Lc
680	
681	        S_local = S_local_chunks[:, c, :Lc]
682	        S_global = S_local + s_prev.unsqueeze(1) * pow_vec[:Lc]
683	
684	        S_rev[:, start:end] = S_global
685	        s_prev = S_global[:, -1]
686	
687	    if pad > 0:
688	        S_rev = S_rev[:, :T]
689	
690	    return torch.flip(S_rev, dims=[1])
691	
692	
693	def chunked_gae(
694	    rewards: torch.Tensor,
695	    values: torch.Tensor,
696	    gamma: float,
697	    lambd: float,
698	    chunk_size: int = 128,
699	):
700	    """Compute Generalized Advantage Estimation using a chunked scan."""
701	    assert rewards.ndim == 2 and values.ndim == 2
702	    B, T = rewards.shape
703	    assert values.shape == (B, T)
704	
705	    next_values = torch.cat(
706	        [values[:, 1:], torch.zeros(B, 1, device=values.device, dtype=values.dtype)],
707	        dim=1,
708	    )
709	    deltas = rewards + gamma * next_values - values
710	    advantages = chunked_discounted_returns(deltas, gamma * lambd, chunk_size)
711	    returns = advantages + values
712	
713	    return advantages, returns
714	
715	
716	def calculate_log_probs_and_entropy(
717	    logits,
718	    tokens,
719	    tp_group,
720	    with_entropy: bool = False,
721	    chunk_size: int = -1,
722	    log_prob_keep_mask=None,
723	    with_entropy_grad: bool = True,
724	):
725	    logits = logits.contiguous()
726	    entropy = None
727	    if logits.size(0) != 0:
728	        if chunk_size > 0:
729	            num_chunks = (logits.size(0) - 1) // chunk_size + 1
730	            logits_chunks = logits.chunk(num_chunks, dim=0)
731	            tokens_chunks = tokens.chunk(num_chunks, dim=0)
732	            mask_chunks = (
733	                log_prob_keep_mask.chunk(num_chunks, dim=0) if log_prob_keep_mask is not None else [None] * num_chunks
734	            )
735	
736	            log_probs = []
737	            entropy_chunks = []
738	            for tokens_chunk, logits_chunk, mask_chunk in zip(tokens_chunks, logits_chunks, mask_chunks, strict=True):
739	                log_prob, entropy_chunk = _calculate_log_probs_and_entropy_chunk(
740	                    logits_chunk,
741	                    tokens_chunk,
742	                    tp_group,
743	                    with_entropy=with_entropy,
744	                    with_entropy_grad=with_entropy_grad,
745	                    log_prob_keep_mask=mask_chunk,
746	                )
747	                log_probs.append(log_prob)
748	                if entropy_chunk is not None:
749	                    entropy_chunks.append(entropy_chunk)
750	            log_prob = torch.cat(log_probs, dim=0)
751	            if entropy_chunks:
752	                entropy = torch.cat(entropy_chunks, dim=0)
753	        else:
754	            log_prob, entropy = _calculate_log_probs_and_entropy_chunk(
755	                logits,
756	                tokens,
757	                tp_group,
758	                with_entropy=with_entropy,

760	                log_prob_keep_mask=log_prob_keep_mask,
761	            )
762	    else:

764	        if with_entropy:
765	            entropy = logits.new_zeros((0,))
766	
767	    return log_prob, entropy

#!/bin/bash
#
# Multi-Turn PPO on Endless Terminals with Qwen3-1.7B, on slime v0.3.2.
#
# The run has two stages:
#
#   Stage A -- "the previous training run".  A real PPO rollout (actor + critic)
#              starting from the base HF model, which saves a Megatron
#              checkpoint for both roles.
#
#   Stage B -- "the model was reloaded".  The actor genuinely resumes from
#              Stage A's Megatron checkpoint (weights *and* optimizer state).
#              The critic's backbone is reloaded from the base model.  Stage B
#              opens with NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS critic-only rollouts (the
#              warmup window) and then trains actor and critic jointly.
#
# The full slime source tree is bundled in the workspace (slime/) and is the
# copy that runs -- this script puts it ahead of the image's install on
# PYTHONPATH, so editing slime/ here is what takes effect, with nothing to
# install first.
#
# NOTE ON A SHARED HOST: unlike slime's own example scripts this one never runs
# `pkill -9 ray / pkill -9 python / ray stop --force` on entry.  It is meant to
# run inside its own container, and it brings up a private Ray head on a
# non-default port with a private temp dir.

set -euo pipefail

WS="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" &>/dev/null && pwd)"

# The container runs as root while /workspace is a bind mount owned by whoever
# checked the case out, so any .pyc written here lands root-owned in their tree
# -- and `importlib` copies the *source* file's mode onto the .pyc, so a 600
# source yields a 600 root-owned file that even the owner cannot read, and
# `cp -r` of the case fails. Nothing here benefits from a bytecode cache.
export PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1

MODEL_DIR="${MODEL_DIR:-${WS}/Qwen3-1.7B}"
ET_SRC="${ET_SRC:-${WS}/endless-terminals}"
SLIME_HOME="${SLIME_HOME:-${WS}/slime}"
OUT_DIR="${OUT_DIR:-${WS}/outputs}"
CKPT_ROOT="${CKPT_ROOT:-/ckpt}"

# Endless Terminals sandbox knobs; also forwarded into the Ray workers, which
# read them at import time in et/rollout.py.
#
# These must NOT live under /dev/shm: it is mounted noexec in the training
# image, and many tasks' verifiers assert os.access(path, os.X_OK), which is
# False there even at mode 755.
export ET_DATA_ROOT="${ET_DATA_ROOT:-/tmp/et_prompts}"
export ET_SCRATCH="${ET_SCRATCH:-/tmp/et_episodes}"
export ET_MAX_TURNS="${ET_MAX_TURNS:-6}"
export ET_MAX_NEW_TOKENS="${ET_MAX_NEW_TOKENS:-384}"
export ET_CMD_TIMEOUT="${ET_CMD_TIMEOUT:-20}"
export ET_MAX_OBS_CHARS="${ET_MAX_OBS_CHARS:-1200}"

NUM_GPUS="${NUM_GPUS:-2}"
TP_SIZE="${TP_SIZE:-2}"
SGLANG_MEM_FRACTION="${SGLANG_MEM_FRACTION:-0.55}"
# Rollouts per stage. Both stages use the same count on purpose, and must:
# slime derives `train_iters` from `--num-rollout` (model.py:203) and Megatron
# stores the resulting LR/weight-decay horizons inside the checkpoint, then
# asserts on reload that they match the ones the new arguments imply
# ("total number of iterations do not match"). Giving Stage B a different
# rollout count than Stage A would trip that assert before any training runs.
# In Stage A these rollouts are ordinary PPO; Stage B opens with
# NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS critic-only rollouts -- the warmup window -- and then
# trains actor and critic jointly for the rest.
NUM_ROLLOUTS="${NUM_ROLLOUTS:-2}"
# Stage B is the long one: critic warmup followed by joint PPO, trained until
# the validation pass rate stops moving. It no longer has to match Stage A's
# rollout count -- see --override-opt-param-scheduler at the submit site.
NUM_ROLLOUTS_B="${NUM_ROLLOUTS_B:-${NUM_ROLLOUTS}}"
# Rollouts at the start of Stage B in which only the critic trains. This is the
# warmup window the incident was reported against, and the window in which the
# value loss is measured.
NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS="${NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS:-${NUM_ROLLOUTS_B}}"

# Episodes per rollout = ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE x N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT; optimizer
# steps per rollout = that, divided by GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE.
ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE="${ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE:-8}"
N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT="${N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT:-2}"
GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE="${GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE:-8}"
LR="${LR:-1e-6}"

# How many leading critic optimizer steps the reported warmup statistics cover.
# Derived rather than guessed, because once Stage B runs past the critic-only
# phase the two are no longer the same thing: averaging the value loss over all
# of a 30-rollout Stage B measures mostly a critic that has already been
# trained, which is not what "warmup value loss" names and not what the
# incident was about.
CRITIC_WARMUP_STEPS=$(( NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS * ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE * N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT / GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE ))
[ "${CRITIC_WARMUP_STEPS}" -gt 0 ] || CRITIC_WARMUP_STEPS=1

# value-loss-only reproduction wants.
#
# val and test get different sample budgets. val only has to say *when* the
# curve flattens, so 2 samples x 150 tasks is enough; test carries the
# end-to-end claim and is compared per task, where the useful quantity is each

# How often Stage B checkpoints. Trained to convergence, Stage B runs for well
# over an hour, which on a shared host is long enough to be interrupted -- two
# runs of this case were killed from outside the container mid-training, once
# with SIGTERM and once with SIGKILL. So Stage B saves as it goes and a second
# invocation picks up where the first stopped, instead of starting the hour

# 2492->1489 admission is environment-fixed and reproducible, so there is no need
# to re-run the ~40min transpile+validate pass (and ET_SRC is never read). The
# copy lands in a writable, exec-capable dir (ET_DATA_ROOT defaults to /tmp) --
# the bundled tree under /workspace may be a root-owned bind mount. If the
# prebuilt payload is absent, fall through to building from ET_SRC as before.
if [ ! -s "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals.jsonl" ] && [ -s "${WS}/et_prompts/endless_terminals.jsonl" ]; then

    mkdir -p "${ET_DATA_ROOT}"
    cp -a "${WS}/et_prompts/." "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/"
fi
if [ ! -s "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals.jsonl" ]; then
    echo "=== transpiling + validating the Endless Terminals tasks ==="
    (cd "${WS}" && python3 -m et.build_dataset --src "${ET_SRC}" --out "${ET_DATA_ROOT}") \
        2>&1 | tee "${OUT_DIR}/build_dataset.log"
fi
# Deliberately not silenced. A report that is quietly 0 bytes is worse than one
# that is loudly absent: it reads as "every task was rejected" to anyone who

# across the TP group, so it is only defined for TP > 1; Megatron asserts on it.

# slime derives `train_iters` from --num-rollout (model.py:203) and Megatron

STAGE_B_ARGS=(
    --megatron-config-path "${OUT_DIR}/megatron_roles_stage_b.yaml"

19	class FlattenedTensorBucket:
20	    """
21	    A bucket that flattens multiple tensors into a single tensor for efficient processing
22	    while preserving all metadata needed for reconstruction.
23	    """
24	
25	    # This field is solely for users of to check whether the class supports this feature
26	    supports_multi_dtypes = True
27	
28	    def __init__(
29	        self,
30	        named_tensors: List[Tuple[str, torch.Tensor]] = None,
31	        flattened_tensor: torch.Tensor = None,
32	        metadata: List[FlattenedTensorMetadata] = None,
33	    ):
34	        """
35	        Initialize a tensor bucket from a list of named tensors OR from pre-flattened data.
36	        Args:
37	            named_tensors: List of (name, tensor) tuples (for creating new bucket)
38	            flattened_tensor: Pre-flattened tensor (for reconstruction)
39	            metadata: Pre-computed metadata (for reconstruction)
40	        """
41	        if named_tensors is not None:
42	            # Create bucket from named tensors
43	            self.metadata: List[FlattenedTensorMetadata] = [None] * len(named_tensors)
44	            self.flattened_tensor: torch.Tensor = None
45	
46	            if not named_tensors:
47	                raise ValueError("Cannot create empty tensor bucket")
48	
49	            # Collect metadata and flatten tensors
50	            current_idx = 0
51	            flattened_tensors: List[torch.Tensor] = [None] * len(named_tensors)
52	
53	            for i, (name, tensor) in enumerate(named_tensors):
54	                flattened = tensor.flatten().view(torch.uint8)
55	                flattened_tensors[i] = flattened
56	
57	                # Store metadata
58	
59	                numel = flattened.numel()
60	                metadata_obj = FlattenedTensorMetadata(
61	                    name=name,
62	                    shape=tensor.shape,
63	                    dtype=tensor.dtype,
64	                    start_idx=current_idx,
65	                    end_idx=current_idx + numel,
66	                    numel=numel,
67	                )
68	                self.metadata[i] = metadata_obj
69	                current_idx += numel
70	
71	            # Concatenate all flattened tensors
72	            self.flattened_tensor = torch.cat(flattened_tensors, dim=0)
73	        else:
74	            # Initialize from pre-flattened data
75	            if flattened_tensor is None or metadata is None:
76	                raise ValueError(
77	                    "Must provide either named_tensors or both flattened_tensor and metadata"
78	                )
79	            self.flattened_tensor = flattened_tensor
80	            self.metadata = metadata
81	
82	    def get_flattened_tensor(self) -> torch.Tensor:
83	        """Get the flattened tensor containing all bucket tensors"""
84	        return self.flattened_tensor
85	
86	    def get_metadata(self) -> List[FlattenedTensorMetadata]:
87	        """Get metadata for all tensors in the bucket"""
88	        return self.metadata
89	
90	    def reconstruct_tensors(self) -> List[Tuple[str, torch.Tensor]]:
91	        """
92	        Reconstruct original tensors from flattened tensor with optimized performance.
93	        Uses memory-efficient operations to minimize allocations and copies.
94	        """
95	        # preallocate the result list
96	        reconstructed = [None] * len(self.metadata)
97	
98	        for i, meta in enumerate(self.metadata):
99	            tensor = (
100	                self.flattened_tensor[meta.start_idx : meta.end_idx]
101	                .view(meta.dtype)
102	                .reshape(meta.shape)
103	            )
104	
105	            reconstructed[i] = (meta.name, tensor)
106	
107	        return reconstructed

309	        """
310	        if self.custom_convert_samples_to_train_data_func is not None:
311	            return self.custom_convert_samples_to_train_data_func(self.args, samples)
312	
313	        raw_rewards, rewards = self._post_process_rewards(samples)
314	
315	        assert len(raw_rewards) == len(samples)
316	        assert len(rewards) == len(samples)
317	
318	        rollout_ids = [sample.rollout_id for sample in samples]
319	        existed_rollout_id_values = set(rid for rid in rollout_ids if rid is not None)
320	        tmp_id = 0
321	        for i in range(len(rollout_ids)):
322	            if rollout_ids[i] is None:
323	                while tmp_id in existed_rollout_id_values:
324	                    tmp_id += 1
325	                rollout_ids[i] = tmp_id
326	                existed_rollout_id_values.add(tmp_id)
327	
328	        train_data = {
329	            "tokens": [sample.tokens for sample in samples],
330	            "response_lengths": [sample.response_length for sample in samples],
331	            # some reward model, e.g. remote rm, may return multiple rewards,
332	            # we could use key to select the reward.
333	            "rewards": rewards,
334	            "raw_reward": raw_rewards,
335	            "truncated": [1 if sample.status == Sample.Status.TRUNCATED else 0 for sample in samples],
336	            "sample_indices": [sample.index for sample in samples],
337	            "rollout_ids": rollout_ids,
338	        }
339	
340	        # loss mask
341	        # TODO: compress the loss mask
342	        loss_masks = []
343	        for sample in samples:
344	            # always instantiate loss_mask if not provided
345	            if sample.loss_mask is None:
346	                sample.loss_mask = [1] * sample.response_length
347	
348	            assert (
349	                len(sample.loss_mask) == sample.response_length
350	            ), f"loss mask length {len(sample.loss_mask)} != response length {sample.response_length}"
351	            if sample.remove_sample:
352	                sample.loss_mask = [0] * sample.response_length
353	            loss_masks.append(sample.loss_mask)
354	        train_data["loss_masks"] = loss_masks
355	
356	        # Per-rollout aggregate, precomputed at the step level (where we can
357	        # see every sample of every rollout) and broadcast per-sample so the
358	        # per-mb loss reducer uses the correct whole-rollout denominator even
359	        # when a rollout's samples land in different micro-batches (first-fit
360	        # packing can split a rollout across mbs):
361	        #
362	        #   ``rollout_mask_sums[i]`` — sum of loss-mask totals over every
363	        #   sample in sample i's rollout. Used as the reducer's denominator
364	        #   so summing partial contributions across mbs yields one
365	        #   token-weighted mean per rollout.
366	        rollout_id_list = train_data["rollout_ids"]
367	        mask_sums_per_sample = [sum(m) for m in loss_masks]
368	        rollout_total_mask: dict[int, int] = {}
369	        for rid, ms in zip(rollout_id_list, mask_sums_per_sample, strict=True):
370	            rollout_total_mask[rid] = rollout_total_mask.get(rid, 0) + ms
371	        train_data["rollout_mask_sums"] = [rollout_total_mask[rid] for rid in rollout_id_list]
372	
373	        # Overwrite raw_reward when available. Mixed-source batches may only
374	        # populate this field for a subset of samples (e.g. SWE but not code).
375	        if any(sample.metadata and "raw_reward" in sample.metadata for sample in samples):
376	            train_data["raw_reward"] = [
377	                sample.metadata["raw_reward"] if sample.metadata and "raw_reward" in sample.metadata else sample.reward

428	    def _split_train_data_by_dp(self, data):
429	        """Compute the DP/mbs schedule and package each rank's rollout_data
430	        into a Ray Box. The schedule itself is computed by
431	        :func:`build_dp_schedule` so it stays unit-testable without Ray/sglang.
432	
433	        Step split is by rollout id (``samples[i].rollout_id``, falling back
434	        to ``samples[i].index``); each step holds exactly
435	        ``args.global_batch_size`` rollouts so the training-step count per
436	        rollout is fixed at ``rollout_batch_size * n_samples_per_prompt //
437	        global_batch_size`` regardless of how many training samples each
438	        rollout produced.
439	        """
440	        dp_size = self.train_parallel_config["dp_size"]
441	        total_lengths = [len(t) for t in data["tokens"]]
442	        data["total_lengths"] = total_lengths
443	
444	        partitions, micro_batch_indices, num_microbatches, global_batch_sizes = build_dp_schedule(
445	            self.args,
446	            self.train_parallel_config,
447	            total_lengths,
448	            global_batch_size=self.args.global_batch_size,
449	            rollout_indices=data["rollout_ids"],
450	        )
451	
452	        # Package per-rank rollout_data
453	        rollout_data_refs = []
454	        for r in range(dp_size):
455	            partition = partitions[r]
456	            rollout_data = {"partition": partition}
457	            for key in [
458	                "tokens",
459	                "multimodal_train_inputs",
460	                "response_lengths",
461	                "rewards",
462	                "truncated",
463	                "loss_masks",
464	                "round_number",
465	                "sample_indices",
466	                "rollout_ids",
467	                "rollout_mask_sums",
468	                "rollout_log_probs",
469	                "rollout_top_p_token_ids",
470	                "rollout_top_p_token_offsets",
471	                "rollout_routed_experts",
472	                "source_names",
473	                "prompt",
474	                "teacher_log_probs",
475	            ]:
476	                if key not in data:
477	                    continue
478	                rollout_data[key] = [data[key][j] for j in partition]
479	            # keys that need to be splited at train side
480	            for key in ["raw_reward", "total_lengths"]:
481	                if key not in data:
482	                    continue
483	                rollout_data[key] = data[key]
484	            rollout_data["global_batch_sizes"] = global_batch_sizes
485	            rollout_data["num_microbatches"] = num_microbatches
486	            rollout_data["micro_batch_indices"] = micro_batch_indices[r]
487	            tensorize_rollout_data_for_training(rollout_data)
488	            transport = getattr(self.args, "rollout_data_transport", "object-store")
489	            if transport == "nixl":
490	                rollout_data_refs.append(Box(ray.put(rollout_data, _tensor_transport="nixl")))
491	            elif transport == "object-store":
492	                rollout_data_refs.append(Box(ray.put(rollout_data)))
493	            else:
494	                raise ValueError(f"Unsupported rollout data transport: {transport!r}")
495	        return rollout_data_refs

12	def num_requests_from_load(load: Any) -> int:
13	    if isinstance(load, list):
14	        return sum(num_requests_from_load(item) for item in load)
15	
16	    if not isinstance(load, dict):
17	        return 0
18	
19	    if "loads" in load:
20	        return num_requests_from_load(load["loads"])
21	
22	    for key in ("num_reqs", "num_total_reqs", "total_reqs"):
23	        value = load.get(key)
24	        if isinstance(value, int):
25	            return value
26	
27	    running = load.get("num_running_reqs", load.get("total_running_reqs"))
28	    waiting = load.get("num_waiting_reqs", load.get("total_waiting_reqs"))
29	    return (running if isinstance(running, int) else 0) + (waiting if isinstance(waiting, int) else 0)

32	async def _abort_server_once(url: str) -> None:
33	    try:
34	        await post(f"{url}/abort_request", {"abort_all": True})
35	    except Exception as e:
36	        logger.warning(f"Failed to abort SGLang server at {url}: {e}")
37	
38	
39	async def _get_server_num_requests(url: str) -> int:
40	    return num_requests_from_load(await get(f"{url}/v1/loads?include=core"))
41	
42	
43	async def abort_server_until_idle(url: str, retry_interval: int = ABORT_RETRY_INTERVAL_SECONDS) -> None:
44	    attempt = 1
45	    while True:
46	        logger.info(f"Abort request for SGLang server {url}")
47	        await _abort_server_once(url)
48	
49	        try:
50	            num_requests = await _get_server_num_requests(url)
51	        except Exception as e:
52	            logger.warning(f"Failed to get SGLang server load from {url}: {e}")
53	            return
54	
55	        if num_requests <= 0:
56	            return
57	
58	        logger.info(
59	            f"SGLang server {url} still has {num_requests} requests after abort attempt {attempt}; "
60	            f"retrying in {retry_interval} seconds."
61	        )
62	        await asyncio.sleep(retry_interval)
63	        attempt += 1
64	
65	
66	async def abort_servers_until_idle(urls: list[str]) -> None:
67	    await asyncio.gather(*(abort_server_until_idle(url) for url in urls))

446	
447	        if gpus_per_engine > args.num_gpus_per_node:
448	            num_node_per_engine = gpus_per_engine // args.num_gpus_per_node
449	            if local_rank % num_node_per_engine == 0:
450	                dist_init_addr = f"{get_addr()}:{get_port(30 + args.sglang_dp_size)}"

        self.auto_create_handle_loop()

        """Update weights via IPC for checkpoint-engine integration."""
        self.auto_create_handle_loop()
        try:
            # For now, we only support single data parallel instance
            assert (
                self.server_args.dp_size == 1 or self.server_args.enable_dp_attention
            ), "dp_size must be 1 or dp attention must be enabled for update weights from IPC"
            logger.info("Starting IPC weight update")

            async with self.is_pause_cond:
                is_paused = self.is_pause
                if is_paused:
                    result = (await self.update_weights_from_ipc_communicator(obj))[0]

                    result = (await self.update_weights_from_ipc_communicator(obj))[0]
                    success, message = result.success, result.message
        except Exception as e:
            error_msg = f"IPC weight update failed: {str(e)}"
            logger.error(error_msg)
            success, message = False, error_msg

"""
        Update specific parameter in the model weights online
        through `_model_update_group` process group.

        Args:
            name: the name of the parameter to be updated.
            dtype: the data type of the parameter to be updated.
            shape: the shape of the parameter to be updated.

        assert group_name in self._model_update_group, (
            f"Group {group_name} not in {list(self._model_update_group.keys())}. "
            "Please call `init_weights_update_group` first."
        )

        if load_format == "flattened_bucket":
            return self._update_bucketed_weights_from_distributed(
                names, dtypes, shapes, group_name
            )
        try:
            weights = []
            handles = []
            for name, dtype, shape in zip(names, dtypes, shapes):
                target_dtype = (
                    dtype if isinstance(dtype, torch.dtype) else getattr(torch, dtype)
                )
                weight = torch.empty(shape, dtype=target_dtype, device=self.device)
                handles.append(
                    torch.distributed.broadcast(
                        weight,
                        src=0,
                        group=self._model_update_group[group_name],
                        async_op=True,
                    )
                )
                weights.append((name, weight))
            for handle in handles:
                handle.wait()

            self.model.load_weights(weights)
            return True, "Succeeded to update parameter online."

        except Exception as e:
            error_msg = (
                f"Failed to update parameter online: {e}. "
                f"The full weights of the ModelRunner are partially updated. "
                f"Please discard the whole weights."
            )
            logger.error(error_msg)
            return False, error_msg

    def _update_bucketed_weights_from_distributed(
        self, names, dtypes, shapes, group_name
    ):
        try:
            named_tensors = []
            for name, dtype, shape in zip(names, dtypes, shapes):
                target_dtype = (
                    dtype if isinstance(dtype, torch.dtype) else getattr(torch, dtype)
                )
                named_tensors.append(
                    (name, torch.empty(shape, dtype=target_dtype, device=self.device))
                )
            bucket = FlattenedTensorBucket(named_tensors=named_tensors)
            flattened_tensor = bucket.get_flattened_tensor()
            torch.distributed.broadcast(
                flattened_tensor,
                src=0,
                group=self._model_update_group[group_name],
            )
            reconstructed_tensors = bucket.reconstruct_tensors()
            self.model.load_weights(reconstructed_tensors)
            return True, f"Succeeded to update parameter online."
        except Exception as e:
            error_msg = (
                f"Failed to update parameter online: {e}. "
                f"The full weights of the ModelRunner are partially updated. "
                f"Please discard the whole weights."
            )
            logger.error(error_msg)
            return False, error_msg

    def update_weights_from_tensor(
        self,
        named_tensors: List[Tuple[str, Union[torch.Tensor, LocalSerializedTensor]]],
        load_format: Optional[str] = None,
    ):
        monkey_patch_torch_reductions()
        if load_format == "flattened_bucket":
            # Handle flattened bucket format
            return self._update_weights_from_flattened_bucket(
                flattened_tensor_bucket_dict=named_tensors
            )

        # We need to get device after patch otherwise the device would be wrong
        device_module = torch.get_device_module(self.device)
        infered_device = device_module.current_device()

        named_tensors = [
            (name, _unwrap_tensor(tensor, tp_rank=self.tp_rank, device=infered_device))
            for name, tensor in named_tensors
        ]
        if load_format == "direct":
            _model_load_weights_direct(self.model, named_tensors)
        elif load_format in self.server_args.custom_weight_loader:
            custom_loader = dynamic_import(load_format)
            custom_loader(self.model, named_tensors)
        elif load_format is None:
            self.model.load_weights(named_tensors)
        else:
            raise NotImplementedError(f"Unknown load_format={load_format}")
        return True, "Success"

    def _update_weights_from_flattened_bucket(
        self,
        flattened_tensor_bucket_dict,
    ):
        """Handle flattened bucket format for weight updates"""
        flattened_tensor = flattened_tensor_bucket_dict["flattened_tensor"]
        metadata = flattened_tensor_bucket_dict["metadata"]

        # Convert metadata dict to our format
        converted_metadata = []
        for meta in metadata:
            converted_meta = FlattenedTensorMetadata(
                name=meta.name,
                shape=meta.shape,
                dtype=meta.dtype,
                start_idx=meta.start_idx,
                end_idx=meta.end_idx,
                numel=meta.numel,
            )
            converted_metadata.append(converted_meta)

        # Create bucket and reconstruct tensors
        bucket = FlattenedTensorBucket(
            flattened_tensor=flattened_tensor, metadata=converted_metadata
        )
        reconstructed_tensors = bucket.reconstruct_tensors()

        # Load the reconstructed tensors using the standard method
        self.model.load_weights(reconstructed_tensors)

        # The flattened tensor can be backed by CUDA IPC memory owned by the
        # training process.  Weight loaders enqueue device-to-device copies,
        # while the RPC response releases the producer-side IPC buffer.  Make
        # the copies complete before returning so a following bucket cannot
        # reuse that storage and corrupt the just-loaded weights.
        if self.device == "cuda":
            torch.cuda.synchronize()

        return True, "Success"

    txt = open(f).read()

    body = m.group(1) if m else txt

    grads_for_norm: Union[List[torch.Tensor], torch.Tensor],
    norm_type: Union[int, float] = 2,
    grad_stats_parallel_group: Optional[torch.distributed.ProcessGroup] = None,
) -> float:
    """Calculate the norm of gradients in fp32.

    This is adapted from torch.nn.utils.clip_grad.clip_grad_norm_ and
    added functionality to handle model parallel parameters.

    Arguments:
        grads_for_norm (Iterable[Tensor] or Tensor): an iterable of Tensors or a single
            Tensor that will be used for calculating the grad norm.
        norm_type (float or int): type of the used p-norm. Can be ``'inf'`` for
            infinity norm.
        grad_stats_parallel_group (group): Process group for reducing the grad norms. This is
            generally the model-parallel group for non-distributed optimizers, and the entire
            world for the distributed optimizer.

    Returns:
        Total norm of the parameters (viewed as a single vector).
    """

    if isinstance(grads_for_norm, torch.Tensor):
        grads_for_norm = [grads_for_norm]

    data_parallel_group = None
    for grad in grads_for_norm:
        data_parallel_group = get_data_parallel_group_if_dtensor(grad, data_parallel_group)

    grads_for_norm = [to_local_if_dtensor(grad) for grad in grads_for_norm]

    # Norm parameters.
    norm_type = float(norm_type)
    total_norm = 0.0

    # Calculate norm.
    if norm_type == inf:
        total_norm = max(grad.abs().max() for grad in grads_for_norm)
        total_norm_cuda = torch.tensor([float(total_norm)], dtype=torch.float, device='cuda')
        # Take max across all data-parallel GPUs if using FSDP and then all model-parallel GPUs.
        if data_parallel_group:
            torch.distributed.all_reduce(
                total_norm_cuda, op=torch.distributed.ReduceOp.MAX, group=data_parallel_group
            )
        torch.distributed.all_reduce(
            total_norm_cuda, op=torch.distributed.ReduceOp.MAX, group=grad_stats_parallel_group
        )
        total_norm = total_norm_cuda[0].item()

    else:
        if norm_type == 2.0:
            dummy_overflow_buf = torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int, device='cuda')
            # Use apex's multi-tensor applier for efficiency reasons.
            # Multi-tensor applier takes a function and a list of list
            # and performs the operation on that list all in one kernel.
            if grads_for_norm:
                grad_norm, _ = multi_tensor_applier(
                    l2_norm_impl,
                    dummy_overflow_buf,
                    [grads_for_norm],
                    False,  # no per-parameter norm
                )
            else:
                grad_norm = torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.float, device='cuda')
            # Since we will be summing across data parallel groups,
            # we need the pow(norm-type).
            total_norm = grad_norm**norm_type

        else:
            for grad in grads_for_norm:
                grad_norm = torch.norm(grad, norm_type)
                total_norm += grad_norm**norm_type

        # Sum across all data-parallel GPUs if using FSDP and then all model-parallel GPUs.
        if data_parallel_group:
            torch.distributed.all_reduce(
                total_norm, op=torch.distributed.ReduceOp.SUM, group=data_parallel_group
            )
        torch.distributed.all_reduce(
            total_norm, op=torch.distributed.ReduceOp.SUM, group=grad_stats_parallel_group
        )
        total_norm = total_norm.item() ** (1.0 / norm_type)

    return total_norm

150	        split (rollout_metrics.py:232), so one `None` raises;

But these are FIRST-COMPLETED samples — biased toward the SHORTEST episodes (they complete first)! A first-completed sample being short is selection-biased: multi-turn episodes take longer. So first-sample content can't establish the distribution. Still, immediate-done at rollout 0's first sample is notable — the baseline model DOES sometimes emit done immediately (consistent with eval 0's ~1% done-first).

So rollout 4's prompt isn't structurally different from 1,2,3,5. The `<title>/<background>` format appears only in rollout 0 (different task corpus style?). Hmm — but wait: rollout 0's prompt came from the train set sample for that rollout; the EVAL prompts were the `<title>` style?? Let me recall eval 0's example: "You are a support-operations engineer..." — no, the eval examples I extracted earlier were plain prose with `<verification>` markdown code blocks... Let me recall the eval_4_mobile_build example: "You are working as a mobile-build engineer... 4. The file ... follows the required pattern..." — plain prose with numbered verification lists. And that eval-4 first-completed val sample (mobile-build!) IS THE SAME TASK as rollout 5's first sample (mobile-build, task_000000_21013e33)!

The eval-4 first sample was "et_val/mobile-build..."? and rollout 5's is "task_000000_21013e33" label. Whatever — task genre overlapping.

The KEY new fact from this extraction: **the done-first pattern was already visible in FIRST-COMPLETED samples at rollouts 0-5 uniformly** — including rollout 0 and 1 (critic-only era, ZERO actor updates!). Rollout 0's first sample = immediate `<action>done</action>` with reward 0. So immediate-done responses are NOT new at rollout 4 — they existed from the very beginning (before ANY training). I still lack rollout-0-2 length data to establish "healthy before the actor trained". BUT I have the engine activity timeline: rollout 0-2 each took ~25 seconds (18:03:20→18:05:05 for rollout 0 → 105s? hmm: rollout 0 start ~18:02:xx end 18:05:05; rollout 1: 18:05:35→18:06:08 = 33s; rollout 2: 18:06:40→18:08:10 = 90s; rollout 3: 18:08:40→18:08:55 = 15s?!). Rollout 4 (200 tokens mean): 18:10:06-18:10:20 = 14s ✓ plausible.

OK so no smoking gun in durations for rollouts 0-2 (I don't have their response-length metrics — only their WALL TIME, and all of 0-3 fit 15-90s. Hmm, rollout 2 at 90s with rounds ~4.5? rollout 2's first sample showed 1 command + done = 2 rounds... eh — first-completed bias again).

import re
# Prefill lines: ts, #new-seq, #new-token, #cached, #queue-req
pat = re.compile(r"\[(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2} \d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2})\]\s+Prefill batch.*?#new-seq: (\d+), #new-token: (\d+), #cached-token: (\d+), #queue-req: (\d+)")
abort_pat = re.compile(r"\[(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2} \d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2})\]\s*(DELETE|GET) /(abort_request|flush_cache)")
evts = []
for line in open('stage_b.log', errors='replace'):
    m = pat.search(line)
    if m:
        evts.append(('P', m.group(1), int(m.group(2)), int(m.group(3))))
        continue
    m = abort_pat.search(line)
    if m and m.group(3) == 'abort_request':
        evts.append(('A', m.group(1), 0, 0))
# window boundaries from abort times; also known rollout starts

    ('rollout0', '18:02:00', '18:05:06'),
    ('rollout1', '18:05:20', '18:06:14'),
    ('rollout2', '18:06:30', '18:08:16'),
    ('rollout3', '18:08:35', '18:08:58'),
    ('rollout4', '18:10:02', '18:10:22'),
    ('rollout5', '18:14:45', '18:15:05'),
]
def t(s): return s
for name, a, b in windows:
    seqs = toks = reqs = 0
    for typ, ts, ns, nt in evts:
        tt = ts.split()[1]
        if a <= tt <= b:
            if typ == 'P':
                seqs += ns; toks += nt; reqs += 1
    # response tokens ~ newtok (prefill includes prompt+obs); turns/episode = seqs/128

EOF

steps.message: The regex was wrong — `#cached-token` isn't adjacent to `#queue-req`. Fixing:
steps.reasoning_content:
The issue: my regex used `\s+Prefill batch.*?#new-seq: (\d+)` — that should match. Oh wait — the ANSI escape codes! The raw stage_b.log has `[36m` prefix etc. But my regex requires `\[(\d{4}-...)` which comes after the pid. Line: `[36m(SGLangEngine pid=23341)[0m [2026-10-09 17:59:29] Prefill batch, #new-seq: 1, ...`

My pattern: `\[(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2} \d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2})\]\s+Prefill batch.*?#new-seq: (\d+), #new-token: (\d+), #cached-token: (\d+), #queue-req: (\d+)`

The line contains `[2026-10-09 17:59:29] Prefill batch, #new-seq: 1, #new-token: 1084, #cached-token: 0, token usage: 0.04, #running-req: 0, #queue-req: 104, ...`

Between `#cached-token: (\d+),` and `#queue-req:` there's `token usage: 0.04, #running-req: 0, ` — my regex required `#cached-token: (\d+), #queue-req: (\d+)` directly adjacent. That's the bug. Fix the regex.

arguments.command:
cd /tmp/etanalysis && python3 - <<'EOF'
import re
pat = re.compile(r"\[(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2} (\d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2}))\] Prefill batch, #new-seq: (\d+), #new-token: (\d+),")
windows = [
    ('rollout0', '18:00:00', '18:05:06'),
    ('rollout1', '18:05:20', '18:06:14'),
    ('rollout2', '18:06:30', '18:08:16'),
    ('rollout3', '18:08:35', '18:08:58'),
    ('rollout4', '18:10:02', '18:10:22'),
    ('rollout5', '18:14:45', '18:15:05'),
    ('rollout6', '18:17:10', '18:17:50'),
    ('rollout7', '18:19:00', '18:19:40'),
]
res = {name: [0,0,0] for name,_,_ in windows}
for line in open('stage_b.log', errors='replace'):
    m = pat.search(line)
    if not m: continue
    tt = m.group(2)
    for name, a, b in windows:
        if a <= tt <= b:
            res[name][0] += int(m.group(3))
            res[name][1] += int(m.group(4))
            res[name][2] += 1
            break
for name,_,_ in windows:
    s, tok, batches = res[name]
    print(f"{name}: prefill-batches={batches:4d}  #new-seq={s:5d} (~{s/128:5.1f} seq/episode, ~{s/128:.2f} turns)  newtok={tok}")
EOF

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
## 1. Primary Request and Intent

The user requested a **read-only investigation** of a staged RL post-training experiment workspace: a vendored **slime v0.3.2** + **Megatron-LM** stack at `/workspace/slime` plus a custom rollout at `/workspace/et`, with the goal of tracing the **ACTOR training math precisely**, reporting **file:line for everything** and **exact code quotes (small snippets)**. Five specific questions:

1. **Train-loop formulas**: In the Megatron actor train loop (likely `/workspace/slime/slime/backends/megatron_utils/model.py`, esp. around `train/...` metric logging near line 918 — keys train/loss, train/pg_loss, train/entropy_loss, train/pg_clipfrac, train/ppo_kl, train/train_rollout_logprob_abs_diff, train/grad_norm): exact formulas for pg_loss, pg_clipfrac, ppo_kl, entropy_loss, train_rollout_logprob_abs_diff; which tokens contribute (loss_mask? response tokens only?); any scaling (global_batch_size normalization, sequence-length weighting).
2. **Advantages source**: Find the advantage estimation (GAE/GRPO/reinforce) code; report the formula, gamma/lambda values, whether/how advantages are normalized, what estimator the frozen run args configure, HOW values enter (critic value predictions vs returns), and what the `rollout/values`, `rollout/advantages`, `rollout/returns` logged metrics are and where computed/aggregated.
3. **num_critic_only_steps**: Where the actor SKIPS training during critic-only steps; what happens to the actor's optimizer/step counter during skipped cycles (does Adam step counter / lr scheduler advance?); why the actor's first logged train steps are numbered **6 and 7** (both lr 2e-06 flat); what increments `train/step`.
4. **Post-backward path**: Gradient clipping config (clip_grad in args?), optimizer step call (DistributedOptimizer / DistributedFusedAdam?), weight decay, exact place where metrics grad_norm is computed vs where clip is applied; FP16/BF16 overflow handling (log shows nothing about overflow — confirm).
5. **Custom rollout writes**: In `/workspace/et/rollout.py`, what it writes back into Sample objects that downstream advantage estimation reads (loss_mask coverage, reward placement at episode end, values, does it set sample.metadata['et_finish'] or reward scalar?), and check `/workspace/slime/slime/utils/types.py` Sample for fields used by advantage estimation.

Explicit constraints: "Report concisely with code excerpts and precise file:line citations. Do not edit anything." System constraints: READ-ONLY mode (no file creation/modification/deletion/moving/copying, no redirects, no state-changing commands); final report delivered as a regular message, not a file; absolute paths always; no emojis.

## 2. Key Technical Concepts

- **slime v0.3.2** RL post-training framework (Ray-orchestrated actor/critic/rollout managers, SGLang rollout engines, Megatron-LM training backend)
- **Megatron-LM** core: `train_one_step`, pipeline schedules (forward_backward_func), `DistributedOptimizer` (sharded fp32 main params), `MixedPrecisionOptimizer.step()` (prepare_grads → clip_grad_norm → step_with_ready_grads), `finalize_model_grads`, `OptimizerParamScheduler`
- **PPO policy loss** with ratio clipping (`eps_clip`/`eps_clip_high`/dual-clip `eps_clip_c`), per-token `ppo_kl = old_log_probs - log_probs`
- **GAE** (`vanilla_gae` / `chunked_gae`) with gamma=1.0, lambd=1.0; PPO-path token-level rewards = `-kl_coef * kl` plus scalar episode reward added at the **last response token**
- **Per-rollout token-weighted mean** reducer (`get_sum_of_sample_mean` with `rollout_mask_sums` denominators)
- **Loss rescaling for Megatron**: `loss × num_microbatches / step_global_batch_size × dp_world_size`; Megatron schedule divides by num_microbatches; `reduce_train_step_metrics` divides by `step_global_batch_size`
- **`train/step` = `rollout_id * num_steps_per_rollout + step_id`** — a derived counter, not an optimizer step count
- **`actor_trains = (not use_critic) or rollout_id >= num_critic_only_steps`** gating in the top-level train loop (train.py:61)
- **loss_mask semantics**: response-only mask; environment/observation tokens appended `trainable=False` → mask 0 and rollout_log_probs 0.0
- **Two-stage run**: Stage A (PPO from base model, saves Megatron ckpt), Stage B (actor resumes from Stage A ckpt incl. optimizer state; opens with 3 critic-only rollouts then joint PPO)
- bf16 training (fp16=False), grad_scaler=None → no overflow skipping; `check_for_nan_in_loss_and_grad=True` bypasses the manual prepare_grads/get_grad_norm path in model.py

## 3. Files and Code Sections

- **`/workspace/slime/slime/backends/megatron_utils/loss.py`** (core file; read 704-882, 950-1212, 1282-1382)
  - `policy_loss_function` (ends ~line 962; body 963-1172) — answers Q1:
    - L963: `advantages = torch.cat(batch["advantages"], dim=0)`
    - L964: `old_log_probs = batch["rollout_log_probs"] if args.use_rollout_logprobs else batch.get("log_probs")` (run has use_rollout_logprobs=False → old = actor-recomputed log_probs)
    - L1030-1032: `old_log_probs = torch.cat(old_log_probs, dim=0); log_probs = torch.cat(log_probs, dim=0); ppo_kl = old_log_probs - log_probs`
    - L1037-1043: `pg_loss, pg_clipfrac = compute_policy_loss(ppo_kl, advantages, args.eps_clip, args.eps_clip_high, eps_clip_c=args.eps_clip_c)`
    - L1104-1106: `pg_loss = pg_loss_reducer(pg_loss); pg_clipfrac = sum_of_sample_mean(pg_clipfrac); ppo_kl = sum_of_sample_mean(ppo_kl)`
    - L1109-1111: `entropy = log_probs_and_entropy["entropy"]; entropy = torch.cat(entropy, dim=0); entropy_loss = sum_of_sample_mean(entropy)`
    - L1113: `loss = pg_loss - args.entropy_coef * entropy_loss` (entropy_coef=0.0 here)
    - L1135-1139: `train_rollout_logprob_abs_diff = sum_of_sample_mean((log_probs_to_compare - rollout_log_probs).abs())` with `log_probs_to_compare = log_probs if args.use_rollout_logprobs else old_log_probs` (L1138)
    - L1141-1150: `reported_loss` dict keys loss/pg_loss/entropy_loss/pg_clipfrac/ppo_kl/train_rollout_logprob_abs_diff
  - `compute_advantages_and_returns` (L704-881) — answers Q2:
    - L743-746: `if args.kl_coef == 0 or not log_probs: kl = [torch.zeros_like(x, dtype=torch.float32, device=x.device) for x in xs]` (kl_coef=0.0 → kl all zeros)
    - L769-781 (ppo branch): `kl_coef = -args.kl_coef; ... for reward, per_token_kl in zip(old_rewards, kl, strict=False): token_level_rewards = per_token_kl * kl_coef; if cp_rank == 0: token_level_rewards[-1] += reward; rewards.append(token_level_rewards); advantages, returns = get_advantages_and_returns_batch(total_lengths, response_lengths, values, rewards, args.gamma, args.lambd)` — scalar reward added to the LAST response token; `values` = critic value predictions from `rollout_data["values"]`
    - L818-877: `if args.normalize_advantages:` whitening via `distributed_masked_whiten(all_advs, all_masks, process_group=dp_cp_group, shift_mean=True)` (disabled: normalize_advantages=False)
    - L879-880: `rollout_data["advantages"] = advantages; rollout_data["returns"] = returns`
  - `loss_function` (L1282-1382) — scaling: L1316 `num_tokens = sum([torch.clamp_min(loss_mask.sum(), 1) ...])`; L1318-1324 builds `sum_of_sample_mean` with `batch["rollout_mask_sums"]`; L1352-1358: `loss = loss * num_microbatches / step_global_batch_size * mpu.get_data_parallel_world_size(with_context_parallel=True)` (when not calculate_per_token_loss)

- **`/workspace/slime/slime/utils/ppo_utils.py`** (read fully)
  - `compute_policy_loss` L124-148: `ratio = (-ppo_kl).exp(); pg_losses1 = -ratio * advantages; pg_losses2 = -ratio.clamp(1 - eps_clip, 1 + eps_clip_high) * advantages; clip_pg_losses1 = torch.maximum(pg_losses1, pg_losses2); clipfrac = torch.gt(pg_losses2, pg_losses1).float()` (+ optional dual-clip eps_clip_c branch L138-146)
  - `vanilla_gae` L584-605: `delta = rewards[:, t] + gamma * next_value - values[:, t]; lastgaelam = delta + gamma * lambd * lastgaelam; ...; full_returns = full_advantages + values`
  - `chunked_gae` L693-713; `get_advantages_and_returns_batch` L476-581 (pads to max_len, CP-aware)
  - `get_grpo_returns` L361-368; `compute_approx_kl` L11-51 (k1/k2/k3/low_var_kl); `compute_cispo_loss` L151-171; `compute_gspo_kl` L95-121; `compute_opsm_mask` L54-92

- **`/workspace/slime/slime/backends/megatron_utils/cp_utils.py`** L47-121 — `get_sum_of_sample_mean`: for cp_size==1 returns `sum([(x_i * loss_mask_i).sum() / torch.clamp_min(denom, 1) for x_i, loss_mask_i, denom in zip(x.split(response_lengths, dim=0), loss_masks, sample_denoms)])`; `sample_denoms` defaults to per-sample `loss_mask.sum()` but callers pass per-rollout `rollout_mask_sums` for token-weighted per-rollout means

- **`/workspace/slime/slime/backends/megatron_utils/model.py`** (read 235-345, 512-829, 830-940)
  - `train_one_step` L512-702: L553-555 zero grads; L580-602 get_batch keys incl. loss_masks/advantages/values/returns/rollout_log_probs/rollout_mask_sums; L648-657 forward_backward_func; L659-670 `if not getattr(args, "check_for_nan_in_loss_and_grad", True): found_inf_flag = optimizer.prepare_grads(); ... grad_norm = optimizer.get_grad_norm()` — **skipped** because check_for_nan_in_loss_and_grad=True (log line 79); L679-686 `if valid_step: update_successful, grad_norm, num_zeros_in_grad = optimizer.step(); assert update_successful; opt_param_scheduler.step(increment=step_global_batch_size)`; L693-701 reduce_train_step_metrics
  - `train` L710-829: L816 `num_steps_per_rollout = len(num_microbatches)`; L827 loop `for step_id in range(num_steps_per_rollout)`; L772 `config.finalize_model_grads_func = finalize_model_grads`; L776-796 reset_optimizer_states block (disabled)
  - Logging block L873-918: L879 `accumulated_step_id = rollout_id * num_steps_per_rollout + step_id`; L882-885 log_dict from loss_dict with `train/` prefix; L886 `log_dict[f"train/{role_tag}grad_norm"] = grad_norm`; L893 `log_dict[f"train/{role_tag}lr-pg_{param_group_id}"] = opt_param_scheduler.get_lr(param_group)`; L896 global_batch_size; L897 `log_dict["train/step"] = accumulated_step_id`; **L918** `logger.info(f"{role_tag}step {accumulated_step_id}: {log_dict}")` (the "step 6:" / "critic-step N:" lines in the log)
  - `setup_model_and_optimizer` L269-321: L301-304 builds OptimizerConfig from args fields; L313 `get_megatron_optimizer(config=config, model_chunks=model, ...)`; L320 opt_param_scheduler

- **`/workspace/slime/slime/observability/train_metric_utils.py`** (read fully) — answers rollout/* metrics (Q2):
  - `reduce_train_step_metrics` L18-59: sums per-mb values, `dist.all_reduce(values, group=dp_with_cp_group)`, then `{key: value * cp_factor / num_samples_or_tokens ...}` with `num_samples_or_tokens = step_global_batch_size`, `cp_factor = 1` for per-rollout-mean mode (L53-59) — final division by global batch size

  - `rollout_log_metric_contribution` L62-83: `sum_value = cp_size * per_rank_reducer_sum; count = num_rollouts_in_rollout / dp_size` (reduced to Σsum/Σcount)
  - `gather_log_data` L117-139: `reduced_log_dict = {f"{metric_name}/{key}": value ...}` → the `rollout/values`, `rollout/advantages`, `rollout/returns` keys; logged at **train_metric_utils.py:135** (matches the log's source line)

- **`/workspace/slime/slime/backends/megatron_utils/actor.py`** (read 340-536) — answers Q2 values entry:
  - `train_critic` L363-389: L370 `rollout_data.update(forward_only(get_values, self.args, self.model, data_iterator, num_microbatches))` — critic computes current values; L372 compute_advantages_and_returns; L374 `self.args.loss_type = "value_loss"`; L385-388 returns `{"values": tensors_to_cpu(rollout_data["values"])}`

1	#!/bin/bash
2	#
3	# Multi-Turn PPO on Endless Terminals with Qwen3-1.7B, on slime v0.3.2.
4	#
5	# The run has two stages:
6	#
7	#   Stage A -- "the previous training run".  A real PPO rollout (actor + critic)
8	#              starting from the base HF model, which saves a Megatron
9	#              checkpoint for both roles.
10	#
11	#   Stage B -- "the model was reloaded".  The actor genuinely resumes from
12	#              Stage A's Megatron checkpoint (weights *and* optimizer state).
13	#              The critic's backbone is reloaded from the base model.  Stage B
14	#              opens with NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS critic-only rollouts (the
15	#              warmup window) and then trains actor and critic jointly.
16	#
17	# The full slime source tree is bundled in the workspace (slime/) and is the
18	# copy that runs -- this script puts it ahead of the image's install on
19	# PYTHONPATH, so editing slime/ here is what takes effect, with nothing to
20	# install first.
21	#
22	# NOTE ON A SHARED HOST: unlike slime's own example scripts this one never runs
23	# `pkill -9 ray / pkill -9 python / ray stop --force` on entry.  It is meant to
24	# run inside its own container, and it brings up a private Ray head on a
25	# non-default port with a private temp dir.
26	
27	set -euo pipefail
28	
29	WS="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" &>/dev/null && pwd)"
30	
31	# The container runs as root while /workspace is a bind mount owned by whoever
32	# checked the case out, so any .pyc written here lands root-owned in their tree
33	# -- and `importlib` copies the *source* file's mode onto the .pyc, so a 600
34	# source yields a 600 root-owned file that even the owner cannot read, and
35	# `cp -r` of the case fails. Nothing here benefits from a bytecode cache.
36	export PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1
37	
38	MODEL_DIR="${MODEL_DIR:-${WS}/Qwen3-1.7B}"
39	ET_SRC="${ET_SRC:-${WS}/endless-terminals}"
40	SLIME_HOME="${SLIME_HOME:-${WS}/slime}"
41	OUT_DIR="${OUT_DIR:-${WS}/outputs}"
42	CKPT_ROOT="${CKPT_ROOT:-/ckpt}"
43	
44	# Endless Terminals sandbox knobs; also forwarded into the Ray workers, which
45	# read them at import time in et/rollout.py.
46	#
47	# These must NOT live under /dev/shm: it is mounted noexec in the training
48	# image, and many tasks' verifiers assert os.access(path, os.X_OK), which is
49	# False there even at mode 755.
50	export ET_DATA_ROOT="${ET_DATA_ROOT:-/tmp/et_prompts}"
51	export ET_SCRATCH="${ET_SCRATCH:-/tmp/et_episodes}"
52	export ET_MAX_TURNS="${ET_MAX_TURNS:-6}"
53	export ET_MAX_NEW_TOKENS="${ET_MAX_NEW_TOKENS:-384}"
54	export ET_CMD_TIMEOUT="${ET_CMD_TIMEOUT:-20}"
55	export ET_MAX_OBS_CHARS="${ET_MAX_OBS_CHARS:-1200}"
56	
57	NUM_GPUS="${NUM_GPUS:-2}"
58	TP_SIZE="${TP_SIZE:-2}"
59	SGLANG_MEM_FRACTION="${SGLANG_MEM_FRACTION:-0.55}"
60	# Rollouts per stage. Both stages use the same count on purpose, and must:
61	# slime derives `train_iters` from `--num-rollout` (model.py:203) and Megatron
62	# stores the resulting LR/weight-decay horizons inside the checkpoint, then
63	# asserts on reload that they match the ones the new arguments imply
64	# ("total number of iterations do not match"). Giving Stage B a different
65	# rollout count than Stage A would trip that assert before any training runs.
66	# In Stage A these rollouts are ordinary PPO; Stage B opens with
67	# NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS critic-only rollouts -- the warmup window -- and then
68	# trains actor and critic jointly for the rest.
69	NUM_ROLLOUTS="${NUM_ROLLOUTS:-2}"
70	# Stage B is the long one: critic warmup followed by joint PPO, trained until
71	# the validation pass rate stops moving. It no longer has to match Stage A's
72	# rollout count -- see --override-opt-param-scheduler at the submit site.
73	NUM_ROLLOUTS_B="${NUM_ROLLOUTS_B:-${NUM_ROLLOUTS}}"
74	# Rollouts at the start of Stage B in which only the critic trains. This is the
75	# warmup window the incident was reported against, and the window in which the
76	# value loss is measured.
77	NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS="${NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS:-${NUM_ROLLOUTS_B}}"
78	
79	# Episodes per rollout = ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE x N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT; optimizer
80	# steps per rollout = that, divided by GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE.
81	ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE="${ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE:-8}"
82	N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT="${N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT:-2}"
83	GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE="${GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE:-8}"
84	LR="${LR:-1e-6}"
85	
86	# How many leading critic optimizer steps the reported warmup statistics cover.
87	# Derived rather than guessed, because once Stage B runs past the critic-only
88	# phase the two are no longer the same thing: averaging the value loss over all
89	# of a 30-rollout Stage B measures mostly a critic that has already been
90	# trained, which is not what "warmup value loss" names and not what the
91	# incident was about.
92	CRITIC_WARMUP_STEPS=$(( NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS * ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE * N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT / GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE ))
93	[ "${CRITIC_WARMUP_STEPS}" -gt 0 ] || CRITIC_WARMUP_STEPS=1
94	
95	# Held-out evaluation during Stage B. 0 disables it, which is what the short
96	# value-loss-only reproduction wants.
97	#
98	# val and test get different sample budgets. val only has to say *when* the
99	# curve flattens, so 2 samples x 150 tasks is enough; test carries the
100	# end-to-end claim and is compared per task, where the useful quantity is each
101	# task's success *rate*, which 1 or 2 samples cannot resolve at all.
102	EVAL_INTERVAL="${EVAL_INTERVAL:-0}"
103	N_EVAL_SAMPLES="${N_EVAL_SAMPLES:-2}"
104	N_EVAL_SAMPLES_TEST="${N_EVAL_SAMPLES_TEST:-4}"
105	
106	# How often Stage B checkpoints. Trained to convergence, Stage B runs for well
107	# over an hour, which on a shared host is long enough to be interrupted -- two
108	# runs of this case were killed from outside the container mid-training, once
109	# with SIGTERM and once with SIGKILL. So Stage B saves as it goes and a second
110	# invocation picks up where the first stopped, instead of starting the hour
111	# again. 0 disables it, which is what the short value-loss-only reproduction
112	# wants: it writes nothing and measures only the reload.
113	STAGE_B_SAVE_INTERVAL="${STAGE_B_SAVE_INTERVAL:-0}"
114	
115	RAY_PORT="${RAY_PORT:-6479}"
116	DASH_PORT="${DASH_PORT:-8277}"
117	RAY_TMP="${RAY_TMP:-/tmp/ray_ppo}"
118	
119	mkdir -p "${OUT_DIR}" "${CKPT_ROOT}" "${ET_SCRATCH}"
120	
121	# --------------------------------------------------------- 0. the slime source
122	# The full slime source tree is bundled in the workspace (${SLIME_HOME}) and is
123	# put ahead of the image's editable install on PYTHONPATH below, so it is the
124	# copy that trains -- there is nothing to install first.
125	test -f "${SLIME_HOME}/train.py" || {
126	    echo "FATAL: bundled slime source not found at ${SLIME_HOME}" >&2
127	    exit 1
128	}
129	
130	# ------------------------------------------------------- 1. the prompt dataset
131	# prepare.sh ships the already-built dataset (transpiled + validated + split) at
132	# ${WS}/et_prompts. Seed ET_DATA_ROOT from it so the build below is skipped: the
133	# 2492->1489 admission is environment-fixed and reproducible, so there is no need
134	# to re-run the ~40min transpile+validate pass (and ET_SRC is never read). The
135	# copy lands in a writable, exec-capable dir (ET_DATA_ROOT defaults to /tmp) --
136	# the bundled tree under /workspace may be a root-owned bind mount. If the
137	# prebuilt payload is absent, fall through to building from ET_SRC as before.
138	if [ ! -s "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals.jsonl" ] && [ -s "${WS}/et_prompts/endless_terminals.jsonl" ]; then
139	    echo "=== seeding ET_DATA_ROOT from prebuilt ${WS}/et_prompts (skipping transpile+validate) ==="
140	    mkdir -p "${ET_DATA_ROOT}"
141	    cp -a "${WS}/et_prompts/." "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/"
142	fi
143	if [ ! -s "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals.jsonl" ]; then
144	    echo "=== transpiling + validating the Endless Terminals tasks ==="
145	    (cd "${WS}" && python3 -m et.build_dataset --src "${ET_SRC}" --out "${ET_DATA_ROOT}") \
146	        2>&1 | tee "${OUT_DIR}/build_dataset.log"
147	fi
148	# Deliberately not silenced. A report that is quietly 0 bytes is worse than one
149	# that is loudly absent: it reads as "every task was rejected" to anyone who
150	# opens it later, and that has happened here more than once.
151	copy_artifact() {   # copy_artifact <src>
152	    local src="$1" dst="${OUT_DIR}/$(basename "$1")"
153	    if ! cp -f "${src}" "${dst}"; then
154	        echo "WARNING: could not copy ${src} into ${OUT_DIR}" >&2
155	    elif [ ! -s "${dst}" ] && [ -s "${src}" ]; then
156	        echo "WARNING: ${dst} came out empty although ${src} is not" >&2
157	    fi
158	}
159	copy_artifact "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/validation_report.json"
160	N_PROMPTS="$(wc -l < "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals.jsonl")"
161	echo "prompt set: ${N_PROMPTS} validated Endless Terminals tasks"
162	if [ "${N_PROMPTS}" -lt 4 ]; then
163	    echo "FATAL: too few tasks survived validation to train on." >&2
164	    exit 1
165	fi
166	
167	# Train on one part of the task set and measure on another. The split is a pure
168	# function of the admitted list and a fixed seed, so every run trains and is
169	# scored on exactly the same tasks -- otherwise a comparison between runs is
170	# partly measuring which tasks each one happened to get.
171	if [ ! -s "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals_train.jsonl" ]; then
172	    (cd "${WS}" && python3 -m et.make_splits --prompts "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals.jsonl")
173	fi
174	copy_artifact "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/splits.json"
175	TRAIN_SPLIT="${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals_train.jsonl"
176	VAL_SPLIT="${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals_val.jsonl"
177	TEST_SPLIT="${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals_test.jsonl"
178	printf 'splits: train %s / val %s / test %s\n' \
179	    "$(wc -l < "${TRAIN_SPLIT}")" "$(wc -l < "${VAL_SPLIT}")" "$(wc -l < "${TEST_SPLIT}")"
180	
181	# ------------------------------------------------------------- 2. shared args
182	source "${WS}/configs/model_args.sh"
183	
184	ROLLOUT_ARGS=(
185	    --prompt-data "${TRAIN_SPLIT}"
186	    --input-key prompt
187	    --label-key label
188	    --rollout-shuffle
189	    --rollout-batch-size "${ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE}"
190	    --n-samples-per-prompt "${N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT}"
191	    --rollout-max-response-len 2048
192	    --rollout-temperature 1.0
193	    --global-batch-size "${GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE}"
194	    --balance-data
195	    # The multi-turn terminal loop and its pytest-based episode reward.
196	    --custom-generate-function-path et.rollout.generate
197	    --custom-rm-path et.rollout.reward_func
198	)
199	
200	PPO_ARGS=(
201	    --advantage-estimator ppo   # -> args.use_critic
202	    --gamma 1.0
203	    --lambd 1.0
204	    --eps-clip 0.2
205	    --value-clip 0.2
206	    --kl-coef 0.0               # no reference model, hence no --ref-load and
207	    --entropy-coef 0.0          # no HF -> torch_dist conversion step
208	)
209	
210	PERF_ARGS=(
211	    --tensor-model-parallel-size "${TP_SIZE}"
212	    --pipeline-model-parallel-size 1
213	    --context-parallel-size 1
214	    --recompute-granularity full
215	    --recompute-method uniform
216	    --recompute-num-layers 1
217	    --use-dynamic-batch-size
218	    --max-tokens-per-gpu 8192
219	)
220	# Sequence parallelism splits the activations of the non-tensor-parallel ops
221	# across the TP group, so it is only defined for TP > 1; Megatron asserts on it.
222	# Spelled as an `if` rather than `[ ... ] && ...`: the latter evaluates to the
223	# test's status, which under `set -e` ends the script whenever TP_SIZE is 1.
224	if [ "${TP_SIZE}" -gt 1 ]; then
225	    PERF_ARGS+=(--sequence-parallel)
226	fi
227	
228	OPTIMIZER_ARGS=(
229	    --optimizer adam
230	    --lr "${LR}"
231	    --lr-decay-style constant
232	    --weight-decay 0.0
233	    --adam-beta1 0.9
234	    --adam-beta2 0.95
235	)
236	
237	SGLANG_ARGS=(
238	    --rollout-num-gpus-per-engine "${NUM_GPUS}"
239	    # Colocated: this fraction is what SGLang keeps, and Megatron's weights,
240	    # gradients and Adam state have to fit in the rest. At TP 2 each GPU carries
241	    # half of each role, so 0.55 leaves enough; drop it when NUM_GPUS is 1 and
242	    # one device has to hold both roles whole.
243	    --sglang-mem-fraction-static "${SGLANG_MEM_FRACTION}"
244	)
245	
246	# Held-out scoring, used only by Stage B. slime evaluates once before the first
247	# rollout and then every EVAL_INTERVAL rollouts, which gives both the starting
248	# pass rate and the curve that says whether training has converged.
249	#
250	# val and test are evaluated at the same points on purpose. The convergence
251	# *decision* is read off val; test is reported only at the final point, and
252	# evaluating it throughout costs generation but no statistical validity, since
253	# nothing about the run is conditioned on it.
254	#
255	# Spelled as an --eval-config YAML rather than --eval-prompt-data because the
256	# two splits need different sample counts, and --n-samples-per-eval-prompt is
257	# one global number. Everything the YAML leaves out still falls back to the
258	# command line (eval_config.py:10 DATASET_RUNTIME_SPECS), so temperature,
259	# response length and the prompt/label keys are set once, below and above.
260	EVAL_ARGS=()
261	if [ "${EVAL_INTERVAL}" -gt 0 ]; then
262	    cat > "${OUT_DIR}/eval_datasets.yaml" <<YAML
263	eval:
264	  datasets:
265	    - name: et_val
266	      path: ${VAL_SPLIT}
267	      n_samples_per_eval_prompt: ${N_EVAL_SAMPLES}
268	    - name: et_test
269	      path: ${TEST_SPLIT}
270	      n_samples_per_eval_prompt: ${N_EVAL_SAMPLES_TEST}
271	YAML
272	    EVAL_ARGS=(
273	        --eval-interval "${EVAL_INTERVAL}"
274	        --eval-config "${OUT_DIR}/eval_datasets.yaml"
275	        --eval-max-response-len 2048
276	        --eval-temperature 1.0
277	        --log-passrate
278	        --custom-eval-rollout-log-function-path et.eval_log.log_eval_rollout_data
279	    )
280	fi

282	MISC_ARGS=(
283	    --attention-dropout 0.0
284	    --hidden-dropout 0.0
285	    --accumulate-allreduce-grads-in-fp32
286	    --attention-softmax-in-fp32
287	    --attention-backend flash

293	# each other's checkpoints (the critic's output layer is [1, hidden_size], the

303	  - name: stage-a-critic

306	      load: ${MODEL_DIR}
307	      save: ${CKPT_ROOT}/critic
308	YAML

310	# Stage B can be entered two ways, and they are not the same event.
311	#
312	#   fresh   -- "the model was reloaded". The actor resumes from Stage A's
313	#              Megatron checkpoint; the critic's backbone comes from the base

317	#              own checkpoints, optimizer state included, and the run continues
318	#              from the last saved rollout. The first attempt's log is kept,
319	#              not overwritten (see the STAGE_B_LOG choice below).

336	megatron:

338	    role: actor
339	    overrides:

[metadata] {"type": "text", "file": {"filePath": "/workspace/run.sh", "content": "#!/bin/bash\n#\n# Multi-Turn PPO on Endless Terminals with Qwen3-1.7B, on slime v0.3.2.\n#\n# The run has two stages:\n#\n#   Stage A -- \"the previous training run\".  A real PPO rollout (actor + critic)\n#              starting from the base HF model, which saves a Megatron\n#              checkpoint for both roles.\n#\n#   Stage B -- \"the model was reloaded\".  The actor genuinely resumes from\n#              Stage A's Megatron checkpoint (weights *and* optimizer state).\n#              The critic's backbone is reloaded from the base model.  Stage B\n#              opens with NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS critic-only rollouts (the\n#              warmup window) and then trains actor and critic jointly.\n#\n# The full slime source tree is bundled in the workspace (slime/) and is the\n# copy that runs -- this script puts it ahead of the image's install on\n# PYTHONPATH, so editing slime/ here is what takes effect, with nothing to\n# install first.\n#\n# NOTE ON A SHARED HOST: unlike slime's own example scripts this one never runs\n# `pkill -9 ray / pkill -9 python / ray stop --force` on entry.  It is meant to\n# run inside its own container, and it brings up a private Ray head on a\n# non-default port with a private temp dir.\n\nset -euo pipefail\n\nWS=\"$(cd -- \"$(dirname -- \"${BASH_SOURCE[0]}\")\" &>/dev/null && pwd)\"\n\n# The container runs as root while /workspace is a bind mount owned by whoever\n# checked the case out, so any .pyc written here lands root-owned in their tree\n# -- and `importlib` copies the *source* file's mode onto the .pyc, so a 600\n# source yields a 600 root-owned file that even the owner cannot read, and\n# `cp -r` of the case fails. Nothing here benefits from a bytecode cache.\nexport PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1\n\nMODEL_DIR=\"${MODEL_DIR:-${WS}/Qwen3-1.7B}\"\nET_SRC=\"${ET_SRC:-${WS}/endless-terminals}\"\nSLIME_HOME=\"${SLIME_HOME:-${WS}/slime}\"\nOUT_DIR=\"${OUT_DIR:-${WS}/outputs}\"\nCKPT_ROOT=\"${CKPT_ROOT:-/ckpt}\"\n\n# Endless Terminals sandbox knobs; also forwarded into the Ray workers, which\n# read them at import time in et/rollout.py.\n#\n# These must NOT live under /dev/shm: it is mounted noexec in the training\n# image, and many tasks' verifiers assert os.access(path, os.X_OK), which is\n# False there even at mode 755.\nexport ET_DATA_ROOT=\"${ET_DATA_ROOT:-/tmp/et_prompts}\"\nexport ET_SCRATCH=\"${ET_SCRATCH:-/tmp/et_episodes}\"\nexport ET_MAX_TURNS=\"${ET_MAX_TURNS:-6}\"\nexport ET_MAX_NEW_TOKENS=\"${ET_MAX_NEW_TOKENS:-384}\"\nexport ET_CMD_TIMEOUT=\"${ET_CMD_TIMEOUT:-20}\"\nexport ET_MAX_OBS_CHARS=\"${ET_MAX_OBS_CHARS:-1200}\"\n\nNUM_GPUS=\"${NUM_GPUS:-2}\"\nTP_SIZE=\"${TP_SIZE:-2}\"\nSGLANG_MEM_FRACTION=\"${SGLANG_MEM_FRACTION:-0.55}\"\n# Rollouts per stage. Both stages use the same count on purpose, and must:\n# slime derives `train_iters` from `--num-rollout` (model.py:203) and Megatron\n# stores the resulting LR/weight-decay horizons inside the checkpoint, then\n# asserts on reload that they match the ones the new arguments imply\n# (\"total number of iterations do not match\"). Giving Stage B a different\n# rollout count than Stage A would trip that assert before any training runs.\n# In Stage A these rollouts are ordinary PPO; Stage B opens with\n# NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS critic-only rollouts -- the warmup window -- and then\n# trains actor and critic jointly for the rest.\nNUM_ROLLOUTS=\"${NUM_ROLLOUTS:-2}\"\n# Stage B is the long one: critic warmup followed by joint PPO, trained until\n# the validation pass rate stops moving. It no longer has to match Stage A's\n# rollout count -- see --override-opt-param-scheduler at the submit site.\nNUM_ROLLOUTS_B=\"${NUM_ROLLOUTS_B:-${NUM_ROLLOUTS}}\"\n# Rollouts at the start of Stage B in which only the critic trains. This is the\n# warmup window the incident was reported against, and the window in which the\n# value loss is measured.\nNUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS=\"${NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS:-${NUM_ROLLOUTS_B}}\"\n\n# Episodes per rollout = ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE x N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT; optimizer\n# steps per rollout = that, divided by GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE.\nROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE=\"${ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE:-8}\"\nN_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT=\"${N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT:-2}\"\nGLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE=\"${GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE:-8}\"\nLR=\"${LR:-1e-6}\"\n\n# How many leading critic optimizer steps the reported warmup statistics cover.\n# Derived rather than guessed, because once Stage B runs past the critic-only\n# phase the two are no longer the same thing: averaging the value loss over all\n# of a 30-rollout Stage B measures mostly a critic that has already been\n# trained, which is not what \"warmup value loss\" names and not what the\n# incident was about.\nCRITIC_WARMUP_STEPS=$(( NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS * ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE * N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT / GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE ))\n[ \"${CRITIC_WARMUP_STEPS}\" -gt 0 ] || CRITIC_WARMUP_STEPS=1\n\n# Held-out evaluation during Stage B. 0 disables it, which is what the short\n# value-loss-only reproduction wants.\n#\n# val and test get different sample budgets. val only has to say *when* the\n# curve flattens, so 2 samples x 150 tasks is enough; test carries the\n# end-to-end claim and is compared per task, where the useful quantity is each\n# task's success *rate*, which 1 or 2 samples cannot resolve at all.\nEVAL_INTERVAL=\"${EVAL_INTERVAL:-0}\"\nN_EVAL_SAMPLES=\"${N_EVAL_SAMPLES:-2}\"\nN_EVAL_SAMPLES_TEST=\"${N_EVAL_SAMPLES_TEST:-4}\"\n\n# How often Stage B checkpoints. Trained to convergence, Stage B runs for well\n# over an hour, which on a shared host is long enough to be interrupted -- two\n# runs of this case were killed from outside the container mid-training, once\n# with SIGTERM and once with SIGKILL. So Stage B saves as it goes and a second\n# invocation picks up where the first stopped, instead of starting the hour\n# again. 0 disables it, which is what the short value-loss-only reproduction\n# wants: it writes nothing and measures only the reload.\nSTAGE_B_SAVE_INTERVAL=\"${STAGE_B_SAVE_INTERVAL:-0}\"\n\nRAY_PORT=\"${RAY_PORT:-6479}\"\nDASH_PORT=\"${DASH_PORT:-8277}\"\nRAY_TMP=\"${RAY_TMP:-/tmp/ray_ppo}\"\n\nmkdir -p \"${OUT_DIR}\" \"${CKPT_ROOT}\" \"${ET_SCRATCH}\"\n\n# --------------------------------------------------------- 0. the slime source\n# The full slime source tree is bundled in the workspace (${SLIME_HOME}) and is\n# put ahead of the image's editable install on PYTHONPATH below, so it is the\n# copy that trains -- there is nothing to install first.\ntest -f \"${SLIME_HOME}/train.py\" || {\n    echo \"FATAL: bundled slime source not found at ${SLIME_HOME}\" >&2\n    exit 1\n}\n\n# ------------------------------------------------------- 1. the prompt dataset\n# prepare.sh ships the already-built dataset (transpiled + validated + split) at\n# ${WS}/et_prompts. Seed ET_DATA_ROOT from it so the build below is skipped: the\n# 2492->1489 admission is environment-fixed and reproducible, so there is no need\n# to re-run the ~40min transpile+validate pass (and ET_SRC is never read). The\n# copy lands in a writable, exec-capable dir (ET_DATA_ROOT defaults to /tmp) --\n# the bundled tree under /workspace may be a root-owned bind mount. If the\n# prebuilt payload is absent, fall through to building from ET_SRC as before.\nif [ ! -s \"${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals.jsonl\" ] && [ -s \"${WS}/et_prompts/endless_terminals.jsonl\" ]; then\n    echo \"=== seeding ET_DATA_ROOT from prebuilt ${WS}/et_prompts (skipping transpile+validate) ===\"\n    mkdir -p \"${ET_DATA_ROOT}\"\n    cp -a \"${WS}/et_prompts/.\" \"${ET_DATA_ROOT}/\"\nfi\nif [ ! -s \"${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals.jsonl\" ]; then\n    echo \"=== transpiling + validating the Endless Terminals tasks ===\"\n    (cd \"${WS}\" && python3 -m et.build_dataset --src \"${ET_SRC}\" --out \"${ET_DATA_ROOT}\") \\\n        2>&1 | tee \"${OUT_DIR}/build_dataset.log\"\nfi\n# Deliberately not silenced. A report that is quietly 0 bytes is worse than one\n# that is loudly absent: it reads as \"every task was rejected\" to anyone who\n# opens it later, and that has happened here more than once.\ncopy_artifact() {   # copy_artifact <src>\n    local src=\"$1\" dst=\"${OUT_DIR}/$(basename \"$1\")\"\n    if ! cp -f \"${src}\" \"${dst}\"; then\n        echo \"WARNING: could not copy ${src} into ${OUT_DIR}\" >&2\n    elif [ ! -s \"${dst}\" ] && [ -s \"${src}\" ]; then\n        echo \"WARNING: ${dst} came out empty although ${src} is not\" >&2\n    fi\n}\ncopy_artifact \"${ET_DATA_ROOT}/validation_report.json\"\nN_PROMPTS=\"$(wc -l < \"${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals.jsonl\")\"\necho \"prompt set: ${N_PROMPTS} validated Endless Terminals tasks\"\nif [ \"${N_PROMPTS}\" -lt 4 ]; then\n    echo \"FATAL: too few tasks survived validation to train on.\" >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\n# Train on one part of the task set and measure on another. The split is a pure\n# function of the admitted list and a fixed seed, so every run trains and is\n# scored on exactly the same tasks -- otherwise a comparison between runs is\n# partly measuring which tasks each one happened to get.\nif [ ! -s \"${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals_train.jsonl\" ]; then\n    (cd \"${WS}\" && python3 -m et.make_splits --prompts \"${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals.jsonl\")\nfi\ncopy_artifact \"${ET_DATA_ROOT}/splits.json\"\nTRAIN_SPLIT=\"${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals_train.jsonl\"\nVAL_SPLIT=\"${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals_val.jsonl\"\nTEST_SPLIT=\"${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals_test.jsonl\"\nprintf 'splits: train %s / val %s / test %s\\n' \\\n    \"$(wc -l < \"${TRAIN_SPLIT}\")\" \"$(wc -l < \"${VAL_SPLIT}\")\" \"$(wc -l < \"${TEST_SPLIT}\")\"\n\n# ------------------------------------------------------------- 2. shared args\nsource \"${WS}/configs/model_args.sh\"\n\nROLLOUT_ARGS=(\n    --prompt-data \"${TRAIN_SPLIT}\"\n    --input-key prompt\n    --label-key label\n    --rollout-shuffle\n    --rollout-batch-size \"${ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE}\"\n    --n-samples-per-prompt \"${N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT}\"\n    --rollout-max-response-len 2048\n    --rollout-temperature 1.0\n    --global-batch-size \"${GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE}\"\n    --balance-data\n    # The multi-turn terminal loop and its pytest-based episode reward.\n    --custom-generate-function-path et.rollout.generate\n    --custom-rm-path et.rollout.reward_func\n)\n\nPPO_ARGS=(\n    --advantage-estimator ppo   # -> args.use_critic\n    --gamma 1.0\n    --lambd 1.0\n    --eps-clip 0.2\n    --value-clip 0.2\n    --kl-coef 0.0               # no reference model, hence no --ref-load and\n    --entropy-coef 0.0          # no HF -> torch_dist conversion step\n)\n\nPERF_ARGS=(\n    --tensor-model-parallel-size \"${TP_SIZE}\"\n    --pipeline-model-parallel-size 1\n    --context-parallel-size 1\n    --recompute-granularity full\n    --recompute-method uniform\n    --recompute-num-layers 1\n    --use-dynamic-batch-size\n    --max-tokens-per-gpu 8192\n)\n# Sequence parallelism splits the activations of the non-tensor-parallel ops\n# across the TP group, so it is only defined for TP > 1;
