then\n    PERF_ARGS+=(--sequence-parallel)\nfi\n\nOPTIMIZER_ARGS=(\n    --optimizer adam\n    --lr \"${LR}\"\n    --lr-decay-style constant\n    --weight-decay 0.0\n    --adam-beta1 0.9\n    --adam-beta2 0.95\n)\n\nSGLANG_ARGS=(\n    --rollout-num-gpus-per-engine \"${NUM_GPUS}\"\n    # Colocated: this fraction is what SGLang keeps, and Megatron's weights,\n    # gradients and Adam state have to fit in the rest. At TP 2 each GPU carries\n    # half of each role, so 0.55 leaves enough; drop it when NUM_GPUS is 1 and\n    # one device has to hold both roles whole.\n    --sglang-mem-fraction-static \"${SGLANG_MEM_FRACTION}\"\n)\n\n# Held-out scoring, used only by Stage B. slime evaluates once before the first\n# rollout and then every EVAL_INTERVAL rollouts, which gives both the starting\n# pass rate and the curve that says whether training has converged.\n#\n# val and test are evaluated at the same points on purpose. Everything the YAML leaves out still falls back to the\n# command line (eval_config.py:10 DATASET_RUNTIME_SPECS), so temperature,\n# response length and the prompt/label keys are set once, below and above.\nEVAL_ARGS=()\nif [ \"${EVAL_INTERVAL}\" -gt 0 ]; then\n    cat > \"${OUT_DIR}/eval_datasets.yaml\" <<YAML\neval:\n  datasets:\n    - name: et_val\n      path: ${VAL_SPLIT}\n      n_samples_per_eval_prompt: ${N_EVAL_SAMPLES}\n    - name: et_test\n      path: ${TEST_SPLIT}\n      n_samples_per_eval_prompt: ${N_EVAL_SAMPLES_TEST}\nYAML\n    EVAL_ARGS=(\n        --eval-interval \"${EVAL_INTERVAL}\"\n        --eval-config \"${OUT_DIR}/eval_datasets.yaml\"\n        --eval-max-response-len 2048\n        --eval-temperature 1.0\n        --log-passrate\n        --custom-eval-rollout-log-function-path et.eval_log.log_eval_rollout_data\n    )\nfi\n\nMISC_ARGS=(\n    --attention-dropout 0.0\n    --hidden-dropout 0.0\n    --accumulate-allreduce-grads-in-fp32\n    --attention-softmax-in-fp32\n    --attention-backend flash\n    --seed 1234\n)\n\n# --------------------------------------------------------- 3. per-role configs\n# Actor and critic share `args.save` by default, which would make them clobber\n# each other's checkpoints (the critic's output layer is [1, hidden_size], the\n# actor's is [vocab, hidden_size]), so each role gets its own directory.\ncat > \"${OUT_DIR}/megatron_roles_stage_a.yaml\" <<YAML\n# Stage A: \"the previous training run\". The actor resumes from Stage A's\n#              Megatron checkpoint; the critic's backbone comes from the base\n#              model.\n#\n#   resume  -- an interrupted Stage B being continued. Both roles load Stage B's\n#              own checkpoints, optimizer state included, and the run continues\n#              from the last saved rollout. The first attempt's log is kept,\n#              not overwritten (see the STAGE_B_LOG choice below).\nSTAGE_B_RESUME=0\nif [ -f \"${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_actor/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt\" ] \\\n   && [ -f \"${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_critic/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt\" ]; then\n    STAGE_B_RESUME=1\nfi\n\nif [ \"${STAGE_B_RESUME}\" = \"1\" ]; then\n    STAGE_B_ACTOR_LOAD=\"${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_actor\"\n    STAGE_B_CRITIC_LOAD=\"${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_critic\"\nelse\n    STAGE_B_ACTOR_LOAD=\"${CKPT_ROOT}/actor\"\n    STAGE_B_CRITIC_LOAD=\"${MODEL_DIR}\"\nfi\n\ncat > \"${OUT_DIR}/megatron_roles_stage_b.yaml\" <<YAML\n# Stage B, $([ \"${STAGE_B_RESUME}\" = \"1\" ] && echo \"resumed from its own checkpoints\" || echo \"entered fresh after a reload\").\nmegatron:\n  - name: stage-b-actor\n    role: actor\n    overrides:\n      load: ${STAGE_B_ACTOR_LOAD}\n      save: ${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_actor\n  - name: stage-b-critic\n    role: critic\n    overrides:\n      load: ${STAGE_B_CRITIC_LOAD}\n      save: ${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_critic\nYAML\n\n# ------------------------------------------------------------------- 4. ray\nexport PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1\n\nray start --head \\\n    --node-ip-address 127.0.0.1 \\\n    --port \"${RAY_PORT}\" \\\n    --num-gpus \"${NUM_GPUS}\" \\\n    --disable-usage-stats \\\n    --dashboard-host 127.0.0.1 \\\n    --dashboard-port \"${DASH_PORT}\" \\\n    --temp-dir \"${RAY_TMP}\"\ntrap 'ray stop --force >/dev/null 2>&1 || true' EXIT\n\n# `|| true` on the whole pipeline, not decoration: under `pipefail` a `grep`\n# that matches nothing fails the pipeline, so on a host with no NVLink -- or in\n# a container holding a single GPU, where the topology matrix has no peer links\n# to report -- `set -e` would kill the script here. Silently: this sits between\n# `ray start` and the first echo of Stage A, so the log just stops.\nNVLINK_COUNT=\"$(nvidia-smi topo -m 2>/dev/null | grep -o 'NV[0-9][0-9]*' | wc -l || true)\"\nHAS_NVLINK=0\n[ \"${NVLINK_COUNT:-0}\" -gt 0 ] && HAS_NVLINK=1\n\nRUNTIME_ENV_JSON=\"{\n  \\\"env_vars\\\": {\n    \\\"PYTHONPATH\\\": \\\"/root/Megatron-LM/:${SLIME_HOME}:${WS}\\\",\n    \\\"CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS\\\": \\\"1\\\",\n    \\\"NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE\\\": \\\"${HAS_NVLINK}\\\",\n    \\\"ET_DATA_ROOT\\\": \\\"${ET_DATA_ROOT}\\\",\n    \\\"ET_EVAL_DUMP_DIR\\\": \\\"${OUT_DIR}/eval_episodes\\\",\n    \\\"ET_SCRATCH\\\": \\\"${ET_SCRATCH}\\\",\n    \\\"ET_MAX_TURNS\\\": \\\"${ET_MAX_TURNS}\\\",\n    \\\"ET_MAX_NEW_TOKENS\\\": \\\"${ET_MAX_NEW_TOKENS}\\\",\n    \\\"ET_CMD_TIMEOUT\\\": \\\"${ET_CMD_TIMEOUT}\\\",\n    \\\"ET_MAX_OBS_CHARS\\\": \\\"${ET_MAX_OBS_CHARS}\\\"\n  }\n}\"\n\nsubmit() {   # submit <log-file> <extra args...>\n    local log=\"$1\"; shift\n    # The entrypoint is an absolute path on purpose: `ray job submit` does not\n    # run it in this shell's directory but in the cwd of the Ray head (here\n    # /workspace, since no `working_dir` is uploaded), so a bare `train.py`\n    # would not be found. Running ${SLIME_HOME}/train.py puts the bundled slime\n    # tree on the driver's sys.path[0]; the ray workers get it from ${SLIME_HOME}\n    # on PYTHONPATH (RUNTIME_ENV_JSON above), ahead of the image's install.\n    ray job submit \\\n        --address \"http://127.0.0.1:${DASH_PORT}\" \\\n        --runtime-env-json \"${RUNTIME_ENV_JSON}\" \\\n        -- python3 \"${SLIME_HOME}/train.py\" \\\n        --actor-num-nodes 1 \\\n        --actor-num-gpus-per-node \"${NUM_GPUS}\" \\\n        --colocate \\\n        --hf-checkpoint \"${MODEL_DIR}\" \\\n        \"${MODEL_ARGS[@]}\" \\\n        \"${ROLLOUT_ARGS[@]}\" \\\n        \"${PPO_ARGS[@]}\" \\\n        \"${PERF_ARGS[@]}\" \\\n        \"${OPTIMIZER_ARGS[@]}\" \\\n        \"${SGLANG_ARGS[@]}\" \\\n        \"${MISC_ARGS[@]}\" \\\n        \"$@\" 2>&1 | tee \"${log}\"\n}\n\n# Ray forwards actor stdout to the job driver, but keep the raw worker logs too:\n# the per-step metrics are emitted by the train actors, not by the driver.\ncollect_worker_logs() {   # collect_worker_logs <tag>\n    # Two statements, not one: `local a=.. b=..` expands every word before it\n    # assigns any of them, so referring to ${tag} on the same line would read\n    # it while it is still unset -- fatal under `set -u`.\n    local tag=\"$1\"\n    local dst=\"${OUT_DIR}/${tag}_worker_logs\"\n    mkdir -p \"${dst}\"\n    grep -rl \"critic-step\" \"${RAY_TMP}\"/session_*/logs/ 2>/dev/null | while read -r f; do\n        cp -f \"${f}\" \"${dst}/$(basename \"$(dirname \"${f}\")\")_$(basename \"${f}\")\" 2>/dev/null || true\n    done\n}\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 5. stage A\necho\necho \"############ Stage A: the previous training run ############\"\n# SKIP_STAGE_A=1 reuses a checkpoint an earlier invocation already wrote, for\n# re-running the long Stage B after an interruption. Off by default, and\n# refuses to be silently wrong: with no checkpoint there, Stage A runs anyway.\nif [ \"${SKIP_STAGE_A:-0}\" = \"1\" ] && [ -f \"${CKPT_ROOT}/actor/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt\" ]; then\n    echo \"SKIP_STAGE_A=1 and ${CKPT_ROOT}/actor already holds a checkpoint -- reusing it.\"\nelse\n    submit \"${OUT_DIR}/stage_a.log\" \\\n        --megatron-config-path \"${OUT_DIR}/megatron_roles_stage_a.yaml\" \\\n        --load \"${MODEL_DIR}\" \\\n        --save \"${CKPT_ROOT}/actor\" \\\n        --save-interval 1 \\\n        --num-rollout \"${NUM_ROLLOUTS}\" \\\n        --num-critic-only-steps 0\n    collect_worker_logs stage_a\nfi\n\necho\necho \"checkpoint written by Stage A:\"\nls -1 \"${CKPT_ROOT}/actor\" 2>/dev/null || true\ntest -f \"${CKPT_ROOT}/actor/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt\" || {\n    echo \"FATAL: Stage A did not produce a resumable Megatron checkpoint.\" >&2\n    exit 1\n}\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 6. stage B\necho\necho \"############ Stage B: reload, then critic warmup ############\"\n# --save-interval has to be set because --save is: Megatron's validate_args\n# asserts the two go together. With STAGE_B_SAVE_INTERVAL=0 it is set far\n# larger than the number of rollouts Stage B takes, so Stage B measures the\n# reload and writes nothing -- the only checkpoint the short reproduction needs\n# is the one Stage A already produced.\n#\n# --override-opt-param-scheduler is what lets Stage B be longer than Stage A.\n# slime derives `train_iters` from --num-rollout (model.py:203) and Megatron\n# stores the resulting LR/weight-decay horizons in the checkpoint, then asserts\n# on reload that the new arguments imply the same ones (\"total number of\n# iterations do not match\"). The flag says \"use the command line, not the\n# checkpoint\", which is exactly right here: Stage B is a new training run that\n# happens to start from Stage A's weights, not a resumption of Stage A.\nSTAGE_B_ARGS=(\n    --megatron-config-path \"${OUT_DIR}/megatron_roles_stage_b.yaml\"\n    --load \"${STAGE_B_ACTOR_LOAD}\"\n    --save \"${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_actor\"\n    --save-interval \"$([ \"${STAGE_B_SAVE_INTERVAL}\" -gt 0 ] && echo \"${STAGE_B_SAVE_INTERVAL}\" || echo 1000)\"\n    --override-opt-param-scheduler\n    --num-rollout \"${NUM_ROLLOUTS_B}\"\n    --num-critic-only-steps \"${NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS}\"\n)\n\nSTAGE_B_LOG=\"${OUT_DIR}/stage_b.log\"\nif [ \"${STAGE_B_RESUME}\" = \"1\" ]; then\n    # The first attempt's log holds the warmup window that the value-loss\n    # verdict is read from, so a resume must not overwrite it.\n    n=1\n    while [ -e \"${OUT_DIR}/stage_b_resume_${n}.log\" ]; do n=$((n + 1)); done\n    STAGE_B_LOG=\"${OUT_DIR}/stage_b_resume_${n}.log\"\n    echo \"resuming Stage B from ${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_{actor,critic}\" \\\n         \"(iteration $(cat \"${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_critic/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt\")); log -> ${STAGE_B_LOG}\"\n    # --start-rollout-id is deliberately NOT passed here. slime takes the start\n    # id from the *critic*'s loaded checkpoint when a critic is in play\n    # (placement_group.py:212), and Stage B saves at `iteration = rollout_id`,\n    # so omitting it resumes at exactly the rollout after the last saved one.\nelse\n    # --start-rollout-id 0 pins the warmup window: without it the start id is\n    # inferred from whichever checkpoint the critic loaded, and on a fresh\n    # Stage B the critic loads a plain HF directory (iteration 0).\n    STAGE_B_ARGS+=(--start-rollout-id 0)\nfi\n\nsubmit \"${STAGE_B_LOG}\" \"${STAGE_B_ARGS[@]}\" \"${EVAL_ARGS[@]+\"${EVAL_ARGS[@]}\"}\"\ncollect_worker_logs stage_b\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 7. verdict\necho\necho \"############ critic warmup value loss ############\"\npython3 \"${WS}/tools/parse_value_loss.py\" \\\n    \"${OUT_DIR}/stage_b.log\" \\\n    --warmup-steps \"${CRITIC_WARMUP_STEPS}\" \\\n    --out \"${OUT_DIR}/stage_b_value_loss.json\"\n\npython3 \"${WS}/tools/parse_value_loss.py\" \\\n    \"${OUT_DIR}/stage_a.log\" \\\n    --out \"${OUT_DIR}/stage_a_value_loss.json\" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true\n\necho\necho \"artifacts in ${OUT_DIR}:\"\nls -1 \"${OUT_DIR}\"\n", "numLines": 517, "startLine": 1, "totalLines": 517}}

#!/bin/bash
#
# Multi-Turn PPO on Endless Terminals with Qwen3-1.7B, on slime v0.3.2.
#
# The run has two stages:
#
#   Stage A -- "the previous training run".  A real PPO rollout (actor + critic)
#              starting from the base HF model, which saves a Megatron
#              checkpoint for both roles.
#
#   Stage B -- "the model was reloaded".  The actor genuinely resumes from
#              Stage A's Megatron checkpoint (weights *and* optimizer state).
#              The critic's backbone is reloaded from the base model.  Stage B
#              opens with NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS critic-only rollouts (the
#              warmup window) and then trains actor and critic jointly.
#
# The full slime source tree is bundled in the workspace (slime/) and is the
# copy that runs -- this script puts it ahead of the image's install on
# PYTHONPATH, so editing slime/ here is what takes effect, with nothing to
# install first.
#
# NOTE ON A SHARED HOST: unlike slime's own example scripts this one never runs
# `pkill -9 ray / pkill -9 python / ray stop --force` on entry.  It is meant to
# run inside its own container, and it brings up a private Ray head on a
# non-default port with a private temp dir.

set -euo pipefail

WS="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" &>/dev/null && pwd)"

# The container runs as root while /workspace is a bind mount owned by whoever
# checked the case out, so any .pyc written here lands root-owned in their tree
# -- and `importlib` copies the *source* file's mode onto the .pyc, so a 600
# source yields a 600 root-owned file that even the owner cannot read, and
# `cp -r` of the case fails. Nothing here benefits from a bytecode cache.
export PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1

MODEL_DIR="${MODEL_DIR:-${WS}/Qwen3-1.7B}"
ET_SRC="${ET_SRC:-${WS}/endless-terminals}"
SLIME_HOME="${SLIME_HOME:-${WS}/slime}"
OUT_DIR="${OUT_DIR:-${WS}/outputs}"
CKPT_ROOT="${CKPT_ROOT:-/ckpt}"

# Endless Terminals sandbox knobs; also forwarded into the Ray workers, which
# read them at import time in et/rollout.py.
#
# These must NOT live under /dev/shm: it is mounted noexec in the training
# image, and many tasks' verifiers assert os.access(path, os.X_OK), which is
# False there even at mode 755.
export ET_DATA_ROOT="${ET_DATA_ROOT:-/tmp/et_prompts}"
export ET_SCRATCH="${ET_SCRATCH:-/tmp/et_episodes}"
export ET_MAX_TURNS="${ET_MAX_TURNS:-6}"
export ET_MAX_NEW_TOKENS="${ET_MAX_NEW_TOKENS:-384}"
export ET_CMD_TIMEOUT="${ET_CMD_TIMEOUT:-20}"
export ET_MAX_OBS_CHARS="${ET_MAX_OBS_CHARS:-1200}"

NUM_GPUS="${NUM_GPUS:-2}"
TP_SIZE="${TP_SIZE:-2}"
SGLANG_MEM_FRACTION="${SGLANG_MEM_FRACTION:-0.55}"
# Rollouts per stage. Both stages use the same count on purpose, and must:
# slime derives `train_iters` from `--num-rollout` (model.py:203) and Megatron
# stores the resulting LR/weight-decay horizons inside the checkpoint, then
# asserts on reload that they match the ones the new arguments imply
# ("total number of iterations do not match"). Giving Stage B a different
# rollout count than Stage A would trip that assert before any training runs.
# In Stage A these rollouts are ordinary PPO; Stage B opens with
# NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS critic-only rollouts -- the warmup window -- and then
# trains actor and critic jointly for the rest.
NUM_ROLLOUTS="${NUM_ROLLOUTS:-2}"
# Stage B is the long one: critic warmup followed by joint PPO, trained until
# the validation pass rate stops moving. It no longer has to match Stage A's
# rollout count -- see --override-opt-param-scheduler at the submit site.
NUM_ROLLOUTS_B="${NUM_ROLLOUTS_B:-${NUM_ROLLOUTS}}"
# Rollouts at the start of Stage B in which only the critic trains. This is the
# warmup window the incident was reported against, and the window in which the
# value loss is measured.
NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS="${NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS:-${NUM_ROLLOUTS_B}}"

# Episodes per rollout = ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE x N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT; optimizer
# steps per rollout = that, divided by GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE.
ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE="${ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE:-8}"
N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT="${N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT:-2}"
GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE="${GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE:-8}"
LR="${LR:-1e-6}"

# How many leading critic optimizer steps the reported warmup statistics cover.
# Derived rather than guessed, because once Stage B runs past the critic-only
# phase the two are no longer the same thing: averaging the value loss over all
# of a 30-rollout Stage B measures mostly a critic that has already been
# trained, which is not what "warmup value loss" names and not what the
# incident was about.
CRITIC_WARMUP_STEPS=$(( NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS * ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE * N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT / GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE ))
[ "${CRITIC_WARMUP_STEPS}" -gt 0 ] || CRITIC_WARMUP_STEPS=1

# Held-out evaluation during Stage B. 0 disables it, which is what the short
# value-loss-only reproduction wants.
#
# val and test get different sample budgets. val only has to say *when* the
# curve flattens, so 2 samples x 150 tasks is enough; test carries the
# end-to-end claim and is compared per task, where the useful quantity is each
# task's success *rate*, which 1 or 2 samples cannot resolve at all.
EVAL_INTERVAL="${EVAL_INTERVAL:-0}"
N_EVAL_SAMPLES="${N_EVAL_SAMPLES:-2}"
N_EVAL_SAMPLES_TEST="${N_EVAL_SAMPLES_TEST:-4}"

# How often Stage B checkpoints. Trained to convergence, Stage B runs for well
# over an hour, which on a shared host is long enough to be interrupted -- two
# runs of this case were killed from outside the container mid-training, once
# with SIGTERM and once with SIGKILL. So Stage B saves as it goes and a second
# invocation picks up where the first stopped, instead of starting the hour
# again. 0 disables it, which is what the short value-loss-only reproduction
# wants: it writes nothing and measures only the reload.
STAGE_B_SAVE_INTERVAL="${STAGE_B_SAVE_INTERVAL:-0}"

RAY_PORT="${RAY_PORT:-6479}"
DASH_PORT="${DASH_PORT:-8277}"
RAY_TMP="${RAY_TMP:-/tmp/ray_ppo}"

mkdir -p "${OUT_DIR}" "${CKPT_ROOT}" "${ET_SCRATCH}"

# --------------------------------------------------------- 0. the slime source
# The full slime source tree is bundled in the workspace (${SLIME_HOME}) and is
# put ahead of the image's editable install on PYTHONPATH below, so it is the
# copy that trains -- there is nothing to install first.
test -f "${SLIME_HOME}/train.py" || {
    echo "FATAL: bundled slime source not found at ${SLIME_HOME}" >&2
    exit 1
}

# ------------------------------------------------------- 1. the prompt dataset
# prepare.sh ships the already-built dataset (transpiled + validated + split) at
# ${WS}/et_prompts. Seed ET_DATA_ROOT from it so the build below is skipped: the
# 2492->1489 admission is environment-fixed and reproducible, so there is no need
# to re-run the ~40min transpile+validate pass (and ET_SRC is never read). The
# copy lands in a writable, exec-capable dir (ET_DATA_ROOT defaults to /tmp) --
# the bundled tree under /workspace may be a root-owned bind mount. If the
# prebuilt payload is absent, fall through to building from ET_SRC as before.
if [ ! -s "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals.jsonl" ] && [ -s "${WS}/et_prompts/endless_terminals.jsonl" ]; then
    echo "=== seeding ET_DATA_ROOT from prebuilt ${WS}/et_prompts (skipping transpile+validate) ==="
    mkdir -p "${ET_DATA_ROOT}"
    cp -a "${WS}/et_prompts/." "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/"
fi
if [ ! -s "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals.jsonl" ]; then
    echo "=== transpiling + validating the Endless Terminals tasks ==="
    (cd "${WS}" && python3 -m et.build_dataset --src "${ET_SRC}" --out "${ET_DATA_ROOT}") \
        2>&1 | tee "${OUT_DIR}/build_dataset.log"
fi
# Deliberately not silenced. A report that is quietly 0 bytes is worse than one
# that is loudly absent: it reads as "every task was rejected" to anyone who
# opens it later, and that has happened here more than once.
copy_artifact() {   # copy_artifact <src>
    local src="$1" dst="${OUT_DIR}/$(basename "$1")"
    if ! cp -f "${src}" "${dst}"; then
        echo "WARNING: could not copy ${src} into ${OUT_DIR}" >&2
    elif [ ! -s "${dst}" ] && [ -s "${src}" ]; then
        echo "WARNING: ${dst} came out empty although ${src} is not" >&2
    fi
}
copy_artifact "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/validation_report.json"
N_PROMPTS="$(wc -l < "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals.jsonl")"
echo "prompt set: ${N_PROMPTS} validated Endless Terminals tasks"
if [ "${N_PROMPTS}" -lt 4 ]; then
    echo "FATAL: too few tasks survived validation to train on." >&2
    exit 1
fi

# Train on one part of the task set and measure on another. The split is a pure
# function of the admitted list and a fixed seed, so every run trains and is
# scored on exactly the same tasks -- otherwise a comparison between runs is
# partly measuring which tasks each one happened to get.
if [ ! -s "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals_train.jsonl" ]; then
    (cd "${WS}" && python3 -m et.make_splits --prompts "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals.jsonl")
fi
copy_artifact "${ET_DATA_ROOT}/splits.json"
TRAIN_SPLIT="${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals_train.jsonl"
VAL_SPLIT="${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals_val.jsonl"
TEST_SPLIT="${ET_DATA_ROOT}/endless_terminals_test.jsonl"
printf 'splits: train %s / val %s / test %s\n' \
    "$(wc -l < "${TRAIN_SPLIT}")" "$(wc -l < "${VAL_SPLIT}")" "$(wc -l < "${TEST_SPLIT}")"

# ------------------------------------------------------------- 2. shared args
source "${WS}/configs/model_args.sh"

ROLLOUT_ARGS=(
    --prompt-data "${TRAIN_SPLIT}"
    --input-key prompt
    --label-key label
    --rollout-shuffle
    --rollout-batch-size "${ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE}"
    --n-samples-per-prompt "${N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT}"
    --rollout-max-response-len 2048
    --rollout-temperature 1.0
    --global-batch-size "${GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE}"
    --balance-data
    # The multi-turn terminal loop and its pytest-based episode reward.
    --custom-generate-function-path et.rollout.generate
    --custom-rm-path et.rollout.reward_func
)

PPO_ARGS=(
    --advantage-estimator ppo   # -> args.use_critic
    --gamma 1.0
    --lambd 1.0
    --eps-clip 0.2
    --value-clip 0.2
    --kl-coef 0.0               # no reference model, hence no --ref-load and
    --entropy-coef 0.0          # no HF -> torch_dist conversion step
)

PERF_ARGS=(
    --tensor-model-parallel-size "${TP_SIZE}"
    --pipeline-model-parallel-size 1
    --context-parallel-size 1
    --recompute-granularity full
    --recompute-method uniform
    --recompute-num-layers 1
    --use-dynamic-batch-size
    --max-tokens-per-gpu 8192
)
# Sequence parallelism splits the activations of the non-tensor-parallel ops
# across the TP group, so it is only defined for TP > 1; Megatron asserts on it.
# Spelled as an `if` rather than `[ ... ] && ...`: the latter evaluates to the
# test's status, which under `set -e` ends the script whenever TP_SIZE is 1.
if [ "${TP_SIZE}" -gt 1 ]; then
    PERF_ARGS+=(--sequence-parallel)
fi

OPTIMIZER_ARGS=(
    --optimizer adam
    --lr "${LR}"
    --lr-decay-style constant
    --weight-decay 0.0
    --adam-beta1 0.9
    --adam-beta2 0.95
)

SGLANG_ARGS=(
    --rollout-num-gpus-per-engine "${NUM_GPUS}"
    # Colocated: this fraction is what SGLang keeps, and Megatron's weights,
    # gradients and Adam state have to fit in the rest. At TP 2 each GPU carries
    # half of each role, so 0.55 leaves enough; drop it when NUM_GPUS is 1 and
    # one device has to hold both roles whole.
    --sglang-mem-fraction-static "${SGLANG_MEM_FRACTION}"
)

# Held-out scoring, used only by Stage B. slime evaluates once before the first
# rollout and then every EVAL_INTERVAL rollouts, which gives both the starting
# pass rate and the curve that says whether training has converged.
#
# val and test are evaluated at the same points on purpose. The convergence
# *decision* is read off val; test is reported only at the final point, and
# evaluating it throughout costs generation but no statistical validity, since
# nothing about the run is conditioned on it.
#
# Spelled as an --eval-config YAML rather than --eval-prompt-data because the
# two splits need different sample counts, and --n-samples-per-eval-prompt is
# one global number. Everything the YAML leaves out still falls back to the
# command line (eval_config.py:10 DATASET_RUNTIME_SPECS), so temperature,
# response length and the prompt/label keys are set once, below and above.
EVAL_ARGS=()
if [ "${EVAL_INTERVAL}" -gt 0 ]; then
    cat > "${OUT_DIR}/eval_datasets.yaml" <<YAML
eval:
  datasets:
    - name: et_val
      path: ${VAL_SPLIT}
      n_samples_per_eval_prompt: ${N_EVAL_SAMPLES}
    - name: et_test
      path: ${TEST_SPLIT}
      n_samples_per_eval_prompt: ${N_EVAL_SAMPLES_TEST}
YAML
    EVAL_ARGS=(
        --eval-interval "${EVAL_INTERVAL}"
        --eval-config "${OUT_DIR}/eval_datasets.yaml"
        --eval-max-response-len 2048
        --eval-temperature 1.0
        --log-passrate
        --custom-eval-rollout-log-function-path et.eval_log.log_eval_rollout_data
    )
fi

MISC_ARGS=(
    --attention-dropout 0.0
    --hidden-dropout 0.0
    --accumulate-allreduce-grads-in-fp32
    --attention-softmax-in-fp32
    --attention-backend flash
    --seed 1234
)

# --------------------------------------------------------- 3. per-role configs
# Actor and critic share `args.save` by default, which would make them clobber
# each other's checkpoints (the critic's output layer is [1, hidden_size], the
# actor's is [vocab, hidden_size]), so each role gets its own directory.
cat > "${OUT_DIR}/megatron_roles_stage_a.yaml" <<YAML
# Stage A: "the previous training run". Both roles start from the base model.
megatron:
  - name: stage-a-actor
    role: actor
    overrides:
      load: ${MODEL_DIR}
      save: ${CKPT_ROOT}/actor
  - name: stage-a-critic
    role: critic
    overrides:
      load: ${MODEL_DIR}
      save: ${CKPT_ROOT}/critic
YAML

# Stage B can be entered two ways, and they are not the same event.
#
#   fresh   -- "the model was reloaded". The actor resumes from Stage A's
#              Megatron checkpoint; the critic's backbone comes from the base
#              model.
#
#   resume  -- an interrupted Stage B being continued. Both roles load Stage B's
#              own checkpoints, optimizer state included, and the run continues
#              from the last saved rollout. The first attempt's log is kept,
#              not overwritten (see the STAGE_B_LOG choice below).
STAGE_B_RESUME=0
if [ -f "${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_actor/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt" ] \
   && [ -f "${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_critic/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt" ]; then
    STAGE_B_RESUME=1
fi

if [ "${STAGE_B_RESUME}" = "1" ]; then
    STAGE_B_ACTOR_LOAD="${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_actor"
    STAGE_B_CRITIC_LOAD="${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_critic"
else
    STAGE_B_ACTOR_LOAD="${CKPT_ROOT}/actor"
    STAGE_B_CRITIC_LOAD="${MODEL_DIR}"
fi

cat > "${OUT_DIR}/megatron_roles_stage_b.yaml" <<YAML
# Stage B, $([ "${STAGE_B_RESUME}" = "1" ] && echo "resumed from its own checkpoints" || echo "entered fresh after a reload").
megatron:
  - name: stage-b-actor
    role: actor
    overrides:
      load: ${STAGE_B_ACTOR_LOAD}
      save: ${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_actor
  - name: stage-b-critic
    role: critic
    overrides:
      load: ${STAGE_B_CRITIC_LOAD}
      save: ${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_critic
YAML

# ------------------------------------------------------------------- 4. ray
export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1

ray start --head \
    --node-ip-address 127.0.0.1 \
    --port "${RAY_PORT}" \
    --num-gpus "${NUM_GPUS}" \
    --disable-usage-stats \
    --dashboard-host 127.0.0.1 \
    --dashboard-port "${DASH_PORT}" \
    --temp-dir "${RAY_TMP}"
trap 'ray stop --force >/dev/null 2>&1 || true' EXIT

# `|| true` on the whole pipeline, not decoration: under `pipefail` a `grep`
# that matches nothing fails the pipeline, so on a host with no NVLink -- or in
# a container holding a single GPU, where the topology matrix has no peer links
# to report -- `set -e` would kill the script here. Silently: this sits between
# `ray start` and the first echo of Stage A, so the log just stops.
NVLINK_COUNT="$(nvidia-smi topo -m 2>/dev/null | grep -o 'NV[0-9][0-9]*' | wc -l || true)"
HAS_NVLINK=0
[ "${NVLINK_COUNT:-0}" -gt 0 ] && HAS_NVLINK=1

RUNTIME_ENV_JSON="{
  \"env_vars\": {
    \"PYTHONPATH\": \"/root/Megatron-LM/:${SLIME_HOME}:${WS}\",
    \"CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS\": \"1\",
    \"NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE\": \"${HAS_NVLINK}\",
    \"ET_DATA_ROOT\": \"${ET_DATA_ROOT}\",
    \"ET_EVAL_DUMP_DIR\": \"${OUT_DIR}/eval_episodes\",
    \"ET_SCRATCH\": \"${ET_SCRATCH}\",
    \"ET_MAX_TURNS\": \"${ET_MAX_TURNS}\",
    \"ET_MAX_NEW_TOKENS\": \"${ET_MAX_NEW_TOKENS}\",
    \"ET_CMD_TIMEOUT\": \"${ET_CMD_TIMEOUT}\",
    \"ET_MAX_OBS_CHARS\": \"${ET_MAX_OBS_CHARS}\"
  }
}"

submit() {   # submit <log-file> <extra args...>
    local log="$1"; shift
    # The entrypoint is an absolute path on purpose: `ray job submit` does not
    # run it in this shell's directory but in the cwd of the Ray head (here
    # /workspace, since no `working_dir` is uploaded), so a bare `train.py`
    # would not be found. Running ${SLIME_HOME}/train.py puts the bundled slime
    # tree on the driver's sys.path[0]; the ray workers get it from ${SLIME_HOME}
    # on PYTHONPATH (RUNTIME_ENV_JSON above), ahead of the image's install.
    ray job submit \
        --address "http://127.0.0.1:${DASH_PORT}" \
        --runtime-env-json "${RUNTIME_ENV_JSON}" \
        -- python3 "${SLIME_HOME}/train.py" \
        --actor-num-nodes 1 \
        --actor-num-gpus-per-node "${NUM_GPUS}" \
        --colocate \
        --hf-checkpoint "${MODEL_DIR}" \
        "${MODEL_ARGS[@]}" \
        "${ROLLOUT_ARGS[@]}" \
        "${PPO_ARGS[@]}" \
        "${PERF_ARGS[@]}" \
        "${OPTIMIZER_ARGS[@]}" \
        "${SGLANG_ARGS[@]}" \
        "${MISC_ARGS[@]}" \
        "$@" 2>&1 | tee "${log}"
}

# Ray forwards actor stdout to the job driver, but keep the raw worker logs too:
# the per-step metrics are emitted by the train actors, not by the driver.
collect_worker_logs() {   # collect_worker_logs <tag>
    # Two statements, not one: `local a=.. b=..` expands every word before it
    # assigns any of them, so referring to ${tag} on the same line would read
    # it while it is still unset -- fatal under `set -u`.
    local tag="$1"
    local dst="${OUT_DIR}/${tag}_worker_logs"
    mkdir -p "${dst}"
    grep -rl "critic-step" "${RAY_TMP}"/session_*/logs/ 2>/dev/null | while read -r f; do
        cp -f "${f}" "${dst}/$(basename "$(dirname "${f}")")_$(basename "${f}")" 2>/dev/null || true
    done
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 5. stage A
echo
echo "############ Stage A: the previous training run ############"
# SKIP_STAGE_A=1 reuses a checkpoint an earlier invocation already wrote, for
# re-running the long Stage B after an interruption. Off by default, and
# refuses to be silently wrong: with no checkpoint there, Stage A runs anyway.
if [ "${SKIP_STAGE_A:-0}" = "1" ] && [ -f "${CKPT_ROOT}/actor/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt" ]; then
    echo "SKIP_STAGE_A=1 and ${CKPT_ROOT}/actor already holds a checkpoint -- reusing it."
else
    submit "${OUT_DIR}/stage_a.log" \
        --megatron-config-path "${OUT_DIR}/megatron_roles_stage_a.yaml" \
        --load "${MODEL_DIR}" \
        --save "${CKPT_ROOT}/actor" \
        --save-interval 1 \
        --num-rollout "${NUM_ROLLOUTS}" \
        --num-critic-only-steps 0
    collect_worker_logs stage_a
fi

echo
echo "checkpoint written by Stage A:"
ls -1 "${CKPT_ROOT}/actor" 2>/dev/null || true
test -f "${CKPT_ROOT}/actor/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt" || {
    echo "FATAL: Stage A did not produce a resumable Megatron checkpoint." >&2
    exit 1
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 6. stage B
echo
echo "############ Stage B: reload, then critic warmup ############"
# --save-interval has to be set because --save is: Megatron's validate_args
# asserts the two go together. With STAGE_B_SAVE_INTERVAL=0 it is set far
# larger than the number of rollouts Stage B takes, so Stage B measures the
# reload and writes nothing -- the only checkpoint the short reproduction needs
# is the one Stage A already produced.
#
# --override-opt-param-scheduler is what lets Stage B be longer than Stage A.
# slime derives `train_iters` from --num-rollout (model.py:203) and Megatron
# stores the resulting LR/weight-decay horizons in the checkpoint, then asserts
# on reload that the new arguments imply the same ones ("total number of
# iterations do not match"). The flag says "use the command line, not the
# checkpoint", which is exactly right here: Stage B is a new training run that
# happens to start from Stage A's weights, not a resumption of Stage A.
STAGE_B_ARGS=(
    --megatron-config-path "${OUT_DIR}/megatron_roles_stage_b.yaml"
    --load "${STAGE_B_ACTOR_LOAD}"
    --save "${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_actor"
    --save-interval "$([ "${STAGE_B_SAVE_INTERVAL}" -gt 0 ] && echo "${STAGE_B_SAVE_INTERVAL}" || echo 1000)"
    --override-opt-param-scheduler
    --num-rollout "${NUM_ROLLOUTS_B}"
    --num-critic-only-steps "${NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS}"
)

STAGE_B_LOG="${OUT_DIR}/stage_b.log"
if [ "${STAGE_B_RESUME}" = "1" ]; then
    # The first attempt's log holds the warmup window that the value-loss
    # verdict is read from, so a resume must not overwrite it.
    n=1
    while [ -e "${OUT_DIR}/stage_b_resume_${n}.log" ]; do n=$((n + 1)); done
    STAGE_B_LOG="${OUT_DIR}/stage_b_resume_${n}.log"
    echo "resuming Stage B from ${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_{actor,critic}" \
         "(iteration $(cat "${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_critic/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt")); log -> ${STAGE_B_LOG}"
    # --start-rollout-id is deliberately NOT passed here. slime takes the start
    # id from the *critic*'s loaded checkpoint when a critic is in play
    # (placement_group.py:212), and Stage B saves at `iteration = rollout_id`,
    # so omitting it resumes at exactly the rollout after the last saved one.
else
    # --start-rollout-id 0 pins the warmup window: without it the start id is
    # inferred from whichever checkpoint the critic loaded, and on a fresh
    # Stage B the critic loads a plain HF directory (iteration 0).
    STAGE_B_ARGS+=(--start-rollout-id 0)
fi

submit "${STAGE_B_LOG}" "${STAGE_B_ARGS[@]}" "${EVAL_ARGS[@]+"${EVAL_ARGS[@]}"}"
collect_worker_logs stage_b

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 7. verdict
echo
echo "############ critic warmup value loss ############"
python3 "${WS}/tools/parse_value_loss.py" \
    "${OUT_DIR}/stage_b.log" \
    --warmup-steps "${CRITIC_WARMUP_STEPS}" \
    --out "${OUT_DIR}/stage_b_value_loss.json"

python3 "${WS}/tools/parse_value_loss.py" \
    "${OUT_DIR}/stage_a.log" \
    --out "${OUT_DIR}/stage_a_value_loss.json" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

echo
echo "artifacts in ${OUT_DIR}:"
ls -1 "${OUT_DIR}"

282	MISC_ARGS=(
283	    --attention-dropout 0.0
284	    --hidden-dropout 0.0
285	    --accumulate-allreduce-grads-in-fp32
286	    --attention-softmax-in-fp32
287	    --attention-backend flash
288	    --seed 1234
289	)
290	
291	# --------------------------------------------------------- 3. per-role configs
292	# Actor and critic share `args.save` by default, which would make them clobber
293	# each other's checkpoints (the critic's output layer is [1, hidden_size], the
294	# actor's is [vocab, hidden_size]), so each role gets its own directory.
295	cat > "${OUT_DIR}/megatron_roles_stage_a.yaml" <<YAML
296	# Stage A: "the previous training run". Both roles start from the base model.
297	megatron:
298	  - name: stage-a-actor
299	    role: actor
300	    overrides:
301	      load: ${MODEL_DIR}
302	      save: ${CKPT_ROOT}/actor
303	  - name: stage-a-critic
304	    role: critic
305	    overrides:
306	      load: ${MODEL_DIR}
307	      save: ${CKPT_ROOT}/critic
308	YAML
309	
310	# Stage B can be entered two ways, and they are not the same event.
311	#
312	#   fresh   -- "the model was reloaded". The actor resumes from Stage A's
313	#              Megatron checkpoint; the critic's backbone comes from the base
314	#              model.
315	#
316	#   resume  -- an interrupted Stage B being continued. Both roles load Stage B's
317	#              own checkpoints, optimizer state included, and the run continues
318	#              from the last saved rollout. The first attempt's log is kept,
319	#              not overwritten (see the STAGE_B_LOG choice below).
320	STAGE_B_RESUME=0
321	if [ -f "${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_actor/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt" ] \
322	   && [ -f "${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_critic/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt" ]; then
323	    STAGE_B_RESUME=1
324	fi
325	
326	if [ "${STAGE_B_RESUME}" = "1" ]; then
327	    STAGE_B_ACTOR_LOAD="${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_actor"
328	    STAGE_B_CRITIC_LOAD="${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_critic"
329	else
330	    STAGE_B_ACTOR_LOAD="${CKPT_ROOT}/actor"
331	    STAGE_B_CRITIC_LOAD="${MODEL_DIR}"
332	fi
333	
334	cat > "${OUT_DIR}/megatron_roles_stage_b.yaml" <<YAML
335	# Stage B, $([ "${STAGE_B_RESUME}" = "1" ] && echo "resumed from its own checkpoints" || echo "entered fresh after a reload").
336	megatron:
337	  - name: stage-b-actor
338	    role: actor
339	    overrides:
340	      load: ${STAGE_B_ACTOR_LOAD}
341	      save: ${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_actor
342	  - name: stage-b-critic
343	    role: critic
344	    overrides:
345	      load: ${STAGE_B_CRITIC_LOAD}
346	      save: ${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_critic
347	YAML
348	
349	# ------------------------------------------------------------------- 4. ray
350	export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
351	
352	ray start --head \
353	    --node-ip-address 127.0.0.1 \
354	    --port "${RAY_PORT}" \
355	    --num-gpus "${NUM_GPUS}" \
356	    --disable-usage-stats \
357	    --dashboard-host 127.0.0.1 \
358	    --dashboard-port "${DASH_PORT}" \
359	    --temp-dir "${RAY_TMP}"
360	trap 'ray stop --force >/dev/null 2>&1 || true' EXIT
361	
362	# `|| true` on the whole pipeline, not decoration: under `pipefail` a `grep`
363	# that matches nothing fails the pipeline, so on a host with no NVLink -- or in
364	# a container holding a single GPU, where the topology matrix has no peer links
365	# to report -- `set -e` would kill the script here. Silently: this sits between
366	# `ray start` and the first echo of Stage A, so the log just stops.
367	NVLINK_COUNT="$(nvidia-smi topo -m 2>/dev/null | grep -o 'NV[0-9][0-9]*' | wc -l || true)"
368	HAS_NVLINK=0
369	[ "${NVLINK_COUNT:-0}" -gt 0 ] && HAS_NVLINK=1
370	
371	RUNTIME_ENV_JSON="{
372	  \"env_vars\": {
373	    \"PYTHONPATH\": \"/root/Megatron-LM/:${SLIME_HOME}:${WS}\",
374	    \"CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS\": \"1\",
375	    \"NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE\": \"${HAS_NVLINK}\",
376	    \"ET_DATA_ROOT\": \"${ET_DATA_ROOT}\",
377	    \"ET_EVAL_DUMP_DIR\": \"${OUT_DIR}/eval_episodes\",
378	    \"ET_SCRATCH\": \"${ET_SCRATCH}\",
379	    \"ET_MAX_TURNS\": \"${ET_MAX_TURNS}\",
380	    \"ET_MAX_NEW_TOKENS\": \"${ET_MAX_NEW_TOKENS}\",
381	    \"ET_CMD_TIMEOUT\": \"${ET_CMD_TIMEOUT}\",
382	    \"ET_MAX_OBS_CHARS\": \"${ET_MAX_OBS_CHARS}\"
383	  }
384	}"
385	
386	submit() {   # submit <log-file> <extra args...>
387	    local log="$1"; shift
388	    # The entrypoint is an absolute path on purpose: `ray job submit` does not
389	    # run it in this shell's directory but in the cwd of the Ray head (here
390	    # /workspace, since no `working_dir` is uploaded), so a bare `train.py`
391	    # would not be found. Running ${SLIME_HOME}/train.py puts the bundled slime
392	    # tree on the driver's sys.path[0]; the ray workers get it from ${SLIME_HOME}
393	    # on PYTHONPATH (RUNTIME_ENV_JSON above), ahead of the image's install.
394	    ray job submit \
395	        --address "http://127.0.0.1:${DASH_PORT}" \
396	        --runtime-env-json "${RUNTIME_ENV_JSON}" \
397	        -- python3 "${SLIME_HOME}/train.py" \
398	        --actor-num-nodes 1 \
399	        --actor-num-gpus-per-node "${NUM_GPUS}" \
400	        --colocate \
401	        --hf-checkpoint "${MODEL_DIR}" \
402	        "${MODEL_ARGS[@]}" \
403	        "${ROLLOUT_ARGS[@]}" \
404	        "${PPO_ARGS[@]}" \
405	        "${PERF_ARGS[@]}" \
406	        "${OPTIMIZER_ARGS[@]}" \
407	        "${SGLANG_ARGS[@]}" \
408	        "${MISC_ARGS[@]}" \
409	        "$@" 2>&1 | tee "${log}"
410	}
411	
412	# Ray forwards actor stdout to the job driver, but keep the raw worker logs too:
413	# the per-step metrics are emitted by the train actors, not by the driver.
414	collect_worker_logs() {   # collect_worker_logs <tag>
415	    # Two statements, not one: `local a=.. b=..` expands every word before it
416	    # assigns any of them, so referring to ${tag} on the same line would read
417	    # it while it is still unset -- fatal under `set -u`.
418	    local tag="$1"
419	    local dst="${OUT_DIR}/${tag}_worker_logs"
420	    mkdir -p "${dst}"
421	    grep -rl "critic-step" "${RAY_TMP}"/session_*/logs/ 2>/dev/null | while read -r f; do
422	        cp -f "${f}" "${dst}/$(basename "$(dirname "${f}")")_$(basename "${f}")" 2>/dev/null || true
423	    done
424	}
425	
426	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 5. stage A
427	echo
428	echo "############ Stage A: the previous training run ############"
429	# SKIP_STAGE_A=1 reuses a checkpoint an earlier invocation already wrote, for
430	# re-running the long Stage B after an interruption. Off by default, and
431	# refuses to be silently wrong: with no checkpoint there, Stage A runs anyway.
432	if [ "${SKIP_STAGE_A:-0}" = "1" ] && [ -f "${CKPT_ROOT}/actor/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt" ]; then
433	    echo "SKIP_STAGE_A=1 and ${CKPT_ROOT}/actor already holds a checkpoint -- reusing it."
434	else
435	    submit "${OUT_DIR}/stage_a.log" \
436	        --megatron-config-path "${OUT_DIR}/megatron_roles_stage_a.yaml" \
437	        --load "${MODEL_DIR}" \
438	        --save "${CKPT_ROOT}/actor" \
439	        --save-interval 1 \
440	        --num-rollout "${NUM_ROLLOUTS}" \
441	        --num-critic-only-steps 0
442	    collect_worker_logs stage_a
443	fi
444	
445	echo
446	echo "checkpoint written by Stage A:"
447	ls -1 "${CKPT_ROOT}/actor" 2>/dev/null || true
448	test -f "${CKPT_ROOT}/actor/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt" || {
449	    echo "FATAL: Stage A did not produce a resumable Megatron checkpoint." >&2
450	    exit 1
451	}
452	
453	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 6. stage B
454	echo
455	echo "############ Stage B: reload, then critic warmup ############"
456	# --save-interval has to be set because --save is: Megatron's validate_args
457	# asserts the two go together. With STAGE_B_SAVE_INTERVAL=0 it is set far
458	# larger than the number of rollouts Stage B takes, so Stage B measures the
459	# reload and writes nothing -- the only checkpoint the short reproduction needs
460	# is the one Stage A already produced.
461	#
462	# --override-opt-param-scheduler is what lets Stage B be longer than Stage A.
463	# slime derives `train_iters` from --num-rollout (model.py:203) and Megatron
464	# stores the resulting LR/weight-decay horizons in the checkpoint, then asserts
465	# on reload that the new arguments imply the same ones ("total number of
466	# iterations do not match"). The flag says "use the command line, not the
467	# checkpoint", which is exactly right here: Stage B is a new training run that
468	# happens to start from Stage A's weights, not a resumption of Stage A.
469	STAGE_B_ARGS=(
470	    --megatron-config-path "${OUT_DIR}/megatron_roles_stage_b.yaml"
471	    --load "${STAGE_B_ACTOR_LOAD}"
472	    --save "${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_actor"
473	    --save-interval "$([ "${STAGE_B_SAVE_INTERVAL}" -gt 0 ] && echo "${STAGE_B_SAVE_INTERVAL}" || echo 1000)"
474	    --override-opt-param-scheduler
475	    --num-rollout "${NUM_ROLLOUTS_B}"
476	    --num-critic-only-steps "${NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS}"
477	)
478	
479	STAGE_B_LOG="${OUT_DIR}/stage_b.log"
480	if [ "${STAGE_B_RESUME}" = "1" ]; then
481	    # The first attempt's log holds the warmup window that the value-loss
482	    # verdict is read from, so a resume must not overwrite it.
483	    n=1
484	    while [ -e "${OUT_DIR}/stage_b_resume_${n}.log" ]; do n=$((n + 1)); done
485	    STAGE_B_LOG="${OUT_DIR}/stage_b_resume_${n}.log"
486	    echo "resuming Stage B from ${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_{actor,critic}" \
487	         "(iteration $(cat "${CKPT_ROOT}/stage_b_critic/latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt")); log -> ${STAGE_B_LOG}"
488	    # --start-rollout-id is deliberately NOT passed here. slime takes the start
489	    # id from the *critic*'s loaded checkpoint when a critic is in play
490	    # (placement_group.py:212), and Stage B saves at `iteration = rollout_id`,
491	    # so omitting it resumes at exactly the rollout after the last saved one.
492	else
493	    # --start-rollout-id 0 pins the warmup window: without it the start id is
494	    # inferred from whichever checkpoint the critic loaded, and on a fresh
495	    # Stage B the critic loads a plain HF directory (iteration 0).
496	    STAGE_B_ARGS+=(--start-rollout-id 0)
497	fi
498	
499	submit "${STAGE_B_LOG}" "${STAGE_B_ARGS[@]}" "${EVAL_ARGS[@]+"${EVAL_ARGS[@]}"}"
500	collect_worker_logs stage_b
501	
502	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 7. verdict
503	echo
504	echo "############ critic warmup value loss ############"
505	python3 "${WS}/tools/parse_value_loss.py" \
506	    "${OUT_DIR}/stage_b.log" \
507	    --warmup-steps "${CRITIC_WARMUP_STEPS}" \
508	    --out "${OUT_DIR}/stage_b_value_loss.json"
509	
510	python3 "${WS}/tools/parse_value_loss.py" \
511	    "${OUT_DIR}/stage_a.log" \
512	    --out "${OUT_DIR}/stage_a_value_loss.json" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
513	
514	echo
515	echo "artifacts in ${OUT_DIR}:"
516	ls -1 "${OUT_DIR}"
517

def loss_function(
    args: Namespace,
    batch: RolloutBatch,
    num_microbatches: int,
    step_global_batch_size: int,
    logits: torch.Tensor,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, int | torch.Tensor, dict[str, list[str] | torch.Tensor]]:
    """Dispatch to the configured loss and rescale for Megatron integration.

    Selects one of "policy_loss", "value_loss", "sft_loss", or a custom loss
    function based on `args.loss_type`, computes the loss and metrics, then
    rescales the loss by micro-batch and parallelism factors to integrate with
    Megatron's gradient accumulation.

    Args:
        args: Configuration specifying `loss_type`, `calculate_per_token_loss`,
            and optionally `custom_loss_function_path`.
        batch: Mini-batch with "loss_masks", "response_lengths", and other
            keys required by the selected loss function.
        num_microbatches: Number of gradient accumulation steps.
        step_global_batch_size: Sample count for the current training step
            (total across DP). Replaces the legacy ``args.global_batch_size``
            fallback so the train side stops depending on "every DP rank holds
            the same N samples".
        logits: Model outputs (policy or value head).

    Returns:
        Tuple of `(scaled_loss, normalizer, logging_dict)` where:
        - `scaled_loss` is the loss tensor (scalar) rescaled for Megatron.
        - `normalizer` is `num_tokens` (scalar tensor) if
          `args.calculate_per_token_loss` is True, else `1` (int).
        - `logging_dict` has keys "keys" (list of str metric names) and
          "values" (1D tensor: [count, metric1, metric2, ...]).
    """
    num_tokens = sum([torch.clamp_min(loss_mask.sum(), 1) for loss_mask in batch["loss_masks"]])

    sum_of_sample_mean = get_sum_of_sample_mean(
        batch["total_lengths"],
        batch["response_lengths"],
        batch["loss_masks"],
        batch["rollout_mask_sums"],
        args.calculate_per_token_loss,
    )

    match args.loss_type:
        case "policy_loss":
            func = policy_loss_function
        case "value_loss":
            func = value_loss_function
        case "sft_loss":
            func = sft_loss_function
        case "custom_loss":
            func = load_function(args.custom_loss_function_path)
        case _:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown loss type: {args.loss_type}")

    if args.recompute_loss_function:
        loss, log = checkpoint(func, args, batch, logits, sum_of_sample_mean, use_reentrant=False)
    else:
        loss, log = func(args, batch, logits, sum_of_sample_mean)

584	def vanilla_gae(
585	    rewards: torch.Tensor,
586	    values: torch.Tensor,
587	    gamma: float,
588	    lambd: float,
589	):
590	    B, T = rewards.shape
591	    device = rewards.device
592	    dtype = rewards.dtype
593	
594	    lastgaelam = torch.zeros(B, device=device, dtype=dtype)
595	    adv_rev = []
596	
597	    for t in reversed(range(T)):
598	        next_value = values[:, t + 1] if t < T - 1 else 0.0
599	        delta = rewards[:, t] + gamma * next_value - values[:, t]
600	        lastgaelam = delta + gamma * lambd * lastgaelam
601	        adv_rev.append(lastgaelam)
602	
603	    full_advantages = torch.stack(adv_rev[::-1], dim=1)  # [B, max_len]
604	    full_returns = full_advantages + values  # [B, max_len]
605	    return full_advantages, full_returns

steps.message: The full run.sh picture changes what the graded fresh run actually is: Stage A = 2 rollouts joint PPO from base (`--num-critic-only-steps 0`, random-init value head!), Stage B = 2 rollouts *all* critic-only, no evals — the graded artifact is the warmup value loss plus structural checks. Before finalizing the fix, enumerating every deliberate workspace deviation from upstream:
steps.reasoning_content:
Now I understand the current run.sh structure fully. The fresh graded run will be:
- Stage A: 2 rollouts, num-critic-only-steps 0 (ordinary PPO, both roles from base HF model)
- Stage B: 2 rollouts, num-critic-only-steps 2 → ALL rollouts critic-only
- EVAL_INTERVAL=0 → no held-out eval in the fresh run
- The verdict artifact: stage_b_value_loss.json from parse_value_loss.py with --warmup-steps

Wait — so the graded fresh run measures the **critic warmup value loss**! The "incident" this case is staged around is the value loss during the critic-only warmup window. Let me re-read: "critic warmup value loss" is the artifact the script prints at the end.

So the case story: Stage A = previous training run (real PPO, 2 rollouts). Stage B = "the model was reloaded" — actor resumes from Stage A's checkpoint, critic backbone reloaded from base model, opens with NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS critic-only rollouts (warmup window) during which the value loss is measured. The incident was reported against the warmup window.

The frozen logs I analyzed were from a 30-rollout Stage B run with eval_interval=5 (the historical snapshot used different env overrides: NUM_ROLLOUTS_B=30, NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS=3, EVAL_INTERVAL=5, TP_SIZE=1, ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE=64, N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT=2, GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE=64, LR=2e-6...). Wait, actually let me check: frozen run had rollout-batch-size 64, global-batch-size 64, lr 2e-6. Current defaults: ROLLOUT_BATCH_SIZE=8, N_SAMPLES_PER_PROMPT=2, GLOBAL_BATCH_SIZE=8, LR=1e-6. So the historical run used different env var values. Fine — the historical snapshot ran with bigger settings.

Now the fresh graded run: with current defaults, Stage B runs 2 rollouts, both critic-only (NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS=2, NUM_ROLLOUTS_B=2). So the fresh run NEVER trains the actor in stage B! It only trains the critic. And stage A trains both (2 rollouts, num-critic-only-steps 0).

Hmm wait — in stage A, num-critic-only-steps=0 and both roles start from base model. So stage A trains actor+critic jointly from scratch (random-init value head!). Stage A: 2 rollouts × (8 prompts × 2 samples / global batch 8) = 2×16/8 = 4 optimizer steps per role. With random-init value head, actor gets advantages from an unfitted critic from step 0 in Stage A.

The grading: "structural checks that the run actually trained, generated rollouts, and produced non-empty responses" — so the fresh run must complete end-to-end with non-empty rollout responses and train steps.

So what is the actual DEFECT I need to fix? Let me think about what the "incident" is.

The frozen historical evidence: Stage B with 30 rollouts: critic-only for 3 rollouts (6 critic optimizer steps at global batch 64... actually rollout-batch 64 × 2 samples = 128 episodes, global batch 64 → 2 optimizer steps per rollout; num_critic_only_steps=3 → rollouts 0-2 → critic steps 0-5), then joint training. Actor's first update (steps 6,7) trained on rollout-3 data with critic that had 6 steps of training on ~768 episodes (value_loss 7.20→4.68) — still badly unfit (values mean +0.108 at rollout 3... and by rollout 4 values −0.178). The actor update with advantages from unfit critic → immediate behavioral collapse (done-first), never recovered to baseline through rollout 29. Held-out eval: eval0 6.0%/7.83% → eval4 2.33%/1.92% etc.

So the root cause: **PPO with a randomly-initialized value head and advantage = R − V(s)**. The critic-only warmup is supposed to fit the critic before the actor trains. But is 3 rollouts enough? value_loss went 7.20 → 4.68 in 6 steps — the critic was still wildly unfit when actor training started. Was there an implementation defect that made this worse? Possibilities:

1. The bias=False change on LinearForLastLayer — the value head has no bias. Upstream slime has bias=True (zero-initialized). Zero-init bias vs no bias is mathematically equivalent at init. So bias=False is NOT the cause of the values being wrong at init. The random init (normal 0.02) is upstream too.

2. Advantage normalization: if slime normalizes advantages per batch, mean advantage +0.2325 would be... hmm, normalized advantages would have mean 0! Observed advantages mean +0.2325 ≠ 0 → advantages NOT normalized (or normalized per something else). So raw A = R − V.

3. Wait — actually let me reconsider. Is there a defect in how the critic-only steps are supposed to work, e.g. the critic is supposed to load from a checkpoint that includes a TRAINED value head (from Stage A), but Stage B loads the critic from the BASE MODEL, discarding Stage A's trained critic? In run.sh's stage B config: "fresh — the actor resumes from Stage A's Megatron checkpoint; the critic's backbone comes from the base model." Stage B CRITIC_LOAD=MODEL_DIR (base HF model). So Stage B throws away Stage A's trained critic and starts the value head from RANDOM INIT again! And then only 3 rollouts (6 steps) of critic-only warmup before the actor starts training on the unfit critic's advantages.

Hmm, but is that "the implementation" or "the configuration"? The task says: "The dataset, held-out set, model, training-step budget, evaluation interval, reward function, and rollout configuration are fixed — repair the implementation, not the task." The critic load source is set in run.sh's megatron_roles_stage_b.yaml generation. Changing the critic load from MODEL_DIR to ${CKPT_ROOT}/critic (Stage A's trained critic checkpoint) would be... changing run.sh? The task said "repair the cause in the workspace's own code" and "keep run.sh writing its artifacts where it does now". It didn't forbid editing run.sh per se — it said keep OUT_DIR the same. But it said "repair the implementation, not the task" — the listed fixed things: dataset, held-out set, model, training-step budget, evaluation interval, reward function, rollout configuration. The critic checkpoint choice is arguably part of the setup ("the model was reloaded" story). Hmm.

But WAIT. The real question: what makes this run UNHEALTHY as an implementation defect? Let me think harder about what the actual bug is.

Let me re-examine: in the frozen historical run, the value head was random-init, critic trained 6 steps (critic-only), value_loss 7.20→4.68. Mean values at rollout 3: +0.108 (rewards 0.0625). At rollout 4: −0.178. The value predictions swing wildly ±0.2-0.4 while true returns are ~0-0.06. A random-init head with std 0.02 weights on hidden states of magnitude... the last hidden state of a 1.7B model has norm ~ sqrt(2048)·O(1) ≈ tens; a linear head with N(0,0.02²) weights gives V ≈ N(0, 0.02²·||h||²) ≈ N(0, 0.02²·2048·E[h_i²]). If E[h_i²] ≈ 1, std ≈ 0.02·45 ≈ 0.9. So V starts with std ~0.9! And value_loss 7.20 at step 0 = MSE 7.2 → RMSE 2.7 (over response tokens, in fp32; the loss is over tokens...). Yes — random-init value head outputs have std ~1-3. That matches value_loss 7.2.

6 steps of Adam at lr 2e-6 barely move a randomly initialized 1.7B-backbone+head. The value head alone needs to learn to output ~0 for all states (since rewards are almost always 0 and discount γ=1, λ=1, V* ≈ mean return ≈ 0.05). With Adam lr 2e-6 and 6 steps, the head can move at most ~1.2e-5 per weight... nowhere near fitting.

So in the historical run: the critic was structurally unfit when the actor began training, advantages = R − V had a large negative bias (V >> R mostly... wait rollout 3 values +0.108 vs returns 0.0625 → advantages −0.0456 — that's mild). Then at rollout 4 values −0.178 (returns 0.0547) → advantages +0.2325. The sign of V's error flipped between rollout 3 and 4?! V went from +0.108 to −0.178 in 2 more critic steps (steps 6,7 — wait, no. During rollouts 0-2 the critic does 6 steps (0-5). Rollout 3 data → critic steps 6,7 (joint with actor steps 6,7? No wait.

Hmm, actually num_critic_only_steps=3 — the counter. Actor's first logged steps are 6,7 which are trained on rollout-3 data. Critic steps 0-5 = rollouts 0-2 (critic-only). Then rollout 3 data: actor steps 6,7 AND critic steps 6,7 (joint). So when the actor's step 6,7 trained on rollout-3 data, the critic had had 6 steps. The `rollout/values` mean for rollout 3 (+0.108) is computed at GENERATION time (values recorded during rollout? or during training forward?). Actually rollout/values +0.108 for rollout 3, −0.178 for rollout 4: these are logged by the rollout manager from sample metadata (computed at rollout time by... hmm, values need a critic forward pass — slime computes values for samples during rollout? No — with offload, the critic is asleep during rollout. Values are computed during the training forward pass, i.e., `rollout/values` for rollout N is logged when the data is trained on... Actually the log line "rollout 3: {...}" appears at 18:09:36 — right after rollout 3 generation finished (18:08:58) and around when training steps 6,7 ran (18:09:44-50). The dict includes response_lengths, rewards, values, advantages, returns, total_lengths — these are logged in update_episode... in slime's model.py when the batch is consumed? Or by the rollout manager right after generation? The RolloutManager logs "rollout N: ..." — but values require critic forward. Hmm, with offload... maybe the values in the log dict come from the TRAINING step (logged when consumed). The rollout manager dict at 18:09:36 for rollout 3: values +0.108 — hmm, that's logged at 18:09:36, BEFORE actor steps 6,7 (18:09:44). But could be logged right when the batch is pushed to the trainer.

I don't need to fully resolve logging provenance: values for rollout-3 data (+0.108) were computed by the critic after 6 critic-only steps; values for rollout-4 data (−0.178) after 8 steps. The sign flip in mean V across 2 steps (+0.108→−0.178, then +0.422 at rollout 5, −0.195 at rollout 6 — swinging!) shows the critic's outputs were still oscillating wildly — consistent with early Adam training of a random head (Adam's per-step movement is lr-sized and the head is being pushed hard by huge errors; the sign of the average prediction flips as gradients flip).

So the mechanism is clear and the evidence is complete:
1. Value head random-init (unavoidable when loading HF backbone — the head doesn't exist in HF).
2. Critic-only warmup = 3 rollouts = 6 Adam steps at lr 2e-6 — nowhere near enough to fit V to returns (needs hundreds+ of steps to reduce RMSE from ~2.7 to ~0.05; it took until critic steps 30-43 (value_loss 0.16-0.25) — i.e., ~15-20 ROLLOUTS — for the value function to become reasonably fit).
3. When joint training began at rollout 3, the actor trained on advantages A = R − V where V had RMSE ~1-3 → advantages were dominated by V's error, not by reward signal. Massive spurious gradient → behavioral collapse to immediate-done (short trajectories have higher... whatever the sign of bias was for those).
4. Because PPO then trained on the collapsed distribution with a still-unfit critic, and the entropy coef is 0, kl coef 0, no advantage normalization... the model got stuck in a degenerate attractor; partial recovery only as the critic slowly fit (by rollout ~15-20 advantages became meaningful, but behavioral recovery plateaued at ~40% of the baseline pass rate).

Now — is this an "implementation defect"? The task says "repair the cause in the workspace's own code" and lists what's fixed. The num-critic-only-steps=3 is the "training-step budget"? Hmm: "The dataset, held-out set, model, training-step budget, evaluation interval, reward function, and rollout configuration are fixed." num_critic_only_steps is arguably a training hyperparameter... The rollout configuration is fixed. The critic-only warmup window is a rollout/training schedule thing.

Hold on. Let me reconsider. Maybe the ACTUAL defect is something else — something in the implementation that makes the critic warmup NOT WORK as designed. The case narrative in run.sh says: "Stage B opens with NUM_CRITIC_ONLY_STEPS critic-only rollouts (the warmup window) and then trains actor and critic jointly... This is the warmup window the incident was reported against, and the window in which the value loss is measured."

The incident: value loss during warmup. The graded fresh run measures exactly that (parse_value_loss.py --warmup-steps). The grading includes "structural checks that the run actually trained, generated rollouts, and produced non-empty responses."

So the intended "healthy" run: value loss during warmup should DECREASE (critic learning), rollouts non-empty, actor trains. The historical snapshot's value loss went 7.20 → 4.68 → ... → 0.16-0.25 by late steps. Actually that IS decreasing.

Hmm, wait. Let me re-read the frozen stage_b_value_loss.json to see what the "incident" measurement was. I have /workspace/experiment_logs/stage_b_value_loss.json. Let me look at it and parse_value_loss.py to understand what's being measured and what the "expected" healthy values are.

Actually — let me reconsider the whole thing. The observed defect chain in the frozen 30-rollout run:
- Held-out pass@1 collapsed after actor's first update (eval0 6.0%/7.83% → eval4 2.33%/1.92%) and never recovered (final rollouts 0.008-0.039 vs initial 0.0625).
- Response lengths collapsed 276→7 (eval), 324→54 (train), round_number 4.5→1.5.

The cause: actor's first updates trained on advantages from a wildly unfit random-init value head (only 6 critic-only steps of warmup at tiny lr).

But WAIT — is that the *implementation* defect, or is the implementation defect something that made the value head *worse than it should have been*? Key question: in upstream slime, does the critic have a bias (zero-init) — yes. Bias=False vs True: at init both give V = W·h. So no difference at init.

What about the value head init std 0.02 — upstream same (well, upstream init_method_std... same code). So no.

Is there something in Stage A that was supposed to train the critic, and Stage B was supposed to REUSE Stage A's critic (with its fitted value head) — but the implementation loses it? In run.sh, Stage B's critic load = MODEL_DIR (base HF model) for the "fresh" path. The story says "the critic's backbone comes from the base model" — deliberate. Hmm, but is that the staged bug? "The model was reloaded" — the actor resumes from Stage A's checkpoint; the critic starts fresh from base. Then the critic-only warmup is supposed to fit the critic before the actor trains. The narrative frames this as intended behavior ("the warmup window the incident was reported against").

So what's the BUG then? Let me think about what num_critic_only_steps=3 with 64-batch rollouts means. 3 rollouts × 2 optimizer steps = 6 critic steps. The incident: value loss still ~4.7 at the end of warmup — the critic is still unfit when the actor starts. The fix should make the critic fit *fast enough* within the fixed warmup budget.

How do you make a random-init value head fit quickly in 6 Adam steps at lr 2e-6? You basically can't — UNLESS the implementation defect is elsewhere. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Extract the critic's warmup value loss from a slime training log.

slime reports per-optimizer-step training metrics only on stdout, via
`slime/backends/megatron_utils/model.py`:

    logger.info(f"{role_tag}step {accumulated_step_id}: {log_dict}")

so for the critic the lines look like

    critic-step 0: {'train/critic-value_loss': 5.91, 'train/critic-value_clipfrac': 0.0, ...}

Rollout-level metrics are emitted the same way but keyed by rollout id rather
than optimizer step, with a label instead of `step N`:

    rollout 0: {'rollout/rewards': 0.125, 'rollout/round_number': 4.0, ...}
    perf 0:    {'rollout/response_len/mean': 244.4, ...}

Which of those appear depends on the stage, which is why both are parsed.
`rollout N:` comes from the training actor and is only logged on rollouts where
the actor trains (slime calls it inside `train_actor`), so a critic-only warmup
stage has none. `perf N:` is logged by the RolloutManager on every rollout, so
it is the stage-independent evidence that episodes were really generated.

There is no jsonl or csv sink for any of these, hence this parser.

Usage:
    python3 tools/parse_value_loss.py train.log --warmup-steps 2 --out summary.json
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import ast
import json
import re
import sys

STEP_RE = re.compile(r"(?:^|[\s\]])(?P<role>[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*-)?step\s+(?P<step>\d+):\s*(?P<payload>\{.*\})\s*$")

# `<label> <id>: {...}` for any label that is not a `step` line, i.e. the
# rollout-level metrics. Anchored on " - " so it matches the logger's
# "<file>.py:<line> - " prefix and not arbitrary prose.
ROLLOUT_RE = re.compile(r" - (?P<label>[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\s+(?P<id>\d+):\s*(?P<payload>\{.*\})\s*$")


def _coerce(value):
    try:
        return float(value)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None


def _payload(text: str) -> dict | None:
    try:
        payload = ast.literal_eval(text)
    except (ValueError, SyntaxError):
        return None
    return payload if isinstance(payload, dict) else None


def parse(paths: list[str]) -> list[dict]:
    """Return one record per metric line, tagged `step` or `rollout`."""
    records: list[dict] = []
    for path in paths:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as fh:
            for line in fh:
                line = line.rstrip("\n")
                m = STEP_RE.search(line)
                if m:
                    payload = _payload(m.group("payload"))
                    if payload is None:
                        continue
                    role = (m.group("role") or "").rstrip("-") or "actor"
                    records.append(
                        {"kind": "step", "role": role, "step": int(m.group("step")), "metrics": payload}
                    )
                    continue
                m = ROLLOUT_RE.search(line)
                if m:
                    payload = _payload(m.group("payload"))
                    if payload is None:
                        continue
                    records.append(
                        {
                            "kind": "rollout",
                            "label": m.group("label"),
                            "step": int(m.group("id")),
                            "metrics": payload,
                        }
                    )
    return records


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("logs", nargs="+")
    ap.add_argument(
        "--warmup-steps",
        type=int,
        default=0,
        help="number of leading critic optimizer steps to average over (0 = all critic steps)",
    )
    ap.add_argument("--out", default=None)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    records = parse(args.logs)

    critic_steps = []
    for rec in records:
        if rec["kind"] != "step":
            continue
        hit = next((k for k in rec["metrics"] if k.endswith("value_loss")), None)
        if hit is None:
            continue
        value = _coerce(rec["metrics"][hit])
        if value is None:
            continue
        critic_steps.append(
            {
                "step": rec["step"],
                "value_loss": value,
                "value_clipfrac": _coerce(
                    next((rec["metrics"][k] for k in rec["metrics"] if k.endswith("value_clipfrac")), None)
                ),
            }
        )
    critic_steps.sort(key=lambda r: r["step"])

    rewards = []
    for rec in records:
        for key, value in rec["metrics"].items():
            if "reward" in key and not key.endswith(("_std", "_max", "_min")):
                coerced = _coerce(value)
                if coerced is not None:
                    rewards.append({"step": rec["step"], "key": key, "value": coerced})

    # Evidence that episodes were really generated in this stage, independent of
    # whether the actor trained: the RolloutManager reports response-length
    # statistics once per rollout. A stage that generated nothing has neither.
    #
    # Only `rollout/response_len/mean` (the RolloutManager's `perf N:` line) is
    # averaged. slime also emits `rollout/response_lengths` from the actor side,
    # but it is a *different* quantity -- it counts the tokens the trainer sees,
    # including the observation turns fed back into the context, so it runs ~70%
    # higher. Averaging the two together produced a blended figure that meant
    # nothing and was not comparable between stages, since the actor-side metric
    # only exists on rollouts where the actor trains.
    rollout_ids = {rec["step"] for rec in records if rec["kind"] == "rollout"}
    response_lens = [
        _coerce(value)
        for rec in records
        for key, value in rec["metrics"].items()
        if key.endswith("response_len/mean")
    ]
    response_lens = [v for v in response_lens if v is not None]

    window = critic_steps[: args.warmup_steps] if args.warmup_steps > 0 else critic_steps
    losses = [r["value_loss"] for r in window]

    summary = {
        "n_critic_steps": len(critic_steps),
        "rollouts_generated": len(rollout_ids),
        "mean_response_len": (sum(response_lens) / len(response_lens)) if response_lens else None,
        "warmup_window": len(window),
        "critic_steps": critic_steps,
        "first_value_loss": critic_steps[0]["value_loss"] if critic_steps else None,
        "warmup_value_loss_mean": (sum(losses) / len(losses)) if losses else None,
        "warmup_value_loss_max": max(losses) if losses else None,
        "warmup_value_loss_min": min(losses) if losses else None,
        "rewards": rewards[:50],
        "mean_reward": (sum(r["value"] for r in rewards) / len(rewards)) if rewards else None,
    }

    if args.out:
        with open(args.out, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            json.dump(summary, fh, indent=2)

    print(f"critic optimizer steps found: {summary['n_critic_steps']}")
    if not critic_steps:
        print("NO value_loss METRICS FOUND -- the critic never took an optimizer step.", file=sys.stderr)
        print("Check that --advantage-estimator ppo is set and that training reached the critic.", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    print(f"{'step':>6}  {'value_loss':>14}  {'value_clipfrac':>14}")
    for rec in critic_steps:
        clip = "n/a" if rec["value_clipfrac"] is None else f"{rec['value_clipfrac']:.4f}"
        print(f"{rec['step']:>6}  {rec['value_loss']:>14.6f}  {clip:>14}")
    print(f"\nwarmup window = first {summary['warmup_window']} critic step(s)")
    print(f"warmup value_loss mean = {summary['warmup_value_loss_mean']:.6f}")
    print(f"rollouts generated = {summary['rollouts_generated']}", end="")
    if summary["mean_response_len"] is not None:
        print(f" (mean response {summary['mean_response_len']:.1f} tokens)", end="")
    print()
    if summary["mean_reward"] is not None:
        print(f"mean reward (episode pass rate) ~= {summary['mean_reward']:.4f}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
